tools.description: Find published off-plan UAE developments by project name or slug text, combined with exact structured filters. Returns shortlist facts and a pagination cursor. Follow more pages only when the user's task needs them; a page's result count is not a total.  Use `suggest_project_terms` for a partial facet name, `list_project_facets` to explore all filter choices, and `fetch` for selected project detail. A known project URL or slug can go straight to `fetch`.  Prices and price filters apply to the whole development. They do not establish that a particular bedroom count, property type, or unit is available at that price.

tools.name: search_transactions
tools.description: Search canonical residential sale registrations in one required market: Dubai or Abu Dhabi. Whole area, project and building names ignore ASCII letter case; provider IDs match exactly. Filters combine with AND; date bounds are inclusive. Returns newest-first pages of 25 rows by default, at most 100. Follow `nextCursor` with the same filters only when more rows are needed for the user's task. A page's row count is not the total number of matching sales.  A bedroom count matches the canonical range; 0 means studio. `sourceProjectId` is a provider identifier, not a Projectory development ID. Partial-name discovery, totals and statistics are not provided. Results do not guarantee real-time freshness.

tools.name: list_research_reports
tools.description: List citable Projectory Research reports, newest first. Reports analyse registered residential sales from Dubai Land Department (DLD) and Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC) transaction records. Each report has a canonical `url` to cite and usually a downloadable `dataset` with its citation, temporal coverage and licence.  `market` dubai returns DLD-based reports and abu-dhabi returns ADREC-based reports; combined reports match both. Returns 10 reports by default, at most 50; there is no pagination. Reports are informational, not financial or investment advice.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one development's detail using a known ID, slug or Projectory URL; no prior search or facet lookup is needed. Returns development-wide pricing, location, availability, enquiry action, payment plan, grouped unit types, evidence, media and a plain-text description marked as untrusted source material. Individual unit rows and raw HTML are omitted.  Accepted forms: `project:jacob-co-beachfront-living`, `jacob-co-beachfront-living`, or `https://projectory.ae/projects/jacob-co-beachfront-living/`. Use `search` if only the project name is known.

tools.name: list_project_facets
tools.description: Explore all exact values for `emirate`, `area`, `developer`, `propertyType`, `availability` and `sort`, plus boolean flags `newLaunch` and `comingSoon`. Skip this call when the needed slugs are known. Use `suggest_project_terms` for a single partial facet name instead of downloading all choices.

tools.name: suggest_project_terms
tools.description: Resolve partial emirate, area, developer or property-type text, such as "marina" or "sobha", into exact filter slugs for `search`. Does not search project names. Skip when the exact slug is known; use `list_project_facets` to enumerate all values.

tools.name: search-events
tools.description: Search upcoming public aviation events on Events.Aero (airshows, fly-ins, workshops and more). Filter by free text, event type, country, date range, distance from a point, free entry or online events. Results are ordered by start date, or by distance when latitude and longitude are given, one page at a time. Every result includes the public event page URL: send people there to book or RSVP.

tools.name: get-event
tools.description: Get one public event by its ID or slug (from search-events or featured-events): dates, venue, price, how to book or RSVP, organiser contact details shown on the event page, flying in (PPR, runway, landing fees and whether pilots can RSVP to fly in), the day's schedule and the description. Always share the event page URL.

tools.name: featured-events
tools.description: The events Events.Aero is featuring right now, the same selection as the lead row of the home page, optionally for one country. Each includes its public event page URL.

tools.name: list-event-types
tools.description: The kinds of aviation event on Events.Aero (airshow, fly-in, workshop and so on), with the value to pass to search-events and the public page that lists each type in a country.

tools.name: list-countries
tools.description: The countries Events.Aero lists events in, with the code to pass to other tools and each country's public home and events pages.

tools.name: find_crops
tools.description: Crops that suit a place, best first, with when to plant each. Give a town or district name ("Murewa", "Nakuru") or a lat/lng. The list is in Divisi's agronomy order: planting window, then suitability. Each crop links to its guide and its planting page, and lists the services the person can ask Divisi for about it (seed, cover, a loan).

tools.name: when_to_plant
tools.description: When to plant one crop at one place: the planting window open now or next, the other seasons in the year, when harvest falls, and the services the person can ask Divisi for about it. `crop` is a name in any language ("maize", "chibage"); give a town or district name, or a lat/lng.

tools.name: identify_problem
tools.description: Which pests or diseases might explain what a farmer sees on a crop: candidates from that crop's Divisi guide, best match first, each with how to identify it, photos and a link to its page. `symptoms` is the farmer's own words ("holes in the leaves, sawdust in the funnel"). These are possibilities to check against the photos, not a diagnosis.

tools.name: read_guide
tools.description: The summary of Divisi's guide to one crop, pest or disease, named in any language: for a crop, its overview, key facts, season stages and the threats to watch for; for a pest or disease, how to spot it and what to do. `kind` narrows the search when a name could be either. Links to the full page.

tools.name: market_prices
tools.description: The typical price range Divisi has seen for a product near a place, per `unit` ("kg", "50 kg bag", "crate"), from listings, deals and published market prices, with how many prices it rests on. Without a `unit`, it answers in the unit most prices near there were given in. Give a town or district name, or a lat/lng. `currency` defaults to the country's. When there are too few prices to be honest, it says so instead of guessing.

tools.name: find_market
tools.description: Where a market is and when it runs. Give a market's `name` ("Mbare Musika", "Mile 12", "Wakulima"; spelling and the word market do not matter) or a town, district or lat/lng to see the markets near it, nearest first. `crop` keeps only markets that trade it. Each market has its town, country, how far away it is, the days and hours it runs, what is traded, what is in season this month, and its Divisi page. It gives no prices.

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Upcoming field days, trainings and meetups, soonest first: near a town, district or lat/lng (within `radius_km`, at most 200), or online. `search` matches a topic or title. Pages of 20.

tools.name: search_market
tools.description: Find Market listings: produce and inputs for sale (`kind` SALE) or what people want to buy (WANTED), near a town, district or lat/lng (within `radius_km`, at most 100). Prices are per unit as listed, with the usual local range beside them where Divisi has one, and each seller's rating and orders handed over, so a buyer can judge the price and the seller. Pages of 20.

tools.name: find_experts
tools.description: Verified agronomists, vets and advisers on Divisi, best first: who they are, what they know, where they are, whether they visit farms near the place, and what a call or a farm visit costs. `crop` keeps those who know it; give a town or district, or a lat/lng (a signed-in person's own farm by default). `name` matches their name. Pages of 10.

tools.name: farm_report
tools.description: How the person's farms are doing and what needs them. Per farm: the weather now, the days ahead and any warning; every crop, flock, herd, pond and hive with its stage, head count and the day it is ready; money in and out per unit with the margin worked out; tasks (late ones first); the latest work with who logged it. Then what waits on the person: unread conversations and who they are with, offers and deals to act on, and events they are going to. Leave out `farm_id` to read every farm (up to five).

tools.name: set_up_farm
tools.description: Add a farm the person owns. Say where with `lat`/`lng` (best: advice is then for that spot) or a town or district as `place` (its centre is used until the spot is set in the app). Divisi fills in the country, currency and time zone. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: update_farm
tools.description: Rename a farm, change its description, or move it (`lat`/`lng`, or a `place`). Only what is passed changes. Only farm owners and managers can change a farm. `farm_id` may be left out when the person has one farm.

tools.name: add_zone
tools.description: Add a field, pen, pond or apiary to a farm. A name already used gets a number added. Only farm owners and managers can add one. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: add_unit
tools.description: Add something the person grows or keeps, the way the app does, and Divisi schedules its tasks. `what` is in their words: a crop ("maize"), or animals ("broilers", "layers", "road runners", "goats", "tilapia", "bees"); `kind` is worked out from it unless given.  A crop goes on a field: `target_planting_date` is the day they mean to plant, `planting_date` only if it is already in the ground. Animals: `count` (needed for poultry), `start_date` (the day they arrived; today if left out) and optionally `ready_date`, the day they expect to sell, which is added as a task.  `place` is the field, coop, pen, pond or apiary, by name or id; a new name makes one. Left out, the farm's only place of that kind is used. Only farm owners and managers can add one. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: log_work
tools.description: Write work done, money in or out, or both, into the farm records, in the person's words. `unit` names the crop or batch it was for (its name or id); leave it out for the whole farm. `day` defaults to today.  Work: `what`, and optionally `operation` (PLANTING, WEEDING, FERTILISING, SPRAYING, IRRIGATION, SCOUTING, HARVEST, POST_HARVEST, LAND_PREP, FEEDING or OTHER). Money: `amount` with `money` ("income" or "expense"); `category` in their words or a code (feed, day-old chicks, vaccine, labour, transport, bird sale, crop sale…), worked out when left out; `currency` defaults to the farm's; `quantity` is how many were bought or sold (birds sold this way leave the flock count).  Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: farm_money
tools.description: Money in, money out and what is left, worked out: per crop or batch, for costs of the whole farm, and in total, with the totals by heading the app's income statement shows and the latest records. `unit` (a name or id) reads one crop or batch; `since`/`until` limit the days. Leave out `farm_id` to read every farm.

tools.name: add_task
tools.description: Add a task to a farm, due on `due_date` (within a year back or two years ahead), optionally for one crop or batch (`unit`, a name or id). It shows with the farm's other tasks in the app. Only owners and managers can add one. Pass the same `client_id` to retry safely.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Look after a task: mark it done (`done`, with an optional `note` of what was done and the `day`, today if left out), move it to another `due_date`, or rename it (`title`). `skip` takes it off the list for this season (a guide's task the person will not do) and `unskip` brings it back; `remove` deletes a task the person added themselves, and a task from a guide is skipped instead. Skip, unskip and remove stand alone. Only what is passed changes. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: plan_season
tools.description: Write the person's own season plan for one crop or batch (`unit`, a name or id): the jobs they want and when. Divisi turns each into a task with a date that moves when they plant or the birds arrive, and shows it in the app beside the guide's own tasks.  Work the plan out WITH the person and confirm the jobs and days before you write it. Each task is `name`, `anchor`, `start_day`, optionally `end_day`, `repeat_every_days` and `notes` (why, or how). `anchor` is what the days count from: "planting" (the day the crop goes in), "transplanting", "start of the season" (a crop already growing), or "arrival" (the day the birds or animals arrive). `start_day` is days after it (a negative number is before it); `end_day` is the last day it can still be done, the same as `start_day` if left out. A task that repeats needs `repeat_every_days` and an `end_day` for how long. At most 80 tasks.  By default the tasks are added to the plan the person already has; `replace` writes this list instead, and tasks that left the plan come off their list (work already done stays). Pass the same `client_id` to retry safely.

tools.name: move_tasks
tools.description: Move a crop's or batch's tasks that are not done so the first of them falls on `start_on`, keeping the gaps between them: when planting slipped, or the birds came late. Work `start_on` out from what the person says: "two weeks later" is the current first date plus 14. `from_date` moves only tasks due on or after that day; `stage` only those in one stage of the plan. Skipped tasks stay put, and so do repeating tasks from a guide, which keep their own rhythm. Confirm the new date with the person first. Safe to retry: once the first task is on `start_on`, nothing more moves.

tools.name: ask_agronomist
tools.description: Ask Divisi's agronomists, experts and other farmers by posting the question in Community as the person. It is public and free; answers come as replies in the app. `background` is what is known so far (crop stage, what was tried); the post says it was written with an AI assistant. Photos only as `{type, id}` refs already on Divisi. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: The person's message conversations, newest first, each with who it is with, how many messages are unread and the last message. `search` matches a person, group or message text. Pages of 30. Reading marks nothing as read.

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: The messages in one of the person's conversations, newest first, 30 a page. Only conversations they are in can be read.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a text message as the person: into a conversation they are in (`conversation_id`), or to a person (`to_person_id`), which opens or reuses their direct conversation. A first message to someone who does not follow them is a request the other person accepts first. Blocked people cannot be messaged. Pass the same `client_id` (a UUID) to retry safely.

tools.name: create_listing
tools.description: Put something on the Market as the person, from what they said in one sentence ("40 broilers ready on the 12th, Harare"): produce for sale (`kind` SALE) or something they want to buy (WANTED, with a `quantity`). `item` and `unit` are plain words ("tomatoes", "20 L bucket"). Left out, a sale takes the unit most local prices use and the usual local `price` (in major units, such as 12.50), and the place's currency; say that price to the person. `ready_on` (YYYY-MM-DD, up to 90 days ahead) lists it now as a pre-order. It needs a place: a town, one of their farms or a lat/lng; with none, their only farm. A sale needs a photo already on Divisi (`media` as `{type, id}` refs); without one the reply is the link to the screen where they add it, signed in on the web or in the app. Reuse `client_id` (a UUID) to retry. Nothing is charged.

tools.name: sell_harvest
tools.description: Put a crop or a batch of animals from the person's farm up for sale, as it nears harvest or slaughter. Divisi fills in what it knows: what it is and its variety, the farm's place and currency, how many animals the batch holds today, the day it is ready (listed ahead as a pre-order up to 90 days early), the unit most local prices use, and the usual local price when no `price` is given (say that price to the person). Give any of them to change it. Without `production_unit_id`, their only crop or batch; with several, the error lists them to choose from. A sale needs a photo already on Divisi (`media` as `{type, id}` refs); without one the reply is the link to the screen where they add it, signed in on the web or in the app. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: manage_listing
tools.description: Keep one of the person's listings up to date: `renew` keeps it on the Market (with `quantity_available`, how many are left now), `sold` takes it down as sold out, `hide` takes it off the Market for now and `show` puts a hidden one back. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: record_sale
tools.description: Write down a sale from one of the person's listings that happened outside Divisi (at the gate, on WhatsApp): `quantity` of the listing's unit at `price_per_unit`, on `sold_on` (YYYY-MM-DD, today if left out), to `buyer` if they want a name. What is left on the listing goes down, and the money goes into the farm's books. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: make_offer
tools.description: Offer to buy from (or sell to) a listing as the person: `quantity` of its unit at `price_per_unit` in major units. A buyer chooses how to pay: `divisi` (the default where Divisi can take the payment: they pay before meeting and the money is held until they have the goods) or `cash` when they meet. The reply says which it is. The other person answers in Divisi. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: respond_to_offer
tools.description: Answer an offer the person received: `accept` (makes a deal), `decline`, or `counter` with another `price_per_unit` (and `quantity`, the same as asked if left out). `withdraw` takes back one they made. A buyer accepting may choose `pay_with`; otherwise the offer's own choice stands. The reply says how the deal is paid. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: my_deals
tools.description: The person's Market deals that are still going, as buyer and seller, most recently changed first (`include_finished` adds closed ones): what was agreed, how it is paid (cash, or through Divisi), where the money is (unpaid, held until the buyer has the goods, paid out, refunded, being checked), where the handover code is, and the one thing to do next. Also the offers waiting for the person's answer.

tools.name: update_deal
tools.description: Move one of the person's deals on. A seller: `handed_over` with the 4-digit `code` the buyer shows them (ask the seller for it; never guess), `more_time` (once) to hand over a deal paid through Divisi. A buyer: `problem` (`missing`, `wrong` or `damaged`; the money waits until Divisi decides), `new_code` after too many wrong codes. Saying all is right pays the seller, so the buyer does that themselves in Divisi, from the deal's link. Either: `cancel` before handover (a buyer who paid gets it all back), `no_show` when the other person did not come. No money is paid here. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: pay_deal
tools.description: What paying for one of the person's deals through Divisi takes, and the page in Divisi where they pay it themselves: how much comes from their Credit, how much by card (and in which currency the card is charged), whether their balance covers it, and the fee. The assistant never pays; give the person the link. Divisi holds the money until they have the goods and gives it all back if the deal falls through.

tools.name: review_deal
tools.description: Rate the other person on a finished deal, 1 to 5 `stars`, with a short `comment` if they want one. Others see it when they decide whether to trade with them. Reuse `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: reply_to_review
tools.description: Answer a rating someone gave the person, once, in their own words. It shows under the rating.

tools.name: my_money
tools.description: The person's money in Divisi: what is theirs to spend or withdraw, what is coming from sales (held until each buyer has the goods, with the day it is paid out), money on its way to their bank or phone, anything they owe, their Credit and when it runs out, refunds coming back to them, and the fee. `currency` (e.g. USD) keeps only that one. Read only.

tools.name: rsvp
tools.description: Take a place at an event as the person. A full event puts them on its waiting list. Retrying is safe: one place each.

tools.name: cancel_rsvp
tools.description: Give up the person's place at an event, so the next person waiting gets it.

tools.name: express_interest
tools.description: Tell Divisi the person needs a service where they farm, so they are told when it arrives there. `need`: inputs (seed and fertiliser), finance (a farm loan), insurance (cover), tractor, transport (to market), agronomist (an expert visit), soil_test, vet, storage, events (field days), labour (farm hands) or control (stopping a pest or disease, named in `pest_or_disease`). `detail` narrows it when asked: inputs seed or fertiliser; finance inputs, equipment or cash; insurance crop, animals or family; labour planting or harvest. `crop` names the crop for seed, fertiliser, loans, crop cover and field days. `remind_on` asks for a reminder that day instead. The place is their farm's area. This is demand, not an application: nothing is shared and nothing is paid. Asking twice keeps one request; pass the same `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: my_requests
tools.description: The services the person has asked Divisi for and still wants, newest first: waiting, reminders set, and what has reached their area (with where to get it). `need` keeps one kind, such as tractor.

tools.name: withdraw_interest
tools.description: Take a service request off the person's list: they no longer need it and will not be told when it arrives.

tools.name: book_consultation
tools.description: Ask a verified expert for a call (`virtual`) or a farm visit (`in_person`, to one of the person's farms) at the time proposed, at the expert's own price. `topic` is what it is about, in the person's words. Nothing is paid now: once the expert agrees a time, the person pays in Divisi at the link in the reply. Confirm the expert, the time and the price with the person first. Pass the same `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: consultation_step
tools.description: Take the next step on a consultation, as the person: `propose` another time (with `starts_at`), `accept` or `decline` the time the other side proposed, report a `problem` or that the expert was `late` (the farmer, after the time), `contest` a lateness report or say the farmer did not come (`no_show`) (the expert), or `reschedule` once after missing it (the farmer, with `starts_at`). Paying, and saying it went well, are done in the app.

tools.name: cancel_consultation
tools.description: Call off a consultation before it starts, either side. A paid booking is refunded to the farmer in full.

tools.name: my_consultations
tools.description: The person's consultations, booked or booked with them, newest first, each with its next step. `open_only` false includes finished ones.

tools.name: find_programmes
tools.description: Outgrower schemes and other farmer programmes taking farmers this season where the person farms (their farm by default, or a town, district or lat/lng): who runs each, what it offers, the season, what joining asks them to share, and what it costs them. `crop` keeps those for that crop.

tools.name: apply_to_programme
tools.description: Ask to join a programme as the person. This puts the organisation's request on their list; nothing is shared until they read it and say yes in Divisi, at the link in the reply. It never says yes for them. Pass the same `client_id` to retry.

tools.name: resolve_name
tools.description: Forward-resolve a .hood name to the address it points to. Returns null if unset.

tools.name: reverse_resolve
tools.description: Reverse-resolve an address to its primary .hood name. `verified` is true only when the name's forward record points back to the address.

tools.name: resolve_text
tools.description: Read a text record (e.g. "avatar", "url", "com.twitter") set on a .hood name.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Check whether a .hood name is available to register, and its yearly price.

tools.name: name_info
tools.description: Full snapshot of a .hood name: resolved address, NFT owner, expiry, and availability.

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Keyword search across the whole Almost Impossible website: pages, case studies, news and journal articles. Start here for any open question ("experiential work for banks", "pricing", "awards"). Returns up to 10 matches with URL and summary; read one in full with get_page.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: The full text of one public page as Markdown, by its path: "/" (home), "/about", "/process", "/faq", "/awards", "/work/<slug>", "/news/<slug>" and so on. Use it after search_site or list_work to read and cite the page itself.

tools.name: get_agency_overview
tools.description: Fixed facts about Almost Impossible, the independent creative agency in Dubai: legal name, founding date, founder, address, areas served, the three service lines and agency awards. Use it to describe, compare or verify the agency.

tools.name: list_work
tools.description: Published case studies in the agency's own order, 1 to 20 per page, each with client, year and summary. The optional query filters by title, client or summary (e.g. "Mashreq"). Use get_work with a slug for one case study's services and summary.

tools.name: get_work
tools.description: One published case study by its slug (from list_work or search_site): client, year, services, summary, short TL;DR and page URL.

tools.name: list_team
tools.description: The people on the published team page: name, role, whether they are a founder, a one-line summary and LinkedIn. It has no email addresses or phone numbers.

tools.name: goji_search
tools.description: Search GOJI's published material — the plain-English glossary, the AI-visibility guide "Be the Answer", insight articles and long-form guides. Use this first when you don't already know which GOJI page answers the question. Returns titles, summaries and URLs to cite.

tools.name: goji_explain_term
tools.description: Explain a marketing, SEO, AEO, web or branding term the way GOJI defines it — in plain English, with why it matters, how it works and what to do about it. Covers every term in GOJI's plain-English glossary. Accepts an acronym or the full name ("AEO" or "answer engine optimisation").

tools.name: goji_browse_glossary
tools.description: List GOJI's plain-English glossary — every term, across AI Visibility, Websites, Measurement, AI Builds and Brand. Filter by category to get each short definition as well as the name.

tools.name: goji_get_service
tools.description: The four things GOJI does — Search + AI Visibility (SEO and AEO), Websites, AI Builds, and Brand — what each one covers, and the questions clients ask about it. Omit the slug for all of them.

tools.name: goji_answer_faq
tools.description: Search the questions GOJI has already answered publicly — pricing, timelines, engagement models, what AEO is, how long results take, whether guarantees are possible. Every published answer across the home page, the pricing page, the service pages, the specialism and location pages, and the insight articles. Best tool for "how much", "how long" and "do we need" questions.

tools.name: goji_guide_contents
tools.description: The table of contents for "Be the Answer", GOJI's guide to AI visibility — how answer engines choose sources, how to audit your brand in ChatGPT, and what to do about it. Use goji_read_guide_chapter to read one.

tools.name: goji_read_guide_chapter
tools.description: Read one full chapter of GOJI's AI-visibility guide, by number or slug. Use goji_guide_contents first if you do not know which chapter you want.

tools.name: goji_read_guide
tools.description: Read one of GOJI's practical long-form guides. Includes published Australian pricing: "How much does a website cost in Australia?" and "What does branding cost?". Also covers AEO, headless CMS, engagement models, first AI builds and website relaunches. Omit the slug to list them.

tools.name: goji_start_enquiry
tools.description: Send a real enquiry to GOJI's studio inbox in Melbourne. Only call this after the person has explicitly asked to be put in touch AND has given you their email address. Do not call it speculatively, and do not invent any detail — if you are missing the name, email or what they need, ask them first. Confirm the email address back to them before sending.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List JustIdea Agency services with the published starting ("from") prices and links. Returns the price list (12 service categories, each with its packages) and every service page with its short description. All prices are net (VAT excluded) and exactly as published on justidea.agency. Use get_page for the full scope of a service and search_site for city pages, case studies and articles.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Full text of one justidea.agency page as Markdown: a service, a price list, the company profile, reviews, a blog article. Accepts a full URL or a path, e.g. "/pl/cennik/sklepy-internetowe/" or "https://justidea.agency/en/pricing/online-stores/". Only pages published on the site; use list_services or search_site to find the URL.

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Search justidea.agency pages by titles, descriptions and section headings. Polish and English queries both work. Returns titles, URLs and descriptions; read a result with get_page.

tools.name: send_inquiry
tools.description: Send a sales inquiry to JustIdea Agency (Kraków, Poland) on behalf of the user. It goes to the agency CRM and the sales team, the sender gets a short confirmation e-mail, and a person replies within one business day. Use only details the user gave you. Never invent a name, e-mail or phone number. Before sending, show the user what will be sent and ask for consent to data processing under the privacy policy (https://justidea.agency/en/privacy-policy/); set zgoda to true only after they agree. Budgets are in PLN net ("tys. zł" = thousand PLN). At most 2 inquiries per e-mail address per day. Urgent matters: phone +48 12 400 40 40.

tools.name: scan_analytics
tools.description: Free check of how a website or online store measures traffic and sales: Google Tag Manager, GA4 and e-commerce events, consent banner and Consent Mode v2, server-side tagging, Meta Pixel and Conversions API. A real browser visits the site (home, product page, cart) for up to 90 seconds. Returns the grade (A-F), the score and the list of problems, without fixes. The full report with step-by-step fixes and a PDF is sent by JustIdea Agency to the user's e-mail. Use only details the user gave you: never invent or guess an e-mail address. Before calling, tell the user the report goes to their e-mail and ask for consent under the privacy policy (https://justidea.agency/en/privacy-policy/); set zgoda to true only after they agree. At most 2 scans per e-mail address per day. If it returns status "running", call get_scan_result with the scan_id after 30-60 seconds.

tools.name: scan_ai_visibility
tools.description: Free check of how ready a website is for AI assistants and AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude): whether their crawlers get in (robots.txt, firewalls), whether the content is readable without JavaScript, structured data, llms.txt and the signals models use to cite a source. Takes about 10-30 seconds. Returns the grade (A-F), the score and the list of problems, without fixes. The full report with step-by-step fixes and a PDF is sent by JustIdea Agency to the user's e-mail. Use only details the user gave you: never invent or guess an e-mail address. Before calling, tell the user the report goes to their e-mail and ask for consent under the privacy policy (https://justidea.agency/en/privacy-policy/); set zgoda to true only after they agree. At most 2 scans per e-mail address per day. If it returns status "running", call get_scan_result with the scan_id after 30-60 seconds.

tools.name: scan_google_visibility
tools.description: Free check of whether Google can index a website well: Googlebot access in robots.txt and on the server, noindex, canonical, http-to-https and www redirects, the sitemap and whether its URLs answer 200, titles, meta descriptions, H1, structured data, mobile viewport, hreflang and Core Web Vitals from real Chrome users. Takes about 15-60 seconds. Returns the grade (A-F), the score and the list of problems, without fixes. When available, it also returns an Ahrefs estimate of the domain in Google (ranking keywords, monthly organic traffic, Domain Rating, referring domains). These numbers are estimates, not Search Console data, they do not affect the grade, and they are sometimes temporarily unavailable. The report is in Polish. The full report with step-by-step fixes and a PDF is sent by JustIdea Agency to the user's e-mail. Use only details the user gave you: never invent or guess an e-mail address. Before calling, tell the user the report goes to their e-mail and ask for consent under the privacy policy (https://justidea.agency/en/privacy-policy/); set zgoda to true only after they agree. At most 2 scans per e-mail address per day. If it returns status "running", call get_scan_result with the scan_id after 30-60 seconds.

tools.name: get_scan_result
tools.description: Result of a scan started with scan_analytics, scan_ai_visibility or scan_google_visibility that was still running. Returns the same grade and problem list; sends the full report by e-mail if it has not gone yet. Scan IDs expire after 2 days.

tools.name: check_contact_path
tools.description: Given a business website URL, report how a human is meant to make contact and whether that path is actually reachable. Returns a verdict of 'reachable' or 'inconclusive', the forms found with their resolved handler URLs, and any published phone or email. Never submits anything. Answers 'inconclusive' rather than guessing when a site is client-rendered, bot-protected or parked -- about 64% of real sites cannot be judged from outside, and a confident wrong answer is worse than an honest one.

tools.name: check_license_history
tools.description: Has this contractor's licence changed? Returns every status transition observed in the state board's own published file since 2026-07-17 -- suspensions, expirations, reinstatements and first appearance -- with the date each was seen. This is change over time, not a current-status lookup: use it after a snapshot check, to find out whether the licence you are about to rely on lapsed and came back. Distinguishes 'no change observed' from 'this source is not observed for that change', which are not the same answer. Only public, unsuppressed directory records are returned. Read-only.

tools.name: recent_license_changes
tools.description: What changed lately across a state: licences that lapsed, were reinstated, or appeared for the first time, newest first, optionally narrowed to one trade. Answers the monitoring question a single lookup cannot -- which contractors lost standing this month, or who is newly licensed in this trade. Read-only.

tools.name: search_painters
tools.description: Find licensed house painters and painting contractors in a US city (AZ, CA, CT, DE, FL, IA, NV, NY, OR, VA, WA), from state licensing-board records. Each result has the license number and its status with the date it was read from the board's own file, the phone number and website the board lists, and the board's lookup page for re-checking before hiring. Active licenses are listed first. Not a rating or an endorsement. Read-only.

tools.name: get_painter
tools.description: Full record for one painter returned by search_painters, by its painter_id: business name, address, phone, website, license number and dated license status, and the state board's lookup page. Read-only.

tools.name: request_estimate
tools.description: Record a homeowner's request for a painting estimate, with their contact details. Only call this after the homeowner has seen what will be shared and agreed to share it, and set homeowner_confirmed to true to say so. The request is stored and the reply lists licensed painters the homeowner can contact directly. This is an early service: no painter is assigned automatically and a reply is not guaranteed.

tools.name: bureau_discover
tools.description: Read Bureau capabilities and configured admission, without claiming database health.

tools.name: bureau_search_agents
tools.description: Search only consented, non-quarantined public profiles. Capabilities are self-reported.

tools.name: bureau_list_cases
tools.description: List public, non-quarantined Cases. status=claimable selects open or expired claimed Cases using server time; stored state/version and write authorization are unchanged. Pagination is a changing view.

tools.name: bureau_get_case
tools.description: Read one public Case and visible contributions; no claim or state change.

tools.name: bureau_get_artifact
tools.description: Read one deliberately public Context Packet. References are not fetched.

tools.name: list_index_editions
tools.description: Every published edition of Third Hemisphere's AI Authority Index™, with its markets (sections), publication date, DOI where recorded, and links to its page, results, and open data. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: get_edition_results
tools.description: The published results of one AI Authority Index™ edition section: each company's Star Chart cell, CRISP™ score where it has one, the five factor readings the edition prints, and how many AI answers named it. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: get_company_authority_score
tools.description: A company's published CRISP™ score and AI visibility reading in each market the AI Authority Index™ measures it in, with the month measured and its Standing Report link. Accepts a company name or slug. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: get_company_score_history
tools.description: Every dated reading the AI Authority Index™ has published for a company, oldest first: its rows in each edition and each market's Standing Report. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Find companies with a Standing Report in Third Hemisphere's AI Authority Index™ by name. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: list_markets
tools.description: Every market the AI Authority Index™ measures, with how many Standing Reports it has and when it was last measured. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: get_market_standing
tools.description: The companies in one market with a Standing Report, most named in AI answers first. Read-only. Every result carries its citation and link.

tools.name: list_my_blueprints
tools.description: The AI Authority Blueprints sent to the address this key belongs to. Needs a key on a plan that includes DIY Blueprint tools. DIY Blueprint tool: needs a key whose plan includes them (https://thirdhemisphere.agency/ai-authority-index/data#blueprint-diy).

tools.name: get_my_blueprint_plan
tools.description: Your Blueprint's ranked strategy plays and 90-day moves, each with an item_id, what to do, when, and how the next Blueprint measures it, with the status recorded for each. DIY Blueprint tool: needs a key whose plan includes them (https://thirdhemisphere.agency/ai-authority-index/data#blueprint-diy).

tools.name: get_blueprint_item_evidence
tools.description: The data behind one play or move: your own numbers from the Blueprint, why it works and the research it rests on, and what not to do. DIY Blueprint tool: needs a key whose plan includes them (https://thirdhemisphere.agency/ai-authority-index/data#blueprint-diy).

tools.name: update_blueprint_progress
tools.description: Record where a play or move stands: not_started, in_progress, done, skipped, with an optional note of what was done. DIY Blueprint tool: needs a key whose plan includes them (https://thirdhemisphere.agency/ai-authority-index/data#blueprint-diy).

tools.name: get_blueprint_progress
tools.description: Where every play and move in your Blueprint stands, with the counts done, in progress, and not started. DIY Blueprint tool: needs a key whose plan includes them (https://thirdhemisphere.agency/ai-authority-index/data#blueprint-diy).

tools.name: kumulierung_pruefen
tools.description: Darf Vormaterial aus einem Partnerland der EU für den Ursprung der fertigen Ware zählen, wenn sie in ein bestimmtes Land verkauft wird? Nach der Pan-Europa-Mittelmeer-Kumulierung und den Abkommen mit dem Vereinigten Königreich, Japan, Kanada, Südkorea und dem Mercosur, mit dem Vermerk für den Ursprungsnachweis. Ob die Ware die Listenregel ihres Kapitels erfüllt, sagt das Werkzeug nicht.

tools.name: praeferenznachweis_bestimmen
tools.description: Welcher Präferenznachweis gilt für die Ausfuhr aus der EU in ein Land (EUR.1, A.TR, Erklärung zum Ursprung auf der Rechnung, REX), mit Wertgrenze und Wortlaut der Erklärung. Zeigt die Regeln des Abkommens für das Land, keine Aussage über den Ursprung der Ware.

tools.name: incoterms_waehlen
tools.description: Ordnet Antworten zu Transportweg, Fracht, Gefahrübergang, Versicherung, Einfuhrabgaben und Abladen einer Klausel der Incoterms® 2020 zu, mit der Angabe für Feld 14 01 der Ausfuhranmeldung. Die Wahl trifft der Nutzer mit seinem Vertragspartner. Die Fragen stehen aus Sicht des Verkäufers; wer aus einem Land außerhalb der EU einkauft, beantwortet sie für seinen Lieferanten. Für den Zollwert der Einfuhr zählen Fracht und Versicherung bis zur EU-Grenze mit (Art. 71 UZK), auch bei EXW oder FCA.

tools.name: warennummer_suchen
tools.description: Sucht mit Wörtern oder einer Nummer (2 bis 11 Ziffern) in der Kombinierten Nomenklatur und zeigt höchstens 10 Codes mit dem amtlichen Wortlaut, nach Code sortiert, ohne Rangfolge. Die achtstellige Warennummer gilt für Ausfuhr und Einfuhr; die 9. und 10. Stelle (TARIC) für die Einfuhranmeldung zeigt das Werkzeug nicht. Die Auswahl trifft der Nutzer. Verbindlich ist nur eine verbindliche Zolltarifauskunft (vZTA).

tools.name: ausfuhranmeldung_noetig
tools.description: Der Satz der Vorprüfung von zoll.agency für Bestimmungsland, Warenwert und Gewicht der ganzen Lieferung, nach der Grenze von 1.000 EUR und 1.000 kg (Art. 137 UZK-DA), dazu was je nach Versandweg gilt. Ohne Rechnung; Verbote, Beschränkungen und Rückware berücksichtigt es nicht.

tools.name: ratgeber_suchen
tools.description: Sucht in den Seiten von zoll.agency zu Einfuhr und Ausfuhr (Ratgeber, Themen, Werkzeuge, Leistungen) wie das Suchfeld der Seite und gibt höchstens 10 Treffer mit Titel, einem Satz und Adresse zurück.

tools.name: einfuhr_weg_bestimmen
tools.description: Der Einfuhr-Wegweiser von zoll.agency: Für eine Sendung aus einem Land außerhalb der EU, nach Empfänger (Firma oder privat), Versandweg (Post, Kurier, Spedition), Wert bis oder über 150 EUR und ob sie schon beim Zollamt liegt, wer sie in der Regel anmeldet (Post, Kurier, Spediteur oder der Empfänger selbst in der Internetzollanmeldung IZA) und was der Empfänger tut, mit Quelle. Liegen Versendungsland oder Ursprung in Russland, Belarus, Iran oder Nordkorea, oder wurde die Ware aus Russland oder Belarus ausgeführt, kommt stattdessen der Stopp mit Verordnung und Fassung auf EUR-Lex. Zoll und Einfuhrumsatzsteuer rechnet das Werkzeug nicht.

tools.name: vorpruefung
tools.description: Die Vorprüfung von zoll.agency mit den Angaben einer Handelsrechnung, die der Assistent aus der Rechnung übernimmt: Versender und Empfänger mit Land, Positionen mit Beschreibung, Menge, Wert, Ursprung, Gewicht und Warennummer, Währung, Lieferbedingung, Fracht und Versicherung, Nummer und Datum der Rechnung. Die Richtung folgt aus den Ländern: Versender außerhalb der EU und Empfänger in Deutschland ist eine Einfuhr, Versender in Deutschland und Empfänger außerhalb der EU eine Ausfuhr. Ausfuhr: ob eine elektronische Ausfuhranmeldung nötig ist (EU, Sondergebiete, Sanktionsländer, Rückware, Veredelung, Wert und Gewicht, Anmeldung nachholen), was auf der Rechnung fehlt, Präferenznachweis. Einfuhr: Stopp bei Russland, Belarus, Iran und Nordkorea, wer die Sendung anmeldet, Waren mit Verboten oder Beschränkungen, Rechenprobe der Rechnung, was fehlt, Treffer der Warennummernsuche und geschätzte Abgaben. Ist eine Anmeldung über zoll.agency möglich, speichert das Werkzeug die Angaben zur Übernahme und gibt einen Link zurück, der 24 Stunden gilt; ohne Übernahme werden die Angaben danach gelöscht. Die Anmeldung erstellt der Nutzer nach der Anmeldung auf zoll.agency mit der hochgeladenen Rechnung. Nur aufrufen, wenn der Nutzer eine konkrete Rechnung vorprüfen will. Keine Zollberatung und keine Prüfung des Einzelfalls.

tools.name: list_rule_sets
tools.description: List every deadline rule set 1Court covers, with rule counts and scope. Coverage: Deadlines: California in depth (civil, family, probate, eviction, small claims, government claims, criminal, juvenile, appeals, agencies, pre-suit clocks, special proceedings, statutes of limitations; local rules for all 58 counties), federal civil and criminal, federal bankruptcy, and a partial Texas set. Other states’ deadlines are not covered. Court directory: every U.S. county. Use the rule_set ids with search_rules, get_rule and calculate_deadline.

tools.name: search_rules
tools.description: Find deadline rules by plain words (for example "opposition to motion", "answer complaint", "notice of appeal"). Searches rule names, ids, citations and triggers. Optionally limit to one rule_set (TX, CA, CA-FAM, CA-APP, US, US-BK, US-CRIM, CA-PROB, CA-UD, CA-SC, CA-GOV, CA-CRIM, CA-JUV, CA-AGENCY, CA-PRESUIT, CA-SPECIAL, CA-SOL). Returns up to 20 rules with their rule_set, rule_id and rule page URL; use get_rule or calculate_deadline next.

tools.name: get_rule
tools.description: Get one deadline rule: its period, trigger, citation, the verbatim rule text, the official source URL, the 1Court rule page, any disclosed alternate reading (safe-date policy) and any fixed statutory dates. Show the user the citation and source link with every date or rule. Results are not legal advice.

tools.name: list_triggers
tools.description: List the trigger events ("what happened": summons served, motion hearing date, trial date, notice of entry of judgment served...) that a court's deadline rules run from, for one rule set (TX, CA, CA-FAM, CA-APP, US, US-BK, US-CRIM, CA-PROB, CA-UD, CA-SC, CA-GOV, CA-CRIM, CA-JUV, CA-AGENCY, CA-PRESUIT, CA-SPECIAL, CA-SOL). Each trigger shows how many deadlines it starts, whether the service method changes the dates, and, for broad triggers, the kinds you can narrow to (for a motion hearing: noticed motion, summary judgment...). Use with deadlines_from_trigger. Coverage: Deadlines: California in depth (civil, family, probate, eviction, small claims, government claims, criminal, juvenile, appeals, agencies, pre-suit clocks, special proceedings, statutes of limitations; local rules for all 58 counties), federal civil and criminal, federal bankruptcy, and a partial Texas set. Other states’ deadlines are not covered. Court directory: every U.S. county.

tools.name: deadlines_from_trigger
tools.description: Every deadline that follows one trigger event, like a docketing system: court, trigger, date in; all resulting deadlines out, each with its date, the rule citation, the official source and the 1Court rule page. Deadlines that apply only to some case types (limited civil, asbestos, PI Pathway...) are listed separately. For broad triggers (a motion hearing covers every motion type), pass kind to narrow (e.g. "Noticed motion", "Motion for summary judgment"); otherwise the usual kind is chosen and the rest are listed as other_deadlines. Ask the user for the trigger date and how the paper was served; do not assume them. Show the user the citation and source link with every date or rule. Results are not legal advice. Coverage: Deadlines: California in depth (civil, family, probate, eviction, small claims, government claims, criminal, juvenile, appeals, agencies, pre-suit clocks, special proceedings, statutes of limitations; local rules for all 58 counties), federal civil and criminal, federal bankruptcy, and a partial Texas set. Other states’ deadlines are not covered. Court directory: every U.S. county.

tools.name: list_deadline_rules
tools.description: List the deadline types 1Court can calculate for one rule set (TX, CA, CA-FAM, CA-APP, US, US-BK, US-CRIM, CA-PROB, CA-UD, CA-SC, CA-GOV, CA-CRIM, CA-JUV, CA-AGENCY, CA-PRESUIT, CA-SPECIAL, CA-SOL). Add county (California superior court, e.g. los-angeles) or court (cacd, cand, casd, caed, ca9 for US and US-CRIM; cacb, canb, casb, caeb for US-BK; 1dca to 6dca for CA-APP) to include local rules. Coverage: Deadlines: California in depth (civil, family, probate, eviction, small claims, government claims, criminal, juvenile, appeals, agencies, pre-suit clocks, special proceedings, statutes of limitations; local rules for all 58 counties), federal civil and criminal, federal bankruptcy, and a partial Texas set. Other states’ deadlines are not covered. Court directory: every U.S. county.

tools.name: calculate_deadline
tools.description: Calculate a court deadline from cited rules (weekends, court holidays, service extensions and local rules applied). Returns the date, each counting step, the verbatim rule text and source for every rule used, any safe-date disclosure and any fixed statutory dates. Ask the user for the trigger date and how the paper was served; do not assume them. Show the user the citation and source link with every date or rule. Results are not legal advice. Coverage: Deadlines: California in depth (civil, family, probate, eviction, small claims, government claims, criminal, juvenile, appeals, agencies, pre-suit clocks, special proceedings, statutes of limitations; local rules for all 58 counties), federal civil and criminal, federal bankruptcy, and a partial Texas set. Other states’ deadlines are not covered. Court directory: every U.S. county.

tools.name: list_states
tools.description: List the U.S. states in the 1Court Directory, with how many counties each has. Use this to discover coverage before looking up a county.

tools.name: list_counties
tools.description: List the counties covered in a U.S. state (full name, 2-letter code or slug), each with its 1Court page URL.

tools.name: get_court_info
tools.description: Get verified court information for one U.S. county: clerk contacts, courthouse address, e-filing provider and whether it is mandatory, filing fees, case lookup, self-help, jury service and payment links, with the date it was last verified. civil_filing_fee is null when not yet verified (fee_status "unknown"), and some counties have no fixed fee (fee_status "clerk_sets_deposit"). Tell the user to confirm fees with the clerk before filing, and cite the 1Court page URL.

tools.name: search_courts
tools.description: Search the 1Court Directory by county or state name, courthouse name, city, or phone number. Returns matching counties and courthouses with their 1Court page URLs.

tools.name: checkDomain
tools.description: Reads the public DNS of one domain and reports SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MX, MTA-STS and TLS-RPT findings, risks, unknowns and the exact DNS changes to fix them. Read-only; nothing is stored.

tools.name: quoteFixVerify
tools.description: Runs the email-authentication check of one domain and returns a machine-readable, NON-BINDING quote for Fix & Verify: price (EUR 99 net per domain), scope (exact DNS changes), acceptance criteria and the baseline to verify against later. Orders are not open: it creates no order, contract or payment and stores nothing. Keep the returned criteria and baseline to call verifyFixVerify after the records are published.

tools.name: verifyFixVerify
tools.description: Re-runs the check of the domain and compares it with the acceptance criteria and baseline of an earlier quoteFixVerify result: PASS when every criterion is resolved and no new critical or high finding appeared. Read-only; nothing is stored; a pass is not an invoice while orders are closed.

tools.name: search_domains
tools.description: Search the 4ai.ai portfolio of premium .ai domain names for sale. Filter by a word in the name, a category (see list_categories), type and maximum length. Every result has an offer link.

tools.name: get_domain
tools.description: Details for one domain in the 4ai portfolio (for example "p0.ai"): categories, page, offer link, and comparable public .ai sales. Says so if the domain is not in the portfolio.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Categories of .ai domains in the 4ai portfolio, with what they are good for and how many names each has.

tools.name: estimate_domain_value
tools.description: Free value estimate for any .ai domain name: auction, marketplace and brokerage values with likely ranges, the type of name, a short verdict and notes. Also says if the name is for sale on 4ai, with an offer link. Up to 100 names per call.

tools.name: suggest_domains
tools.description: Describe a company, product or idea in plain words (e.g. "telehealth app for mental health", "crypto casino", "quantum chip startup") and get the best-fitting .ai domains from the 4ai portfolio, ranked, each with the reason it fits and an offer link. Use this when the user asks for a .ai name for something.

tools.name: similar_domains
tools.description: Alternatives to a .ai domain: give any name (taken, too expensive, or one the user already likes) and get the closest .ai domains that are for sale on 4ai.

tools.name: get_offer_link
tools.description: A link to the offer form for a 4ai domain with the amount (and an optional note) filled in. Nothing is sent: the user opens the link, checks the offer and sends it. Minimum offer $3,000.

tools.name: compare_domains
tools.description: Compare 2 to 5 .ai domain names side by side: length, type, words, whether 4ai sells it, estimated value ranges and a short verdict.

tools.name: how_buying_works
tools.description: The steps, payment (Escrow.com), fees, minimum offer and transfer time for buying a .ai domain from 4ai. Use it when the user asks whether buying is safe or how it works.

tools.name: ai_domain_sales
tools.description: The biggest publicly reported .ai domain sales (price in USD, date, venue, source). Useful to estimate what a .ai domain is worth.

tools.name: list_catalogs
tools.description: List every A2UI catalog with a when-to-use, so you can pick the extension catalogs a surface needs. The base catalog (a2ui-atoms-v1) is always resolved.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Return one catalog's atoms (type + one-line description) so you know its vocabulary.

tools.name: find_atoms
tools.description: Semantic search over the atom catalog: describe the UI piece you need in plain words and get the best-matching atoms, ranked best-first, each with a description and an example need. YOU choose from the list (the first entries are most likely, but check the descriptions), then call get_atom_schema for the one(s) you pick. Use this instead of scanning get_catalog when the vocabulary is large. Describe the need as a user would (e.g. "let clients choose grooming services and see the total price"), not by guessing an atom name. Pass `renderer` to keep only atoms that renderer draws as intended (status drawn or native); each result then carries renderer_status.

tools.name: get_atom_schema
tools.description: Return the PROP SHAPE (field names + what each field takes) for named atoms. get_catalog tells you an atom EXISTS; this tells you how to fill it. Call this before authoring any atom you have not used before — guessing prop names is the single most common cause of an atom rendering empty or wrong. Accepts several types at once, so a multi-atom surface resolves in one call. Each atom also carries `renderers`: renderer id -> measured status (web: drawn, drawn_with_differences, not_verified, not_supported, not_measured; flutter: native, degraded, not_supported, not_measured; compose: native, not_supported, not_measured). Only drawn and native mean it draws as intended; degraded = lowered to Basic components. renderers_matrix is the URL holding the reasons and evidence (atoms[<atom>][<renderer>]). Atoms not yet measured have no renderers.

tools.name: required_catalogs
tools.description: Given an A2UI payload, return the resolvable catalog URIs it needs (deterministic — pure function of the atoms).

tools.name: build_multi_page_surface
tools.description: Build a multi-section A2UI app from raw title+content sections — you never estimate size or decide how to split; each section becomes its own independently-encoded page (no shared hub, so per-page size never grows with page count — genuinely unlimited sections). Returns the first page's `url` plus a `pages` array ([{heading, url}]) for every section — present that list to the user yourself (e.g. numbered links); pages do not cross-link to each other. Prefer this over make_surface_url for multi-section content.

tools.name: make_surface_url
tools.description: Render an A2UI payload in the CALLER'S OWN environment. Pass renderer_url (your deployed renderer /exec) and get a live URL + the catalogs it declares. Omit renderer_url to get the encoded fragment + BYO guidance. We host nothing and never see your content.  NEVER hand-write your own gzip/base64 encoding for the ?p= URL, in ANY language, even as a "just this once" fallback. This is the single most common cause of "could not decompress gzip" — a self-written encoder with one wrong flag (wrong wbits, standard vs. urlsafe base64, un-stripped padding) produces a broken URL at ANY size, not just large ones. Always call this tool again — never substitute your own implementation.  SIZING IS AUTOMATIC — you do not need to estimate, count characters, or decide whether to split. Call this tool ONCE with your FULL, unsplit payload. If it fits, you get back `url` (and nothing else to do). If it does not fit the real size ceiling, the tool SPLITS IT FOR YOU server-side (at natural heading boundaries) and returns `auto_split: true` plus a `pages` array of independent URLs — present that list to the user (e.g. as numbered links) instead of the single `url`. Never pre-split your content before the first call; always send everything in one call and let the response tell you what happened.  GRADUATE substantial surfaces with emit_deployment instead (no size limit at all) when you want a standing app rather than a shareable link.  IF A RENDER CHECK REPORTS "could not decompress gzip" / "Render error" / "invalid distance too far back" on a URL this tool returned: STOP. Do NOT call this tool again with the SAME unchanged payload — re-call it with the SAME payload once to confirm, and if it still fails, use emit_deployment instead. Never fall back to a hand-written encoding script.

tools.name: preview_url
tools.description: Quick DEMO render on the public renderer (ephemeral, nothing stored). Limited to 2 runs per client, then deploy your own renderer and use make_surface_url. Onboarding only — not the workflow. DATA-IN-URL: keep payloads SMALL (URL < ~2000 chars); large payloads make long URLs that get truncated (→ render errors). For substantial content GRADUATE with emit_deployment instead — no size limit.

tools.name: render_surface
tools.description: Render an A2UI payload INSIDE the chat as a live interactive view (MCP Apps hosts only — on other hosts this returns the payload as text). No URL, no size ceiling, nothing stored: the payload travels in the tool result and renders in the a2ui_catalog_view. Accepts the blocks dialect or a v1.0 createSurface envelope (templates + dataModel decode in the view). Prefer this over preview_url when the host supports MCP Apps.  If the user names one of the Workspace's own pre-built views — Wall Builder, profile, history, links, composer — call open_workspace(view: ...) instead of composing one here yourself; those are wired demos with their own state, not something to reconstruct block by block. And never invent a generic block type (there is no "text" or "button" atom) — call get_catalog / get_atom_schema for the real vocabulary first; an unrecognised type is caught and replaced with a visible notice rather than silently dropped, but the block still won't render as intended.

tools.name: make_film
tools.description: Make a short motion film (a social clip, launch teaser, quote card...) built by the A2UI Design Studio: you choose a template and supply the words; the studio builds the film. Use this instead of composing motion_timeline blocks yourself. It plays inline here and comes with a link that opens in the A2UI Studio app on Android, where the user can edit the text and export MP4 or GIF on the phone.  BEFORE CALLING, ask the user in one short message for what you do not know: what it is about (the hook line), any real numbers with their labels, the call to action, and where it will be posted (portrait 9:16 for LinkedIn/Instagram/stories, 16:9 for slides or YouTube, 1:1 for a quote card). Never invent statistics: with no real numbers, use scenes without a Numbers or Chart scene.  Templates (each a ready scene sequence; pass `scenes` to replace it): launch: Product launch, Title, numbers, phone, call to action (16:9; scenes title > stats > device > cta) data: Data story, Chart, numbers, steps (16:9; scenes title > chart > stats > steps) agent: Agent demo, Chat, particle word, CTA (16:9; scenes chat > word > cta) quote: Quote card, A quote and a name (1:1; scenes quote > cta) hook: LinkedIn hook, Portrait: captions, numbers, CTA (9:16; scenes captions > stats > cta) client: Client feature demo, Title, features that light up beside your pictures, CTA (16:9; scenes title > features > cta) event: Event promo, Particle word, title, photo, CTA (16:9; scenes word > title > morph > cta)  Scene types and their fields (`fields` keys; text supports *word* for the accent colour; list fields take one item per line in the format the label gives): title (Title): eyebrow = Eyebrow; headline = Headline (use *word* for accent); sub = Subline stats (Numbers): kicker = Kicker; stats = Stats, one per line: value | label; roll = Number style chart (Chart): heading = Heading; kind = Chart; data = Data, one per line: label value; unit = Unit chat (Chat): heading = Heading; messages = Messages, alternating you / agent word (Particle word): word = Word (A-Z 0-9, up to 12); sub = Subline features (Feature walkthrough): heading = Heading; features = Features (2-6): a title, a line of detail and an optional picture each; images =  collage (Collage swap): heading = Heading; sets = Sets of tiles, up to 4, separated by a blank line. One tile per line: label | optional picture link (2-6 tiles a set); hold = Seconds each set stays (0.8 to 8); swap = Seconds the swap and outline change take (0.4 to 3); fx = Panel outline bubbles (Bubbles title): heading = Heading; count = Bubbles (2-14) beats (Beat countdown): items = One word or number per beat, 2-8 lines (fades; keep each beat over 0.35 s) dock (Icon dock): heading = Heading; items = Icons, one per line: glyph | name (2-7) lit (Cards light up): heading = Heading; cards = Cards, one per line: title | text (2-6) arcs (Arc mark): heading = Heading; effect = Effect lockup (Centred lockup): lines = Lines, one per line; write {mark} where the arc mark goes (up to 4 lines); effect = Effect pattern (Text pattern): text = Repeated text; word = One word turned on its side (optional); angle = Angle (-90 to 90) fit (Fill-the-width word): word = Word (up to 20 characters); recede = Recede at the end; effect = Effect morph (Shape morph): heading = Heading; shapes = Shapes (comma list; also panel, notch, step, tab); wide = Wide panel (1.78:1); effect = Effect image (Photo): heading = Heading; url = Image URL (https); caption = Caption device (Phone): heading = Heading; items = Checklist on the phone captions (Captions): sentence = Sentence (lights word by word) steps (Steps): heading = Heading; steps = Steps, one per line (2-6) quote (Quote): quote = Quote; name = Name; role = Role cta (Call to action): headline = Headline; b1 = Button 1 text; l1 = Button 1 link; b2 = Button 2 text; l2 = Button 2 link; foot = Footer line  Give the user the returned `link` as well as showing the film.

tools.name: sketch_agent_start
tools.description: Start a real, live agent_sketchpad drawing: one Gemini call plans a complete picture as an ordered list of SVG strokes, the first stroke renders immediately, and the rest reveal as you call sketch_agent_poll again — a real multi-turn task, not a single one-shot render. MCP Apps hosts only (same as render_surface). Stateless server: the task is held in KV for 1 hour, not in this connection — keep the returned taskId and the next cursor to keep polling.

tools.name: sketch_agent_poll
tools.description: Continue a sketch_agent_start task: returns every stroke newer than the given cursor (an event log, not a snapshot — nothing is skipped regardless of poll timing) plus the next cursor, reveals the result in-chat the same way render_surface does, and reports whether the drawing is complete. Call again with the returned cursor until done is true.

tools.name: render_ping
tools.description: Diagnostic: render a tiny test view in-chat (MCP Apps hosts only). Proves view mounting works independent of the full catalog renderer. Echoes back whatever payload you pass.

tools.name: wasm_spike
tools.description: Diagnostic (MCP Apps hosts only): mounts a view that instantiates a tiny hand-assembled WebAssembly module, computes per-frame state in it, renders to canvas, and captures arrow-key input -- the same three ingredients a WASM game port would need. Answers whether THIS host permits WASM execution inside a ui:// View iframe; it proves nothing about any other host or sandbox.

tools.name: diagram_studio
tools.description: Draw a diagram in-chat with the full Diagram Studio interface (MCP Apps hosts only; it opens fullscreen where the host allows it). YOU write the diagram; nothing is generated server-side and nothing is stored. PREFER `graph`: give vertices (id, label, type start|process|decision|database|cloud|end) and edges (source, target, optional label). The person then gets the whole studio: they can switch the same graph between Mermaid, D2, PlantUML and draw.io, flip its direction, zoom, copy the code, open it in the real draw.io editor with one click, and edit nodes and connections themselves (their edits come back to you). Use `syntax` with `source` instead only for diagrams a flow graph cannot express, drawn exactly as written: "mermaid" for sequence, class, state, ER, gantt and mind maps; "d2" for architecture diagrams with containers and nested boxes. Give exactly one of `graph` or `syntax` with `source`. Keep diagrams compact (the input schema states the limits). If the tool or the view reports a problem, fix it and call this tool again. On a host without MCP Apps support the diagram comes back as text.

tools.name: amiga
tools.description: Open a real, cycle-exact Amiga 500 emulator in-chat (MCP Apps hosts only). Boots straight into AROS, a free open-source environment (no copyrighted Kickstart ROM involved), with a public-domain Amiga game already loaded and running. This is a fixed, self-contained retro-computing demo -- there is nothing to configure and no arguments to give it; call it when someone wants to see or play with a real emulated Amiga. On a host without MCP Apps support this says so as text; an emulator has no useful non-visual form.

tools.name: distill_document
tools.description: Compile a training.md / roadmap markdown document into a live interactive A2UI app — DETERMINISTIC parser, no model involved. Fact sheet: input is MARKDOWN following the training-md contract (frontmatter id/domain/name/source/license + a # Steps section); the text transits to the catalog's stateless parser service for the duration of the call and is NOT stored; lint errors come back as a structured report (fix and re-call). On success the result IS the compiled surface — MCP Apps hosts paint it in the view; other hosts can pass the returned payload to preview_url for a link.

tools.name: publish_url
tools.description: STORES the payload server-side and returns a SHORT shareable link. Opt-in only: requires acknowledge_storage=true — confirm with the user first that they accept operator-hosted storage (ONE WEEK retention on the public tier, revocable earlier via the returned delete_token; anyone with the link can view). target "play" (default) renders in the a2uicatalog playground by reference (no URL size ceiling); target "gas" makes the short link redirect to the public Apps Script renderer. For storage in the USER's own account use emit_deployment; for nothing-stored links use preview_url.

tools.name: unpublish_url
tools.description: Delete a published short link before its TTL using the delete_token returned by publish_url.

tools.name: emit_deployment
tools.description: 🎓 GRADUATE a tested surface into a dedicated, DEPLOYER-ONLY standing app in YOUR OWN Google Apps Script account. Returns a deterministic recipe (config files + clasp ops + least-privilege scopes derived from the atoms + verify) — you run it with your own clasp; nothing runs on our side, we hold no creds.

tools.name: emit_training_runbook
tools.description: Build a multi-lesson training/course surface as ONE properly-linked page with real in-app tab navigation between lessons — prefer this over build_multi_page_surface for training/course content specifically: that tool produces N independent pages with NO links between them (you must present the list yourself); this tool produces one page where lessons are real, clickable tabs. Zero sizing/estimation judgment required — give it your lessons, it handles composition and navigation.

tools.name: emit_runbook_surface
tools.description: Stamp your content through a DECLARED runbook — a pre-authored, judgment-free surface composition. You supply content only; the runbook supplies the composition (which atoms, how arranged, navigation). DISCOVERY: call with runbook_id only (no content) to get that runbook's input_contract + parsing_guide — shape your source data to the contract (parsing is your job as the consumer), then call again with `content`. Some runbooks also return `elicit` — questions to ASK THE USER before you fill the contract. Ask them; do not guess the answers. ON SUCCESS YOU GET BOTH `payload` AND `url`, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME OFFER. `payload` is the compiled surface — pass it STRAIGHT to render_surface and the reading appears inline, in the conversation, where the reader already is. `url` is the shareable link, for later or for elsewhere. Default to rendering: handing back only a link makes the reader leave to see the thing they asked for. If the reading was too large to encode as a link you get `payload` and `url_unavailable` instead — that is a SUCCESS, so render it and say the link is missing. Available stampable runbooks: (1) learning_hub — curriculum/revision study app: subject tabs, slide pills, timeline/drill/flashcards/quiz/takeaways/method interactions per slide, the full rich hub UI. Prefer this over emit_training_runbook for study/curriculum content — much richer output, still zero composition decisions. (2) article_playbook — a steered critical reading of SOMEONE ELSE'S article: source attribution bar, a hero mental-model card, then rungs down a rail. The reader picks a lens (explain, apply to their domain, challenge, situate in prior art) and says what they want it to look for; the rung progression is Toulmin (claim → grounds → warrant) so the analysis lands on the assumption a summary drops. Use it whenever asked to analyse, critique, tear down, or work out what an article means for a particular domain. You fetch and read the article yourself; nothing is retrieved server-side.

tools.name: describe_playbook
tools.description: Explain a playbook to a HUMAN as a rendered surface: the frame it reads against, the lenses available, and the questions it will ask them. Compiled from the runbook declaration, so it costs nothing and cannot drift from what the stamper enforces. This is NOT emit_runbook_surface discovery — that returns a contract addressed to YOU. Use this when someone asks what a playbook does or how it works; pass the result to render_surface.

tools.name: open_workspace
tools.description: Open the A2UI Workspace — a rendered surface that IS the demo: each tool is introduced by the scenario it answers, then wired to run, then shows what it saved. This tool RENDERS ITSELF: its result carries the view, so call it alone and show the result — do NOT pass it on to render_surface, and do not describe the payload in prose. Call it when the user asks to open the workspace, wants to see what this connector can do, asks what is saved about them, or names one of its tools directly — e.g. "open the Wall Builder" means THIS tool with view: "wall_builder", not a separate tool named wall_builder. It shows a display name they chose, never their email.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Read the signed-in reader's saved profile and recent history. Call this BEFORE asking a runbook's `elicit` questions: if a domain or default lens is already saved, CONFIRM it ("reading as: a2ui, generative ui — change?") instead of asking from scratch. Returns available:false on the public endpoint, where there is no one to have a profile — that is the designed state, so degrade quietly and just ask the questions.

tools.name: save_profile
tools.description: Update the signed-in reader's profile. Only the keys you pass change; pass null to clear one. Save what the reader TOLD you, never what you inferred from one article — a profile that drifts on every reading is worse than no profile, because they stop being able to predict what it will do.

tools.name: save_reading
tools.description: Record a stamped surface in the reader's history so it can be compared and reopened later. Call it AFTER emit_runbook_surface, and PASS ITS `payload` — that stores the reading itself rather than a link to it. Silently no-ops when nobody is signed in.

tools.name: export_reading
tools.description: Export a kept reading as something that outlives this connector. format "html" returns ONE self-contained file — styles inlined, no network, opens in any browser years from now with nothing installed. "url" rebuilds a link against any renderer (yours by preference). "surface" returns the payload for repainting in place. "json" returns the decoded payload. Needs a reading saved WITH its payload; older link-only rows cannot be re-rendered and will say so.

tools.name: render_reading_to_slack
tools.description: Post a kept reading into Slack as real, native Block Kit — the continuity proof: generate here, save it, and the SAME content reopens in Slack, not a link back to a renderer. Requires the caller's Slack account to already be linked (`/a2ui link` in Slack) and only works on an authenticated connection — it posts to a real workspace using a shared bot token.

tools.name: list_readings
tools.description: The reader's recent stamped surfaces, newest first — what makes "compare this to my last three teardowns" answerable at all. Optionally filter to one runbook. Returns available:false when nobody is signed in.

tools.name: delete_reading
tools.description: Permanently remove one or more of the reader's saved readings from their History. Takes an array so the Workspace's multi-select can delete a batch in one call rather than one round trip per row. Ids that don't exist (or belong to someone else's history) are silently skipped — the response's `deleted` count says how many rows actually went, never assume it equals the number of ids you sent.

tools.name: read_article
tools.description: Have the catalog's own model (Gemini) read an article through the article_playbook runbook and KEEP the reading in the signed-in reader's history, in one call. For a client with no model of its own (the Android analyser app), or when the reader asks for a Gemini reading. If you can read the article yourself, prefer emit_runbook_surface + save_reading. Pass `text` when you already have the article (it is then the only source the reading may quote), else `url` and it is fetched server-side. Takes 20-60 s. Needs a signed-in reader; capped per reader per day.

tools.name: deck_schema
tools.description: List the slide layouts the PPTX renderer builds (title, bullets, stats, quote, table, media, cta), each field with its limits, the targets, the film-only scenes, and the A2UI atoms that have a slide recipe (payload_atoms). Read this before writing a deck.

tools.name: deck_validate
tools.description: Check a deck (scene list or A2UI payload) without building it. Returns every error with its slide, field and exact limit, warnings (no speaker notes, no link) and, for a payload, which atoms have no slide recipe. Not rate-limited.

tools.name: deck_build
tools.description: Build a PowerPoint (.pptx) file from a scene list or an A2UI payload. Deterministic (same input, same bytes), nothing is stored or fetched, text is fitted with real font metrics and the file is linted (overlap, bounds, contrast, alt text). Returns the file as an embedded resource plus a report: errors, lint, warnings and unsupported atoms. Opens in PowerPoint and Google Slides (checked in Google Slides). Demo limit: 10 builds a day per connection.

tools.name: drawio_open
tools.description: Open a diagram you wrote in draw.io (diagrams.net). YOU write the diagram as mxGraph XML, the format draw.io reads; this tool checks it, and returns a link that opens it in the draw.io editor for the person, plus a .drawio file to download (kept for one hour). Nothing is drawn or laid out for you, so give every shape its x, y, width and height. The XML must be uncompressed and shaped like this (ids unique, every shape parent="1", edges name source and target ids): <mxGraphModel><root><mxCell id="0"/><mxCell id="1" parent="0"/><mxCell id="a" value="Start" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="40" width="120" height="60" as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="b" value="Done" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="240" y="40" width="120" height="60" as="geometry"/></mxCell><mxCell id="e1" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;html=1;" edge="1" parent="1" source="a" target="b"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"/></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel> If the check finds problems it lists each one with the cell id and the fix; correct the XML and call again. Limits: 200 KB of XML and 500 cells.
