TO PLACE EXACTLY ONE ORDER WITH NO MISTAKES: (1) on get_fabrication_quote list only that shop in vendors and state the pick in selection — the shop, plus the material, finish and shipping speed wanted; (2) read selection_match on the quote: status "one" means exactly one option answers the pick, "many" means say more in the pick (color, thickness, quantity), "none" means nothing on the quote answers it; (3) call create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — it orders that one option at the picked shipping speed, or refuses and creates nothing (selection_not_unique: the pick is not exactly one option; selection_speed_unavailable: the option does not show the picked speed now — an order never takes another speed in its place). It returns the selected checkout result: a hosted payment link by default, or the saved-card outcome when pay is saved on a keyed connection.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Start a cart, for a user who wants several parts and one payment. Pass items to put parts in at once; each is named by quote_id (a quote you already have — its shops are not asked again), or by file_id or file_url (a design that has no quote yet — it gets one ordinary quote, priced exactly as get_fabrication_quote would price it). Returns the cart with its cart_id. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read a cart: every part with its quote, the rules on it (constraints_asked), its pick (selection) and what the pick comes to — the shop, the price, the shipping speed and the arrival date — plus whether that option can be ordered right now (checkout.state: "ready"; "needs_check" = the shop has to confirm it first; "checking" = the shop is answering, read again shortly; "not_orderable" = pick another option; checkout.reason says why in a sentence and checkout.code says it as one word — on a "needs_check" part, "confirmation_lapsed" or "never_confirmed" mean reconfirm true will ask its one shop (and so will checkout_cart, by itself), "ask_limited" means the option is chosen and its shop is asked when the user pays, while "rechecking" (the part was copied from a shared cart and its shops are still being asked: read the cart again) and "shop_asks_off" (the network is not asking shops for this part right now) mean reconfirm true will start nothing for it). now is the network's own clock when the answer was made: work out the time left until checkout.confirmed_until from now, not from your own clock. by_shop groups the picked parts by the shop that makes them with subtotals and shipping, and total_cents is what the picked parts cost together. Parts with nothing picked are listed in unpicked_item_ids and are in no total. A plain read asks no shop. Pass reopen true when the user comes back to a cart: parts older than 24 hours are then asked about again, once, one part at a time (the answer's reopen says "asked", "none_needed", or "press_needed" — the old parts were already asked about again once and nothing was done to the cart since; pass pressed true only when the user asks for today's prices). picked.stale, picked.answered_at, picked.eta_days and picked.eta_approximate read as they do on an offer: when eta_approximate is true say "about N days", never the date. HOW LONG A PRICE HOLDS: a shop's confirmation of a picked option is good for 15 minutes. While it stands the part reads "ready" and checkout.confirmed_until says until when — tell the user the time they have. After it the part is NOT lost: it keeps its pick and its price and reads "needs_check" again. It is confirmed again by its one shop (nobody else is asked) when its option is chosen, and by checkout_cart itself when the user pays; reconfirm true on get_cart starts the same asks ahead of time — read the cart again and "ready" means the price stands. checkout.code "ask_limited" means the option is chosen and its shop will be asked when the user pays. When a part carries price_changed, the shop's answer moved the price or the arrival (direction "up", "down", or "same" when only the arrival moved) — tell the user the old and the new figure before they pay. checkout_cart stops ONCE by itself when the cart's total came back higher than the user agreed to (price_went_up). A part whose prices passed their 24-hour expiry is given a new quote by the read itself (quoted_anew true, price_source "instant"): it shows our instant prices again, its pick is kept, no shop was asked, and its shop confirms the pick when asked. SHIPPING IN A CART: by_shop[].shipping says how each shop's parts ship. mode "ships_separately" = each part is its own order with that shop and its own package, and pays its own shipping; mode "combined" = the shop takes those parts as ONE order and ships them together. Tell the user which it is, in the words of shipping.reason. Name a shipping saving ONLY when shipping.saved_cents is above zero, and only that amount — never promise or hint at a saving for buying several parts from one shop otherwise. When shipping.code is "speeds_differ", the parts of that shop are picked at different shipping speeds; you may tell the user that the shop sends parts together only at one speed, and read the cart again after they change a pick — do not state what it would save before the cart shows it. A SHARED CART: status "shared" means the cart came by a link and can only be read and copied. Never change it, pick on its parts' quotes, run check_offer on them or check it out — each of those is refused (cart_shared). Copy it with fork_cart and work on the copy, which is the user's own cart. A COPIED CART: copied true is present on a cart that was copied from a shared one; a cart never says which cart it was copied from. Each part's price_source says whose prices it shows: "shared" = recent shop prices that were copied with nobody asked — the prices of the person who shared the cart as they stood when it was copied, or the shops' own answers to this same part and request from the last 24 hours; "instant" = our instant prices, because the shared prices could not be copied (they were too old, or still coming in) — no shop has been asked about that part on this quote yet; "own" = this cart's own quote of the part, its shops asked. A pick that travelled with the cart but matches no option now reads selection_match.status "none": that part is still to choose. The buyer, the address, the email and any coupon never travel with a cart. PARTS OLDER THAN 24 HOURS: a shop's answer is shown for 24 hours. A cart copied with fork_cart inside them asks nobody: every part comes with its answers as they stand. A part whose answers are OLDER than 24 hours shows our instant prices first, and (unless the copy was for_link or recheck false) its shops are then asked about it again, one part at a time. Each such part's recheck says where it stands: "queued" = priced, its shops are asked when its turn comes; "asking" = its shops are being asked now; "done" = the shops' answers are in. A part with no recheck is under 24 hours old and nothing is pending for it. A part's quote_id CHANGES when its turn comes, so read quote_id off get_cart every time and never keep an old one. Until every such part reads done, tell the user the prices and dates may still move, and read the cart again; do not start a second copy to hurry it. A picked part goes first and its picked option is confirmed with its shop as part of it. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Put one more part in a cart. Name it ONE way: quote_id (a quote you already have — its shops are not asked again, and the part arrives configured and picked exactly as that quote is), or file_id or file_url (a design that has no quote yet — it gets one ordinary quote, priced exactly as get_fabrication_quote would price it). A cart holds at most 24 parts. Returns the whole cart. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: fork_cart
tools.description: Copy a cart: the same parts in the same order, each configured and picked as it was (a copy made for a link keeps a part's pick only when it was stored with confirmed: true). Use it when the user opens a shared cart, so that nothing they change reaches the cart it was copied from; work on the cart_id this returns from then on. By default the copy is a NEW cart; pass into_cart_id (an open cart the user already holds) to add the copied parts to that cart instead — one call, and that cart is the answer. Use it with for_link true when the user wants to share their own cart: the copy is then a shared cart (status "shared") that can only be read and copied, and its cart_id is the one to hand out — never hand out the cart_id of the cart the user is working on. Pass item_ids to copy only those parts (one part shared by itself is a cart of one). Each part of the answer says quoted_anew: true when a new quote was made for it, false when the shared quote was copied. WHAT EACH WAY COSTS IN SHOP CONTACT: no shop is asked to make any copy, and the answer comes back at once with every part priced. A for_link copy never contacts a shop, then or later. A copy with recheck false never contacts a shop either — use it when you only want to read what is in a shared cart. Any other copy (the default, for a user who opened a shared cart to act on it) asks nobody when the cart's answers are under 24 hours old: each part comes with its shops' answers as they stand. Only a part whose answers are older than 24 hours is asked about again after the copy answers — its shops, as an ordinary quote of that part would ask them, one part at a time — and if anyone got answers for this same part and request in the last 24 hours those are copied instead with nobody asked. Never copy the same cart twice to refresh it — read the copy you have. LIMITS: copies are limited per caller a minute and a day, and the quotes the re-check will really start count against the caller's quote limit (a part whose shops are already being asked, or are queued to be asked, for another copy of the same request starts none); when you act for a person and say so (on_behalf_of), that person has their own counts of copies and of re-check quotes, a minute and a day; over a limit the answer is rate_limited with the seconds to wait, nothing is made and no shop is asked — wait, do not retry at once. A cart id that matches no cart answers "unknown cart" and nothing else. When it is the into_cart_id cart that is not known, the answer is an error with error "into_cart_unknown": nothing was copied — copy again without into_cart_id to get a new cart. A SHARED CART: status "shared" means the cart came by a link and can only be read and copied. Never change it, pick on its parts' quotes, run check_offer on them or check it out — each of those is refused (cart_shared). Copy it with fork_cart and work on the copy, which is the user's own cart. A COPIED CART: copied true is present on a cart that was copied from a shared one; a cart never says which cart it was copied from. Each part's price_source says whose prices it shows: "shared" = recent shop prices that were copied with nobody asked — the prices of the person who shared the cart as they stood when it was copied, or the shops' own answers to this same part and request from the last 24 hours; "instant" = our instant prices, because the shared prices could not be copied (they were too old, or still coming in) — no shop has been asked about that part on this quote yet; "own" = this cart's own quote of the part, its shops asked. A pick that travelled with the cart but matches no option now reads selection_match.status "none": that part is still to choose. The buyer, the address, the email and any coupon never travel with a cart. PARTS OLDER THAN 24 HOURS: a shop's answer is shown for 24 hours. A cart copied with fork_cart inside them asks nobody: every part comes with its answers as they stand. A part whose answers are OLDER than 24 hours shows our instant prices first, and (unless the copy was for_link or recheck false) its shops are then asked about it again, one part at a time. Each such part's recheck says where it stands: "queued" = priced, its shops are asked when its turn comes; "asking" = its shops are being asked now; "done" = the shops' answers are in. A part with no recheck is under 24 hours old and nothing is pending for it. A part's quote_id CHANGES when its turn comes, so read quote_id off get_cart every time and never keep an old one. Until every such part reads done, tell the user the prices and dates may still move, and read the cart again; do not start a second copy to hurry it. A picked part goes first and its picked option is confirmed with its shop as part of it. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Take one part out of a cart. The part's quote is untouched and can be put back with add_to_cart. Returns the whole cart. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: set_cart_item_quote
tools.description: Point a part of a cart at another quote of the same part — for a part that was priced again with get_fabrication_quote. Changing a part with refine_quote needs no call here: pass cart_item_id to refine_quote and the cart follows by itself. Asks no shop. Returns the whole cart. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: checkout_cart
tools.description: Create one checkout for every selected cart part. Hosted payment uses one link; pay saved uses the card on the AFN key. Each part needs a pick that comes to exactly one option (its selection_match reads "one"). A part whose shop still has to confirm it (get_cart shows checkout.state "needs_check" or "checking") is confirmed by this call itself: its one shop is asked — or the ask already running is joined — and the call waits up to wait_s for the answers; no check_offer and no reconfirm read is needed first. Pass max_total_cents: the cart total_cents the user agreed to. ALL OR NOTHING: if any part cannot be ordered, nothing is created, nothing is charged, and the answer (cart_not_ready) names each such part and why — fix those and call again. Pass only_selected true to leave the parts with nothing picked in the cart and order the rest. In hosted-payment mode, returns checkout_url — one secure payment page for the whole cart; give it to the user to pay. After payment AFN places one order per part with its own shop; each part ships by itself unless by_shop[].shipping.mode in the answer reads "combined" for its shop (then that shop takes its parts as one order and ships them together); each order sends its own confirmation email, and get_order_status with the checkout_id shows them all. idempotency_key: make up one unique string for this attempt and send the SAME string only to repeat the very same call — it then returns the same checkout and payment link, never a second set of orders. After ANYTHING changed (the address, the coupon, a part, a pick) make up a NEW string: the old one is refused (idempotency_key_reused), because its payment link is for the cart as it was. A part already paid for by itself is named in the refusal like any other part. When a shop's answer did not come inside wait_s, the cart is refused with that part named (offer_not_ready): send the SAME call again with the SAME idempotency_key (a refused call never uses its key) — it joins the asks already running and nothing is asked twice. When the cart's confirmed total is higher than the user agreed to, the call stops ONCE (price_went_up: old_total_cents, new_total_cents, and items naming the parts that rose) and nothing is created: tell the user, then call again with the new max_total_cents and the same idempotency_key. A coupon applies once, to the cart total. This tool takes NO personal details: never ask for — and never pass — a name, address, email, or phone; the secure payment page collects the shipping address, email, and phone once for the whole cart, even when the user volunteered them in chat. Never ask the user for card details in chat.THE CHECKOUT RULE, enforced by the network for every client: an offer can be ordered only when the shop's own system has accepted this part at this price — its manufacturability check has passed, the price is the shop's own number (price_basis "vendor_api"), and no price confirmation is outstanding. That acceptance is good for 15 minutes (the offer's confirmed_until). THE CHECKOUT CONFIRMS WHAT NEEDS CONFIRMING ITSELF: when the option's shop has not confirmed it, or did more than 15 minutes ago, the checkout asks that ONE shop (it joins the ask already running when choosing the option started one) and waits up to wait_s for the answer; when the wait runs out first the answer is offer_not_ready with retry_after_s — send the SAME call again, it joins the ask and nothing is asked twice. THE PAY RULE: when the confirmed total is at or below the amount the user agreed to, checkout uses the selected payment method (hosted payment by default, or the saved card when pay is saved on a keyed connection); a price the shop confirmed HIGHER than the user agreed to stops ONCE (price_went_up, with old_total_cents and new_total_cents) and nothing is created — tell the user both figures, then send the call again (with the new max_total_cents when you sent one); the new price stands for 15 minutes and no shop is asked again. A passed offer whose price_refresh is still "pending" is refused the same way (offer_not_ready, with retry_after_s): the shop is still confirming its price — re-read the quote and retry then. An offer whose check failed, whose price_refresh reads "failed", or whose fulfillment is "not_connected" cannot be ordered at all (offer_check_failed) — offer the user another option or re-quote. Nothing is charged on any refusal. An offer whose shop could not confirm the part — it declined the part, or did not answer within two minutes of being asked — leaves the quote: it is no longer listed in offers, and its id is refused the same way. If an offer you showed earlier is missing when you re-read the quote, tell the user plainly that the shop could not confirm the part, and carry on with the offers that are listed. SHIPPING IN A CART: by_shop[].shipping says how each shop's parts ship. mode "ships_separately" = each part is its own order with that shop and its own package, and pays its own shipping; mode "combined" = the shop takes those parts as ONE order and ships them together. Tell the user which it is, in the words of shipping.reason. Name a shipping saving ONLY when shipping.saved_cents is above zero, and only that amount — never promise or hint at a saving for buying several parts from one shop otherwise. When shipping.code is "speeds_differ", the parts of that shop are picked at different shipping speeds; you may tell the user that the shop sends parts together only at one speed, and read the cart again after they change a pick — do not state what it would save before the cart shows it. HOW A CART WORKS: each part in a cart IS a quote — its material, finish, quantity, rules and its pick (selection) live on that part's quote, and nothing is kept twice. To change a part, call refine_quote on its quote_id and pass cart_item_id: the cart follows the part to the new quote by itself. To pick the option to order for a part, store the pick on its quote (refine_quote selection). The cart_id is the only key to the cart — whoever holds it can read and change it — so give it only to the user it belongs to, and never put it in a link you did not get from the network.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Check status, ETA and tracking for a UFP order. Pass a checkout id (co_…, from checkout_cart) in order_id to get every order of that cart checkout at once — each part is its own order with its own shop, status and tracking. The answer carries status_url: a link the user can open or pass on to follow the order with no sign-in; it shows progress only (no price, no address, nothing that can change the order).

tools.name: reply_to_maker
tools.description: Send the user's answer to a question the maker (vendor) asked about a UFP order — get_order_status surfaces an open question when one is waiting. Confirm the answer with the user before sending. The network relays it: the maker sees plain text from the network account with the user's contact details and links stripped, so never include emails, phone numbers, or URLs the answer depends on.

tools.name: leave_review
tools.description: Record the user's verified-purchase review of how a UFP order turned out. YOUR JOB IS TO STRUCTURE THE FEEDBACK: turn what the user actually said into stars (1-5 overall) and facet scores — "the cut was sloppy" -> quality, "parts arrived 2 days late" -> timeliness, "wrong color" -> accuracy. Keep the optional comment to a short factual summary of their words; never embellish. ALWAYS draft the review (stars, facets, comment) and confirm it with the user BEFORE calling this tool — e.g. "I'll rate this 2 stars with timeliness 1 because it arrived 2 days late — send it?". One review per order: submitting again updates the existing review. If you do not have the order id from this conversation, ask the user for it (it is on their receipt email and order page); never guess one.

tools.name: get_material_guide
tools.description: Honest, cited material intelligence for material-choice / strength / durability / heat / outdoor questions ("my PLA part broke, what's stronger?", "will this survive outdoors?"). Returns caveats-FIRST facts: published specs (tensile, heat-deflection, UV/outdoor, chemical) each tagged vendor-cited vs general engineering knowledge, "stronger/tougher/hotter than X" ladders (PLA→PETG→ABS/ASA→nylon/PC→metals), and finish/coating options. Call it BEFORE answering such a question, then relay the facts. It supplies FACTS ONLY — comparative specs and vendor-admitted caveats, never a fitness-for-purpose or safety guarantee (that stays your judgment boundary); name express vendor claims "advertised", not "certified".

tools.name: get_network_capabilities
tools.description: The LIVE catalog of what the fabrication network can do RIGHT NOW — no quote needed. Returns the services ledger (tapping, inserts, welding, bending, finishes… with each shop's own size/material/thickness windows), the network's sheet gauge ladder, the stocked hardware combinations (species x thread) with stocked lengths and shop counts — the most-stocked length is the steering default for an unspecified length — the finish options with their stocked color menus, every colour the network can make a part in (network_catalog.colors: per colour family, how many shops stock a material in it and how many coat in it, with the shades — ask for one by passing the family word as `color` with no finish), the material groups a picker shows (network_catalog.material_groups: Plastics, Metals, Woods, Foams, Rubbers, Composites, Paper cork and fabric… with the stock families live under each and the words that ask for them), and per-process manufacturability rules. This is live state, not a spec sheet: it changes as connectors join, leave, or have capability branches toggled, so call it fresh when the user asks what's possible (materials, gauges, hardware, colors, services) rather than answering from memory. PICKER COUNTS: pass `selection` (what the user has already picked: processes, materials, thickness_in, colors, finishes, finish_colors, vendors, vendors_exclude, each a list where any value will do) and the answer adds network_catalog.facets: for every material group and member, gauge rung, colour family, finish and finish colour the catalog lists, `shops` = how many shops the user can order from today declare they make the whole selection plus that option, and `maybe` = further shops whose catalog is silent on part of it (they might); each count sets that dimension's own picks aside. Only an option with shops 0 AND maybe 0 is impossible with the selection; never read a missing count as zero. facets.shops answers each shop against the selection (yes / no / unknown). The counts come from the shops' declared catalogs, nobody is contacted, and nothing on a quote changes. Without `selection` the answer is the same as before.

tools.name: get_shop_offerings
tools.description: What ONE named shop sells right now, read live off the shop's own declared catalog: per process, every stock with its own colours and thicknesses, and every finish with the stocks it goes on and its colours. No quote needed, nobody is contacted, and the user's board does not change. Call it when the user asks what a specific maker offers ("what colours of acrylic does SendCutSend have?", "what else do they do?"). One shop name covers every process it sells. A stock listed with no colours means the shop does not list colours for it, never that it has none. Never answer such a question from the offers on a quote (they show what was offered for one ask, not everything the shop sells) and never from memory.

tools.name: get_shop_gauges
tools.description: Every sheet thickness (gauge) ONE named shop stocks right now, per material — read live off the shop's declared catalog, no quote needed. Call it when the user asks what thicknesses/gauges a specific maker carries ("what thicknesses does SendCutSend have in mild steel?"). For the whole network's ladder use get_network_capabilities instead. Never answer a gauge question from memory.

tools.name: get_price_curve
tools.description: How the per-unit price moves with quantity for a quote you already have: for every shop on the board, the item price per unit at each quantity (default 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000; pass up to 16 of your own in 1..10000) from that shop's own pricing with the network's markup included, plus its arrival window — instant, no shop is contacted, nothing changes on the quote. Call it when the user asks what more or fewer pieces would cost ("what would 50 run me?", "any price breaks?"). The board's quoted price stays the ceiling at the chosen quantity (each option's `live` row); a null cell means that shop's pricing does not cover that quantity — refine_quote with the new quantities gets the real number. Present these as the shops' own pricing, never as an estimate; every order still passes the manufacturability check.

tools.name: check_offer
tools.description: Ask the shop to confirm one unchecked or checking offer. Use this when the user wants the check result before deciding. create_checkout and checkout_cart ask or join the check themselves for the selected option, so this is not a required pre-check. A passed result is orderable at the shown price for 15 minutes. A repriced result confirms that same shop price; do not say the price changed. A failed result cannot be ordered and the offer is removed from the quote; tell the user and continue with the listed offers. Wait up to wait_s (default 45); pending: true means the shop is still answering, so re-read the quote shortly. Nothing else on the quote changes. On an instant-only quote (routing.instant_only true) no shop is asked; relay that result and quote again without instant_only if the user wants to order. On a lazy quote (routing.lazy true) this call is how a shop is asked at all: it asks this offer's shop, and the offer can be ordered once it passes. A shop's confirmation of an offer is good for 15 minutes: while it stands the offer carries confirmed_until (an ISO time) and can be ordered. After it the offer is NOT failed and NOT removed — it keeps its place and the price the shop last confirmed, and its manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "confirmation_lapsed". CHOOSING STARTS THAT SHOP'S CHECK: when the user settles on an option and you store the pick, that one shop is asked again by itself (the answer's selection_match.check reads "running"), and create_checkout and checkout_cart ask it themselves too when it still needs confirming — nobody else is asked, and no separate check_offer call is needed. Pay when it lands: the checkout waits for it. If the shop's price came back higher than the user agreed to, the checkout stops ONCE (price_went_up, with the old and the new figure) and nothing is created: tell the user both figures, then send the same call again. An offer whose manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "network_restarted" was being confirmed by its shop when the network restarted, so the answer never came: tell the user, in these words, "A new version of AFN has been released, please refresh the page". Nothing is lost — the price stands and the offer can simply be checked again with check_offer. Say it once, when a tool's own text tells you to; the same reason still on an offer on a later read is history, not news.

tools.name: scan_website
tools.description: Scan a public website and report how ready it is for AI agents and AI search: which checks pass, which are missing, and what each check is, in plain English and technically. Covers 35 checks in three groups: agent readiness (robots.txt and AI crawler rules, sitemap, Link headers, DNS-AID, markdown for agents, Content Signals, API catalog, OAuth discovery, auth.md, MCP server card, A2A agent card, agent skills, WebMCP, ARD), agentic commerce (x402, MPP, UCP, ACP, AP2; scored only for sites that sell online), and AI search foundations (HTTPS, AI crawler access, indexability, content without JavaScript, heading structure, title and description, canonical URL, structured data, business identity markup, language, response time). Use when someone asks whether their website is ready for AI agents, AI search, ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Muse or agentic commerce. A scan takes 5 to 30 seconds.

tools.name: explain_check
tools.description: Explain one agent-readiness check in depth: what it is, why it matters for AI agents and AI search, exactly how the scanner tests it, what counts as a pass, and the official sources. Call with no check_id to list every check.

tools.name: search_merchants
tools.description: Search OP-verified merchants by rail, chain, category, agent-callable tier, trust tier, and free text. Ranked by trust tier then verification recency.

tools.name: get_merchant
tools.description: Get the full record for one merchant including all rails, payment endpoints, and OP attestation. Tier 2+ requires an AT credential.

tools.name: verify_payment_endpoint
tools.description: Run a live check against a merchant's declared payment endpoint for a rail. Returns health, detail, and rail-specific evidence.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List the category taxonomy with merchant counts.

tools.name: list_rails
tools.description: List supported payment rails and their current merchant counts.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Report the resolved credential state and rate limits for the calling agent.

tools.name: drug_price
tools.description: Looks up what US pharmacies actually pay to acquire a drug (the CMS NADAC benchmark, per unit, with its date; for a pen, syringe, autoinjector or cartridge priced per mL whose description states what one holds, nadac.per_container gives the price of one, with container, ml and usd, as candidates and biosimilars do; box sizes are not in the data, so no fill estimate follows), a fair cash-price estimate range, FDA generic equivalents, and Medicare negotiated prices where they apply (medicare_negotiated_prices: one entry per year, including a year CMS has announced, with effective_date, price_30d for a 30-day equivalent supply, and per_unit where the NDCs share one). The input is a drug name with optional strength and form. result_type is one of three values. match: one drug, with prices, provenance and honesty notes; a brand-name drug with no generic alternatives listed also carries generic_equivalence, a dated statement of what the FDA Orange Book shows for it, with its ingredient where the file names one (status no_orange_book_match means our match did not pair the product with a listing, which says nothing either way about generics). A brand-name match can also carry cms_generic_price, CMS's NADAC figure for the corresponding generic drug, with its effective date, a fair cash estimate where a fill quantity applies, and the generic's name when exactly one generic in the index has that price, strength and ingredient. A biologic that the FDA Purple Book lists biosimilars to also carries biosimilars (each with proprietary and proper names, interchangeable, marketing_status, file_month, and a NADAC price where one is indexed) and biosimilars_statement; a biosimilar carries reference_product, with the same kinds of fields and a statement. candidates: the query fits several drugs. Up to 12 are listed, each with its description and price hint, in this order: the drug named on its own first, then combinations with other drugs, then longer names that hold the word (esomeprazole for omeprazole); generics before brands, then alphabetical with doses in number order (2.5 mg before 10 mg), within each. A number in the query matches only that whole number, so a query for 5 mg does not list 2.5 mg or 15 mg; within each group, drugs that hold every query word whole come first. candidates_total gives how many drugs matched; when that is more than 12, message says the list was cut, and adding a strength or form narrows it. A query equal to one candidate's description returns that drug as a match. no_match: the index has no drug matching the query; this does not mean the drug lacks a fair price, since NADAC covers only drugs with enough pharmacy survey data. did_you_mean, where present, lists drug names to search next, and did_you_mean_basis gives the reason: spelling (the name the query spells, apart from spaces and punctuation, without a dose the index lacks, or names beginning with it; a number typed with no unit is part of the name unless the words before it are a drug name, so vanacof 2 does not get vanacof dm, and stays part of it, whatever the basis, where catalog names put a number of their own after those words or an FDA label name holds it, so vagistat 3, a miconazole kit, does not get tioconazole of VAGISTAT-1, nor sore throat 911, a potassium lotion, the phenol SORE THROAT; for a trade name that is its only active ingredient plus more words, such as theophylline-sr, that ingredient), same_ingredient (the index has no drug under the ingredient name in the query, and the names are priced brands whose only active ingredient in the FDA Orange Book is that ingredient, or, for a biologic, priced brands whose proper (ingredient) name in the FDA Purple Book is that name, such as trulicity for dulaglutide; message adds a sentence naming the catalog and its file; store brands of the ingredient may still be priced under their own names) or generic_name (the index has no drug under the brand name in the query; the one name is that brand's active ingredient, or its ingredients joined by "and", in the FDA Orange Book, such as tamsulosin hydrochloride for flomax, and searching it lists the priced products with it; message adds a sentence naming the file; the name is an ingredient, not a statement that any product is a substitute; a pack name a maker's label gives a brand counts as that brand, so z-pak, Pfizer's pack of Zithromax 250 mg tablets, gets azithromycin; a name current FDA labels use for other drugs gets none, so midol, ibuprofen in the Orange Book but acetaminophen, caffeine and pyrilamine on its label, gets no hint, nor does allay, a discontinued hydrocodone combination whose only current label is a sunscreen; and leading words of a trade name that begin a priced name of another drug get none, so 8 hour, of the discontinued aspirin 8-HOUR BAYER, is not aspirin, since the index prices 8 HOUR ACETAMINOPHEN ER; and leading words that are no name of a drug get none: three letters or fewer, such as cap of CAP-PROFEN (epi, short for epinephrine, aside), and everyday words such as extended or junior, of EXTENDED PHENYTOIN SODIUM and JUNIOR STRENGTH ADVIL). A query that finds nothing as typed is read again: with a hyphen between a number and a word as a space, so 8-hour finds what 8 hour finds; with a bracketed part's brackets dropped, then with the part left out, such as eliquis for "eliquis (apixaban)"; and as a label writes a drug name, so a salt finds NADAC's short form or a description without it (sertraline hydrochloride finds SERTRALINE HCL) and amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium finds AMOX-CLAV. A name the FDA Orange Book or Purple Book lists that no description holds as whole words beginning its first or second word finds nothing, so ranexa gets its ingredient rather than TRANEXAMIC ACID. No name is guessed from a misspelling: did_you_mean holds no name with letters the query lacks or changes (lipiter gets none), since a real name a letter or two from another is often a different drug (afrin is not errin). A spelling hint is a search aid, not an equivalent medicine. Every result also carries freshness, one entry per source (nadac, orangebook, mfp, purplebook) giving as_of, the publisher's date on the file in use (for purplebook, which FDA dates by month, the first day of that month); checked, the date of our newest successful fetch of that source; expected, the publishing cadence (weekly, monthly or irregular); and stale, which is true when the NADAC file is more than 10 days old, the Orange Book file more than 45 days old or the month of the Purple Book file ended more than 60 days ago, or when our newest attempt to fetch that source failed (last_attempt_failed then gives that attempt's date, and the file in use is the newest good one we hold), and then statement says so in plain words. For mfp, whose updates are irregular, stale is true only after a failed fetch. A source we have not fetched yet has no as_of or checked.

tools.name: law_for_location
tools.description: Resolve an address or lat/lon to its full jurisdiction stack: federal, state, county, place, each with its code sources (name, publisher, official URL, current-through, whether we host its text). Unincorporated areas get the county code with no city code; about half of US municipalities publish no code online, and the answer says so and points at where the code lives if anywhere.

tools.name: law_search
tools.description: Search original law by topic, question, or citation. Exact citations resolve directly. Scoped by jurisdiction or source ids (e.g. us, us-tx; us-cfr scopes to the CFR alone, us covers both the US Code and the CFR) or by an address (the address is resolved first, then the search covers exactly its stack's hosted sources). Results are verbatim snippets with citation, official source URL, retrieval time, and a current-through or vintage label adjacent to every snippet; a hit whose source has fallen behind its upstream carries stale:true. Vintage-labeled text is a dated snapshot, not current law. meaning_only:true means no section matched a word of the query, so every hit is only the nearest in meaning and may be unrelated. Requested ids we do not host are named in the response note; law_coverage lists what is hosted.

tools.name: law_get_section
tools.description: Fetch full verbatim text by id or citation, or pass references for a batch of up to 10. Each batch item has its own result/error. Includes provenance (official source URL, current-through or vintage label, retrieval time), parent path, and prev/next siblings. The text is reproduced exactly as published by the official source; nothing is added or removed except publisher editorial matter, which we never carry.

tools.name: law_coverage
tools.description: Per-source coverage: what we host, section counts, current-through or vintage, last_verified, and a stale flag for any source the recurring verify has proven behind its upstream. Machine-generated from the build manifest; never hand-typed. Absence from this list means we do not host that jurisdiction's text, not that no law exists there.

tools.name: environment_near
tools.description: Environmental records within a radius of a US location, from GroundTruth's monthly snapshot of three EPA datasets: National Priorities List (Superfund) sites, facilities from the newest Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) reporting year, and active facilities with a current significant-noncompliance or high-priority-violation flag in EPA ECHO. Each record carries its distance, and provenance gives each dataset's source and snapshot date (as_of). A Superfund distance runs to the nearer of the area EPA maps for the site (distance_to: epa_site_boundary, 0 with inside_site_boundary true inside it) and the one point EPA lists for the site (distance_to: epa_listed_point); each record gives both. Where EPA maps no area, a site that stretches out (a canal, a river, an underground plume) can reach closer than its point. Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates. Results are records, not a safety assessment. An empty list means the snapshot holds no such record within the radius. EPA holds other records this tool does not search (Superfund sites not on the NPL, earlier TRI years, facilities without a current noncompliance flag), and an empty result does not mean the area is free of contamination.

tools.name: drinking_water
tools.description: Public water systems for a US location, from EPA's quarterly drinking-water data (SDWA; GroundTruth checks for a new quarter monthly), with health-based violation summaries, counts of missed or late required tests (monitoring and reporting violations), and each system's latest lead 90th percentile. Input is a street address or lat/lon coordinates (the US Census geocoder gives the county and place, and the point is checked against EPA's Community Water System Service Area Boundaries; a point outside every boundary returns no systems and a message that the home may use a private well or the map may miss its system), or a two-letter state with an optional county and/or city. Each system carries match_basis: service_area_boundary, zip, city, county or state. Some of EPA's boundaries come from states and water systems and the rest are modeled by EPA, so matching is approximate; the user's water bill names their actual utility. Systems are listed by population served, and the order does not say which system serves a given home.

tools.name: location_scores
tools.description: Layer scores for a US location: school quality, natural hazards, groundwater contamination, Superfund proximity, air quality, highway noise, walkability, crime, and climate pleasantness (pleasant days/year). Scores are 0-1 with 1.0 = favorable; null = cannot score that layer here. The scores are model estimates drawn from public datasets, not safety ratings. no_coverage marks a layer that is null because this location lies outside that layer's data, and caveats.<layer> says why. When a layer's number has limits the score alone does not show (a proxy, partial source data), caveats.<layer> states them. Superfund proximity weighs each cleanup site by the nearer of the area EPA maps for it and the one point EPA lists for it; where EPA maps no area, a site that stretches out (a canal, a plume) can be closer than the score reflects. The scores are not a safety assessment, and an absence of adverse signals is not a clean bill of health. Coverage: Superfund/toxic-release proximity national; air quality, groundwater, and natural hazards a San Francisco Bay Area grid (lat 37.0 to 38.6, lon -122.8 to -121.4, which also takes in Sacramento), null elsewhere; highway noise Bay Area; walkability California; schools all 50 states and DC (2023-2025 results); climate CONUS (gridMET 4km, 2015-2024); Alaska, the Florida Keys, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands (Daymet V4, 2011-2020); within 40 km of 3 NOAA weather stations in American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam (2016-2025); null elsewhere; crime police incident feeds inside the city limits of San Francisco; Oakland; Chicago; New York City; Los Angeles; Dallas; Washington, DC; and Kansas City, Missouri only. School scores draw on the Stanford Education Data Archive (SEDA), whose terms require naming it as the source: Reardon, S. F., Ho, A. D., Shear, B. R., Fahle, E. M., Kalogrides, D., Saliba, J. (2024). Stanford Education Data Archive (Version 5.0). [https://purl.stanford.edu/cs829jn7849] [https://doi.org/10.25740/cs829jn7849] (also in citations.school_quality). Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates.

tools.name: broadband_availability
tools.description: Fixed broadband availability for a US location from the FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC), counted per 2020 Census block: each provider and technology the FCC data lists in the block, with advertised maximum download and upload tiers in Mbps and how many of the block's locations each covers (residential and business-only counts). FCC data as of 2026-06-30 (release J26_10nov2026). Wired and fixed wireless service comes first; satellite service is listed last, in its own section. Where a point is in no Census block with FCC data, counts are for the surrounding H3 cell. A block where the FCC records no locations (often a park, a plaza or a street) lists no providers; the building's own address finds the block it sits in. Speeds are advertised maximums reported by providers, not measured speeds. The FCC data has no street addresses, so it cannot confirm service at one house. Input is either a street address (geocoded by the US Census geocoder) or lat/lon coordinates.

tools.name: check_assessment
tools.description: Fairness check for one Maryland property assessment against genuinely similar homes (same triennial reassessment group, similar size, lot and age, same zip), from a copy of the state's own assessment roll (SDAT) refreshed monthly. Input is a Maryland street address with its zip, its Maryland city or county, or MD, or an SDAT account id (acct); the city, county, state and zip can be written in the address itself (1 STATE CIR, ANNAPOLIS, MD 21401), a city or county narrows the match to that place the way a zip does, and MD alone matches the street across the whole state. A single match returns the parcel record, a uniformity object, a plain-language verdict, Maryland's appeal windows with official filing links, and honesty notes. In the parcel record, market_value is the full value an appeal argues about; taxable_now is the phased-in assessment for the Maryland tax year holding today (tax years run July 1 to June 30; taxable_now_tax_year gives its from and to dates, YYYY-MM-DD), and taxable_next with taxable_next_tax_year is the one for the tax year after; either pair is left out when the roll does not hold that year. The uniformity object gives BandSize (how many similar homes), where the assessment sits among them as percentiles (PctFMV for market value, PctImprPSF for improvement value per square foot, PctLand for land value), their medians (MedianFMV, MedianImprPSF, MedianLand), the median sales ratio of assessment to sale price (MedianSalesRatio) and its coefficient of dispersion (COD) over RatioSales sales dated RatioFromYear through RatioToYear (three calendar years ending with the year of the roll's newest sale dated on or before today), and Branch. RatioSales counts sales of $100,000 or more that the roll codes as arm's-length sales of one improved parcel; foreclosures, gifts, auctions, sales of several parcels for one price and sales of a vacant lot are left out. When the roll records no lot size or no year built for the home, the band skips that test: NotCompared names it (lot size or year built; both as lot size, year built) and the plain verdict's not_compared field says so in words. NotCompared is absent when every test ran. When the assessment sits high (PctFMV 75 or more) or low (below 25) and the home's rank on total value per square foot sits 3 or more in 10 from its rank on total value, the plain verdict's size field says so: total value is the rate per square foot times living area, so the difference comes from the home's size. Verdict branches: fair means the assessment is below the 75th percentile of similar homes (the plain headline calls it on the low side below the 25th and lower than almost all of them below the 10th, and the normal range otherwise); review means it is on the high side; elevated means it is higher than almost all of them; insufficient means fewer than 25 similar homes exist for a fair comparison, which is no finding either way. On the insufficient branch the percentile and median fields are 0, meaning not computed. A single-match or multiple_matches result also carries a roll object: as_of is the date the state last updated the roll and pulled is the date this copy was taken (both YYYY-MM-DD), overdue is true when this copy is more than 35 days old, and a field the server does not know is left out. MedianSalesRatio and COD are 0 when RatioSales is below 10, meaning no ratio is published. When several parcels share the address, the result is multiple_matches, listing parcels with their account ids; passing one of those ids as acct selects that parcel. The list is in unit order, each option carries unit (the unit as the roll writes it, such as UNIT 204) when the roll records one, and total gives how many parcels share the address; when more than 10 do (a condominium building, for instance), the list holds the first 10. A unit written after the street (100 HARBORVIEW DR UNIT 204, 100 HARBORVIEW DR #204, or as its own comma-separated part) narrows the match to that unit when the roll records units at the address, and a single match then carries parcel.unit; when the roll records units there and none is the unit written, the result is an error naming that unit, with no match list; a unit at an address where the roll records none is not applied. Every refusal and every miss below is a tool error: isError is true and the text content is the error message, with no verdict and no match list. When nothing matches, the result is an error; the roll writes addresses in its own form (e.g. 1 STATE CIR), so a miss can mean a different spelling, a town other than the one the roll records, or a zip other than the one the roll records, rather than a missing parcel. A zip is 5 digits; a ZIP+4 (21202-1234) is read as its first five digits, and a zip in the zip input takes precedence over one written in the address. A malformed zip or acct returns an error naming the expected form, a zip outside Maryland returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered, an address naming another state or territory returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered and naming that state as not covered yet, an address with no Maryland zip, city, county or state returns an error stating that only Maryland is covered and that a zip, city or county is needed, and an acct the roll does not hold returns an error stating that no parcel has that account id; none of these carries a verdict or a match list. Without a Maryland zip or MD, an address also gets the error asking for a zip, city or county when a comma-separated part after the street is not read as a Maryland place, a state, a zip, a unit or the US, such as a town Maryland lacks, another country or a state written as Miss. (100 MAIN ST, DOVER, KENT or 100 MAIN ST, LAUREL, MISS.), or when its county is written only as <name> Co with no other Maryland place (1 MAIN ST, HOWARD CO). The check is a fairness snapshot of the public record, not an appraisal, and not legal advice; the official SDAT record is authoritative.

tools.name: check_contractor
tools.description: Looks up a contractor's public credential in indexed state and local licensing records. Licenses, registrations and bond records mean different things. Each record carries a credential object (kind, label, note): kind is license, registration, business_license or bond when the source makes that clear; otherwise it is the generic "credential", and the note says what to verify with the issuing agency. The set of covered jurisdictions changes as sources are added, so this description does not list it. Inputs: a record number (license) or business name, with optional jurisdiction and exact listed city, or an entity_id from an earlier result, which selects that one record. Results: match (the credential record with its status and provenance); candidates (several records fit; each page holds up to 20 rows, total_candidates is the full count, offset pages through the rest, and entity_id selects one; a field with the same value on every row of a page is given once, in same_for_all_rows, and each row's entity block omits what the row already states); no_match_in_index (the index holds no record for that input, which does not mean the contractor is unlicensed; for a search across all jurisdictions, the message states how many covered jurisdictions were searched); or jurisdiction_not_covered (the requested jurisdiction is outside the index, with an official pointer URL where one is on file; the response message states exactly what the link is, or that none is on file, and for some jurisdictions the link is a consumer-protection or licensing-board page, not a license lookup). A name or city search sent with no jurisdiction that names a state outside the index ("Smith Plumbing Atlanta GA") answers candidates carrying not_covered (that state's not-covered answer, which also opens the message) when covered records fit the rest, and jurisdiction_not_covered when none do; those rows are records from other places. A name ending in a covered state's code that is also a word or short form ("Smith Plumbing Co", "Smith Plumbing LA") is not limited to that state; did_you_mean gives the name and jurisdiction to send for that state's search. A name whose full text matches nothing but whose last words name a city on the records ("Smith Plumbing Los Angeles") answers that name's records in that city, with city_read {city, name}; send the name alone for every city. Each record carries as_of_date: the publisher's own last-updated date where we have read one, else the day of our fetch. The freshness field on a match, and freshness_notes on candidates and on a no-match with a jurisdiction, state when a source's copy is behind its normal update schedule, slow to refresh by design, or still on its first full pass, with a plain note, the dates, and the issuing body's own lookup.

tools.name: check_product
tools.description: Looks up one US packaged food by barcode (UPC/EAN/GTIN), id, or name, and returns what is known about it: lab results by chemical (with kind of evidence, sample counts, median and highest values in ppb, lots, dates and sources), FDA recalls naming its barcode, restricted additives in its ingredients with each jurisdiction's rule, FDA's typical levels for its kind of food, same-brand products that were tested, the chemical families never tested in it, and a front-of-pack photo from Open Food Facts when one passed our checks (show it with its credit and CC BY-SA 3.0 licence). result_type is match (one product), candidates (a name fit several; call again with id), or no_match.

tools.name: chemical_sources
tools.description: For one contaminant (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic-total, arsenic-inorganic, perchlorate, a phthalate such as dehp or dbp, a substitute such as deht, or a bisphenol such as bpa), returns the everyday foods where FDA's Total Diet Study found the highest typical levels (with samples, detections, averages and years), named products with lab results (highest median first), recent FDA recalls naming it, and a note on drinking water where it matters.

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Lines up two to five products (by id) chemical by chemical, using each product's own lab results where they exist and FDA's typical level for its kind of food otherwise (marked as typical), plus restricted additives and recall counts.

tools.name: food_category
tools.description: For a kind of food (a category slug such as milk, rice, baby-infant-foods-beverages, cereal, water), returns FDA's typical levels of metals and perchlorate, whether FDA's foods are a close or rough stand-in, and the products in that category with lab results: the 50 lowest in the most-tested chemical by default (products below the lab's limit first), with tested_total giving the full count. Pass sort to rank by another chemical, order=high for highest first, and all=true for every tested product.

tools.name: additive_status
tools.description: Returns where an additive is allowed, restricted, banned or requires a warning (US FDA, EU, and US states such as California, West Virginia, Texas and Louisiana), each with its law and effective date, plus how many products list it and examples.

tools.name: interpret_test_result
tools.description: Places a person's urine or blood test result among CDC NHANES population percentiles (newest survey cycle loaded), for everyone or one age group, and says in words how high it is. tier.level is below_median, median_to_95th, top_5_percent or far_above (at least twice the 95th percentile; CDC's tables stop at the 95th, so times_95th_percentile gives the multiple); a far_above result carries clear_line, e.g. "This is far above typical. Talk to your clinician soon." ("right away" for blood lead at CDC's 45 ug/dL children's step, or OSHA's 50 for adults). unit_check is set when the value is more than 10 times the highest 95th percentile in CDC's tables, which can mean a unit mix-up (ug/L typed as ug/dL); show it to the person. For blood lead, official_guidance gives CDC's follow-up steps for children (2025) and, for adults (no CDC schedule), what NIOSH lists from agencies and medical groups (2024), each with its source; age 20+ returns only the adult guidance, under 12 only the children's. official_limits includes CDC's 3.5 ug/dL blood lead reference value. context gives cited lines on what the test shows, e.g. urine perchlorate reflects about the last day of food and water. Pass unit as printed on the report: ug/L (same as ng/mL), ug/dL, or ug/g creatinine for creatinine-adjusted urine results (CDC's creatinine tables); ug/L and ug/dL are converted into the table's unit and entered shows what was typed. Context only, not a diagnosis.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the AgentRoam travel-crypto catalog: gift cards (Airbnb, Uber, airlines, 500+ US brands), eSIM data plans (110+ destinations incl. Europe/Global region plans) and mobile top-ups (carriers in 100+ countries). Returns product handles (brandSlug + countryCode) used by the pricing and order tools. Creates no order.

tools.name: get_price
tools.description: Live crypto price for one product/denomination. Payment coins include USDT, USDC, BTC (incl. Lightning), ETH, SOL, DAI, PYUSD, LTC, TRX, TON, DOGE and SUI across many networks; get_payment_methods returns the current set. Creates no order.

tools.name: validate_order
tools.description: Dry-run an order and mint a one-time confirm_token (valid 10 minutes). Returns a human-readable purchase summary for the buyer to approve, plus the one-time token that create_order requires. Creates no order and reserves no funds.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Creates the real order. Requires a confirm_token minted by validate_order. Returns the payment wallet address, exact crypto amount, 30-minute expiry, and an order-status URL. The purchased code/QR is emailed by Cryptorefills to the buyer — it is never returned here.

tools.name: list_esim_plans
tools.description: Live eSIM data plans for a destination (110+ countries, plus "eu" Europe and "ww" Global multi-country plans) with USD prices and crypto amounts. In clients that support widgets, the response also renders an interactive plan picker. Creates no order by itself.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Poll order state (WAITING_FOR_PAYMENT → PARTIAL → COMPLETED, or CANCELED/EXPIRED). Requires the status_token from create_order.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: Browse all available brands/carriers for a country: gift cards (500+ US brands) and mobile top-up carriers (100+ countries). Creates no order.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List a brand's live products/denominations with prices in the chosen coin — including the exact denomination labels the pricing and order tools expect (eSIM destinations are covered by list_esim_plans). Creates no order.

tools.name: get_currencies
tools.description: List all supported payment cryptocurrencies (the response carries the current set).

tools.name: get_payment_methods
tools.description: Full payment matrix: every supported coin × network combination currently available, with the exact network strings orders require. The response includes live totals for coins, networks and combinations.

tools.name: purchase_wizard
tools.description: Stateful text-only purchase flow for clients without widget support. Called repeatedly with the same session_token, one question at a time, until status is "complete"; the first call takes empty arguments. The final "confirm" answer creates a real order.

tools.name: search_listings
tools.description: Full-text search over AgentsIndex's Published tools. Returns compact records (name, slug, tagline, url). Fetch depth with get_listing.

tools.name: get_listing
tools.description: One tool in full, as answer-first markdown: the summary, then every question on the sheet with its answer, the vendor's own words for it and the URL that proves it. Identical to /{slug}.md and to the HTML page.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: AgentsIndex's categories with their live listing counts, 0 for one with none yet.

tools.name: compare_listings
tools.description: Two tools side by side, as markdown: taglines, pricing, API availability, tags — the researched compare facts, honest about unknowns.

tools.name: get_best_of
tools.description: The Published tools in one category, in the order its category page prints (ranked by what we can confirm: a public price, an API and docs, independent sources, stated limits), as a markdown answer sheet. Payment never moves a row.

tools.name: submit_listing
tools.description: Submit a tool to AgentsIndex: the url alone; we write its name and description from its own pages. Requires an existing signed-in account with verified email; send its session Cookie header on the MCP request, or an agent key the account made at https://agentsindex.ai/dashboard/agents as Authorization: Bearer. Identity and email come only from that session or key. Sign in or explicitly create an account at https://agentsindex.ai/login?next=%2Fsubmit and verify its email before retrying. This tool creates no account and sends no verification email. Returns {httpStatus:201, id, slug, status:'Draft'}; research + the quality gate decide publication. Your own (url, session email) replay within 24h returns httpStatus:200. The fit check starts at once and usually answers within a minute: poll GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/submissions/{id} and wait the Retry-After seconds it sends while fit is "checking". fit then reads "accepted" (it goes live, and the account is mailed), "rejected" (mailed with the reason) or "undecided" (a person looks within 2 days). No session: {httpStatus:401, error:'sign_in_required', message, loginUrl}. Unverified session: {httpStatus:403, error:'email_unverified', message, email, remediation}. The owner must prove the site before anything is listed: the account's address, or an address it proved with a code, must be on the submitted website's domain. Otherwise the answer is the pending state {httpStatus:403, error:'domain_unverified', status:'awaiting_owner_proof', listed:false, message, domain, proveWith, ownerUrl, ownerStep, remediation}: nothing is listed or queued. proveWith names who can receive the 6-digit code (any address at the domain; for a GitHub or other shared-host project, its listed addresses or a one-line file). Submitting for someone else? Give the owner ownerUrl (the submit page with the site filled in): they enter the code there and the listing goes in once proven. With a mailbox at the domain yourself: POST /api/domain-proof/start {url, email}, POST /api/domain-proof/verify {proofId, code}, then submit again. Personal mailboxes (gmail, outlook…) never prove a domain. No refusal creates a listing. Validation returns 400; duplicate/claim responses return 409. Read tools remain keyless.

tools.name: send_lead
tools.description: Send a buyer-intent enquiry (lead) to a tool or a whole category on AgentsIndex. Keyless. Requires consent:true, a real name, a permanent (non-disposable) email, a message of at least 20 chars, and a target (listingSlug OR categorySlug). Returns { ok, delivered }. Idempotent by (email, target) within 7 days. Nothing here changes a listing's rank, tier or copy.

tools.name: list_offers
tools.description: What a listing owner can buy on AgentsIndex, with prices in US cents excl. VAT, each offer's term and what it needs. Keyless. Same answer as GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/agent/catalogue. Listing on AgentsIndex is free and never sold: submit_listing.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: A signed price for one offer (from list_offers) on one listing, valid for a short time, and whether the listing can have it now. Only the account that owns the listing gets one: send its session Cookie header, or its agent key as Authorization: Bearer, on the MCP request. Refusals say why and what to do (httpStatus 401 sign_in_required, 403 not_owner with the claim page, 409 not_accepted, already_live, already_bought, category_full). Nothing is reserved or charged.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Turns a quote (from get_quote) into an order, payable for 24 hours. Same account as the quote: its session Cookie header, or its agent key as Authorization: Bearer (order scope). Returns the order with payment.url: POST it without a credential for a 402 card challenge (MPP, method stripe, a Stripe Shared Payment Token), then again with Authorization: Payment. Pass idempotency_key to make a retry return the same order. The price is excl. VAT: EU buyers without a valid EU VAT ID pay 21% VAT on top, and the 402 shows the total. Nothing is charged by this tool.

tools.name: my_listings
tools.description: What the AgentsIndex owner dashboard shows about the listings an account owns: each one's status (`status.kind`: review with the expected date, accepted with `liveOn` and `paid` ('express' | 'featured' | null: the paid way that releases it, Featured including VIP listing), live, refused with the reason, or archived), the listing as it shows, where AI answers named the product or cited its page, and what it can buy here at this site's prices. Only for the account itself: send its session Cookie header, or its agent key with "Read your listings" as Authorization: Bearer. Same answer as GET https://agentsindex.ai/api/owner/listings. Read-only: corrections go through the dashboard's request form.

tools.name: find_workers
tools.description: Find listed AI workers for a job by skill (coding, design, video, writing, data, automation, support, translation, research, brief, other). onlineNow shows who is active this minute. If none are listed, use draft_job anyway; the job queues for the next available worker.

tools.name: list_completed_jobs
tools.description: List public finished results. Each item includes a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account.

tools.name: get_worker
tools.description: Get the public profile of a listed worker. Unlisted workers are not returned.

tools.name: get_result
tools.description: Get a finished public result by job ID. The same link opens at /r/{id} without an account.

tools.name: draft_job
tools.description: Preview a research or brief job before submitting: deliverable, budget, deadline, Done when, and a matched worker if one is listed. Stores a draft only. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged.

tools.name: submit_job
tools.description: Submit a job after review. Pass a draft id from draft_job, or the original job and idempotency key. Use the same idempotency key if you need to retry. The response includes a job ID. For a brief, it also includes a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account. Capability "research" returns cited findings. Capability "brief" returns a plain-language brief of at most 800 words, with sources as links. Nothing is charged from this tool. If payment is required, the response includes an AgentsRank checkout URL for you to approve. Jobs under $100: you pay in full when you hire; funds are held and released to the agent when you accept. Jobs $100+: businesses pay half at hire, half on acceptance.

tools.name: find_agents
tools.description: Find workers that can take a job for a skill right now (coding, design, video, writing, data, automation, support, translation, research, brief, other).

tools.name: list_open_jobs
tools.description: List jobs a worker can take right now. The first page is never empty: if no paid jobs are open, it includes an unpaid practice task you can take after self-register, used to check that your setup works, plus a next step with POST /api/agents/v1/register and https://agentsrank.ai/earn. Each paid item includes the job ID, the plain task, deliverable, deadline, done-when criteria, budget, whether that budget is a real payout or a demo amount, whether an unclaimed agent may take it, and how to take it. Business jobs: Business pays at hire; funds are held and released to you when the work is accepted. Jobs $100 and up: half at hire, half on acceptance. The deadline starts when the business's payment goes through. Private instructions and the requester's identity are never included. Agents can connect with each other in the Hub and post articles or what they are working on. No owner verification is needed to use the Hub; the owner's claim is only needed to be hired or paid.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Get the status of a job you submitted. Use the job ID returned by submit_job.

tools.name: get_job_result
tools.description: Get the result of a job you submitted, once it is done. Brief jobs include a short summary and a result link (/r/{id}) that opens without an account.

tools.name: get_my_results
tools.description: List jobs you submitted, with their status and result links when a public result page exists.

tools.name: accept_business_delivery
tools.description: Accept a submitted business-job result. Funds already collected at hire are held and released to the agent when you accept. For jobs of $100 and up, the second half is charged on acceptance.

tools.name: reject_business_delivery
tools.description: Reject a submitted result with a required reason_code (criteria_not_met, incomplete, wrong_format, quality, late, or other) and a note of 10–2000 characters. Opens a dispute for manual settlement. Does not issue an automatic refund.

tools.name: mark_business_delivery_inconclusive
tools.description: Mark a submitted result inconclusive when you could not verify it in your environment. The agent may redeliver once with a new idempotency key.

tools.name: list_brief_presets
tools.description: List business-job brief presets. Research is the default. Each preset includes its own acceptance checklist. No sign-in required.

tools.name: preview_business_job
tools.description: Preview a business job or optional $50 paid pilot before posting: quote, acceptance checklist, and matching agents. Default engagement is the full job; default brief preset is research. No sign-in required. Nothing is charged and no job is created.

tools.name: post_business_job
tools.description: Post a business job or an optional $50 paid pilot. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until you hire and complete checkout. Default engagement is the full job. Research is the default brief preset. Each preset carries its own acceptance checklist. The first job is charged like any other.

tools.name: hire_again_job
tools.description: Return a new unpaid draft prefilled from an accepted job (same agent, brief, and preset). Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until you confirm and post.

tools.name: hire_full_job
tools.description: After an accepted $50 pilot, create the intended full job with the same agent and start checkout. Sign-in required. Nothing is charged until checkout is completed.

tools.name: respond_to_counter
tools.description: Accept or decline a counter-price the agent owner sent on your offer. Use the offer id from get_job_status.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Full-text search over the official AGILEX product documentation.          Use this first for any question about AGILEX hardware: pinouts, CAN         protocol details, baud rate, firmware upgrade, error codes, LED/beep         meanings, installation, calibration, SDK usage.          Args:             query: Chinese or English keywords. Include the product name                 (piper / pika / nero / ranger / limo / scout / bunker / hunter /                 tracer / umr) plus the concept, e.g. "piper CAN 波特率".             limit: 1-25 results, default 8.             space: optional space slug or name fragment to narrow the search,                 e.g. "agx-chassis-manual-cn-en" or "底盘使用手册".          Returns JSON: {query, count, results:[{doc_id,title,space,url,score,chars,snippet}]}.         ``count`` is the number of results in this reply (0-``limit``). Pages whose         title carries 【未发】/【暂不对外】 are not offered for reading and never         appear here — they are unpublished, not missing.         ``doc_id`` is what ``get_doc`` expects.

tools.name: find_in_doc
tools.description: Locate a passage *inside* one manual, without paging through it.          Use this after ``search_docs`` whenever you need a specific table, command         or error code rather than the whole page — including short documents,         because manuals commonly open with a preamble and page 1 rarely answers a         question. It returns the exact ``offset`` of each match, so one         ``get_doc(doc_id, offset=...)`` lands on the right section.          Prefer this over repeatedly calling ``get_doc`` with increasing offsets.          Args:             doc_id: id from ``search_docs`` (also accepts the page slug).             query: the *concept*, not the product name — e.g. "波特率" or                 "急停 接线". Terms that already appear in this page's title are                 ignored, because ``search_docs`` picked the page by them; passing                 the product name again only adds noise. Generic words that appear                 in nearly every manual are down-weighted, so one distinctive term                 is enough.             limit: 1-10 passages, default 5.          Matching is OR, not AND: a passage is returned when it contains at least         one term with enough weight. Terms that are absent from this page therefore         do **not** force a zero result — check ``missing_terms`` to see which of         your words this page never mentions, and ``matched_terms`` for the ones it         does. A query made only of stop words (or nothing) returns ``count: 0``         with a hint.          Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,query,count,returned,         matched_terms,missing_terms,hits:[{offset,heading,score,matched,excerpt}],         hint}. ``count`` is the total number of matched passages; ``returned`` is         how many are in ``hits`` (capped by ``limit``). ``heading`` is the nearest         heading above the passage; ``offset`` is absolute in the page body.

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Read one documentation page as Markdown.          Call this with a ``doc_id`` returned by ``search_docs`` (or a slug such as         ``ymZimX7JLe``). Manuals are often 20k-60k characters, so this tool         paginates: if the reply has ``truncated: true`` and a ``next_offset``,         call again with that ``offset`` to continue. Do not re-request the same         offset.          Args:             doc_id: id from search_docs (also accepts the page slug).             max_chars: characters per call, default 20000, max 120000.             offset: start position, default 0.          Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,offset,returned,max_chars,         truncated,next_offset,updated_at,content}. Always cite ``url``.         If the page has no body (folder or unwritten page), the reply has         ``empty: true`` and a hint — do not retry with other offsets.
