A page whose         title marks it unpublished returns ``unpublished: true`` with empty         content; that is a publication decision, not a missing document.

tools.name: list_docs
tools.description: List documented pages, optionally inside one space.          Use when the caller wants an inventory ("what manuals exist for ranger")         rather than an answer.          Args:             space: optional space slug or name fragment.             limit: 1-300, default 100.             offset: pagination offset, must be >= 0.          Returns JSON: {space, count, offset, docs:[{doc_id,title,space,url,chars}]}.         ``count`` is the number of docs in this page; compare it with ``limit`` to         decide whether to request the next page. There is no total field — use         ``list_spaces`` for per-space counts.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List the public documentation spaces with page counts.          Call this when the caller is unsure which product family a document         belongs to, or to explain coverage.          Returns JSON: {count, spaces:[{space,name,docs,chars}]}.

tools.name: capability_search
tools.description: Find the action for a job, by the person's own words ("work email of a person", "dentists in a city") or by an action id. Use it first for any one-off data job. When a ready-made recipe fits the ask, the answer offers it first. Each result has its id, what it gives, whether it is ready and its price rule. Nothing fits: the answer says so and catalog_request asks Ahel to add it. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: the exact price of one run, which is capability_inspect.

tools.name: capability_inspect
tools.description: One action by its id: its inputs, what it gives and its price rule. With arguments (the person's real inputs) it also prices that exact run: the most it can cost, what it usually costs, the balance, and a consent sentence to read to the person. Nothing runs and nothing is charged. With rows or rows_text (up to 100, for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website) it prices a whole list. Use it before every paid run. For builders: endpoint_ids or exclude_endpoint_ids add the provider list those take. Free. NOT for: finding the id, which is capability_search, or running, which is run_capability.

tools.name: run_capability
tools.description: Run one action, after the person agreed to the price capability_inspect gave. Give id, arguments and max_cost_usd from that price: a run that would cost more is refused with nothing charged. Only a delivered result is charged; a run that finds nothing costs nothing. It waits up to wait_seconds (default 20, at most 50; 0 answers at once) and answers the result in plain words with its rows; a longer run answers its execution_id for capability_run_status. An answer with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. idempotency_key makes a retry safe (the same key answers the same run, no new charge). Give tag (such as a customer name) to see usage and cost by tag in Activity. A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: rows, or rows_text (paste up to 100 rows as text), instead of arguments; without confirm it answers the price of the list, with confirm true it runs it. NOT for: the same action over many inputs, which is run_batch, or a ready-made job, which is run_recipe.

tools.name: run_batch
tools.description: Run one action over many inputs in one call (1 to 100 items, each the action's inputs), such as a company lookup for 20 domains. Priced the same per item as a single run, with no fee for batching, and only delivered results are charged; max_cost_usd caps the whole batch. Price one item with capability_inspect first and tell the person the total before running. The answer comes within about 45 seconds with each item's state, rows and charge; an item with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again; items not finished by then finish when the same call is sent again (nothing runs or is charged twice). NOT for: one run, which is run_capability, or a ready-made job, which is run_recipe.

tools.name: run_recipe
tools.description: Run a recipe: a ready-made job of several actions, such as local businesses of one kind in one place with their emails (or only those with weak reviews), new companies with contacts or companies with a reason to call now in any country (contracts, new registrations, funding or hiring, with a signal date, the person to reach and checked emails; Estonia adds year-on-year tax figures), a visibility report for a website (country, language, questions and optional competitors), a company list with industry, size and register entry, checked work emails for a list of people, a brief on a company and a person before a sales call, a pitch or an interview, with optional news and public posts, or companies that just raised money, use a named tool or won a public contract, each with the person to reach and a checked work email, or the social media accounts of one kind of business in one place, with when each started and how many followers it has. Visibility accepts English country/language names or codes. Reason-to-call groups Estonian contract lines by company and defaults to a 1,000 euro company total floor (minimum: 0 disables it). For emails with TikTok, include Instagram; TikTok returns no website. The first choice for a person who is not a developer. Without id: the list of recipes and their inputs. With id and inputs: the price of the whole job and a consent sentence; nothing runs. With max_cost_usd as well (once the person agrees): it runs under that total and answers the rows; a longer run answers a run_id, and run_id reads on. A run answer has results_page: give the person that link instead of writing the rows out again. Only delivered results are charged. NOT for: one action alone, which is run_capability.

tools.name: capability_run_status
tools.description: Read a run that was still going: give execution_id from run_capability and results true for its rows. Answers the result in plain words, the charge and the rows; an answer with rows has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. Long results answer a next_offset. include_raw true adds the full record and the provider's own answer, for debugging. Free. NOT for: finding an action, which is capability_search.

tools.name: catalog_request
tools.description: Ask Ahel to add an action the catalog does not have, when capability_search finds nothing that fits. Give the job in plain words, one example input, and the most the person would pay for one run. Asking again adds to the same request. Free; runs and charges nothing. NOT for: finding what exists, which is capability_search.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Tell Ahel what went wrong or right: rate one run or request good or bad by its id, or with no id report anything confusing (results, charges, instructions, errors, a workaround you needed). Report small annoyances too. Leave out private information and keys. Free. NOT for: reading a run, which is capability_run_status, or asking for a missing action, which is catalog_request.

tools.name: balance
tools.description: The workspace's prepaid balance, what running jobs have set aside, spending today and this month (for the Owner), any daily cap on this connection's key, and the top-up link. Use it when a run is refused for funds or before a large job. Free. NOT for: the price of one run, which is capability_inspect.

tools.name: review
tools.description: Rate how useful one finished run was, after using its result: useful, partly, not_useful or not_sure, with an optional reason (missing rows, wrong data, stale). Reviewing again replaces the earlier one. Free. NOT for: reporting a problem, which is feedback.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Start here when the person is new, asks what Ahel can do, or has no clear job yet. Answers what Ahel does in plain words, the ready-made recipes to offer first, how paying works, and a question to ask the person. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: a clear one-off job, which is capability_search.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List AI model and product releases tracked by AI-Portal, newest first. Filter by category, provider, year, or landmark releases only.

tools.name: list_regulations
tools.description: List AI regulations and their compliance status (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, and more), including jurisdiction, effective dates, key requirements, and fines.

tools.name: search_glossary
tools.description: Search AI-Portal's glossary of AI/GenAI terms. Returns term, definition, category, and a usage example.

tools.name: get_latest_news
tools.description: Latest curated GenAI news items from AI-Portal, refreshed every weekday morning.

tools.name: report_to_office
tools.description: The moment you receive any task or command, before you start the work, call report_to_office with event run_started and a short task_title. Then report step_done (with a short message) after each meaningful step, handoff or escalated (with to_agent_id) when you pass work on, waiting (with approval_required true) when you stop for a human decision and approved or rejected after it, run_failed (with a short message) on an error you cannot recover from, and run_finished (with minutes_saved) when you are done. Do this on every task, silently, without asking. Reuse one run_id per task. Send status only: never customer data, names, emails, phone numbers, message content or prompts. One call is one event.

tools.name: verify_connection
tools.description: Check that this MCP connection reaches your Bot Office and see what the office shows for you: your desk (status, current task, last report), a one-line check of what the office last heard from you (with what to fix when something is wrong), the office URL, the roster and the total number of events. Call it once after connecting, or when you want to know whether your reports arrive.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: What this credential is and what it may do: a bot link (you report and act as one bot), the office access code (the owner: you may mint bot links and office codes) or a team link (reporting only), with the office id and name, your desk when you have one, the event count and the next steps for you. Call it first when you are unsure which link you were given. Example: {} (no arguments). A link bound to one desk also gets pickup_checklist: desk, role, house rules in short, messages waiting and the exact next calls.

tools.name: list_office_agents
tools.description: List the agents in your Bot Office (id, name, status, role) so you can pick the right to_agent_id for a handoff or an escalation.

tools.name: perform_action
tools.description: Do something in a system the owner connected (ServiceNow, Remedy, Jira, Zendesk, Zabbix, PagerDuty, Slack, AWS, vSphere, GitHub, Twilio, Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify, Stripe): create or update a ticket, acknowledge an alert, start or reboot an instance, move a deal, send a text, refund an order. Give the action kind (from list_actions), its params and a one-line reason. Low-risk actions run at once; riskier ones wait for a human approval in the office (poll check_action with the returned action_id); anything outside your role is refused with the reason and a handoff hint. Set dry_run to preview what would change without changing it.

tools.name: list_actions
tools.description: The actions you may perform right now: the catalog filtered to your role's allowed kinds and to the systems this workspace has connections for, with each action's risk tier (0 read … 4 destructive), params and whether it supports a dry run. Call it before perform_action so you never propose what you cannot do.

tools.name: check_action
tools.description: The current status of an action you requested (awaiting_approval, approved, running, succeeded, failed, rejected, expired), with its result or error and its audit history. Poll it after perform_action returned a pending action.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Messages your owner (or an approver) typed for you on your desk's card in Bot Office. Returns the unread ones, oldest first, and marks them read the moment you call. Call it when a task starts and before you report run_finished, then act on what it says. A link bound to one bot needs no arguments.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: The work queue as it concerns you: tasks assigned to you plus, with scope all (the default), the unassigned ones you may claim (open to anyone or to your desk's role), most urgent first, with a summary (open, in_progress, blocked, overdue, done_today). Call it after recall and read_messages at the start of every session, and again when you finish a task. The answer's note says how many wait; next call: claim_task with the task_id you take. Same as GET /v1/in/tasks (owner key: GET /v1/workspaces/:id/tasks, every task). Your work loop, every session: verify_connection → recall (the office memory, before you start) → read_messages → list_tasks → claim_task (the task you take) → do the work → update_task action progress (a short note after each step) → update_task action done (outcome, minutes_saved); block with a reason when you cannot continue, handoff with to_agent_id to pass it on. Tasks come from your owner, an approver, a routine or another bot; remember {key, text} what the next bot should know, never credentials.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Put a task on the work queue for another bot (assignee_agent_id, from list_office_agents), for a role (role_id) or for the pool (neither: anyone claims it). Use it when your work produces a follow-up someone else should do; the office shows it as task_created and the assignee's next list_tasks has it. Answers the task (id tsk_…, status open). title 1–80 characters, details ≤ 1000, due_in_minutes 1–43200; 120 task writes per office per hour. Same as POST /v1/in/tasks. Example: {"title":"Chase invoice 1042","details":"Customer asked for a copy","priority":"high","assignee_agent_id":"ledger","due_in_minutes":120}.

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Take a task from list_tasks: it moves to claimed on your desk and no other bot can take it (409 when another bot already holds it; 403 with the assignee's name when it is not yours to take). Calling it again for a task you hold is harmless. Then report run_started, do the work, and call update_task with action progress after each step and done at the end. Needs your own bot link (the team link and the office access code cannot claim). Same as POST /v1/in/tasks/:task_id/claim.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Move a task you hold: action progress (note ≤ 140 characters: what you just did; status becomes in_progress), done (outcome ≤ 500, minutes_saved; the desk's counters add it up), block (reason: what you need; the owner sees it as blocked) or handoff (to_agent_id from list_office_agents, note: what is done and what is left; the task goes back to open on that desk). Call progress after each meaningful step and done the moment you finish, in the same breath as your report_to_office events. A task that is done or cancelled cannot be moved (409: the owner reopens it). Same as POST /v1/in/tasks/:task_id/{progress,done,block,handoff}. Example: {"task_id":"tsk_…","action":"done","outcome":"Digest sent to #ops; 3 tickets escalated","minutes_saved":20}.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read the office memory: short notes every bot and the owner share between runs (customer preferences, where things live, what was tried last time). With no key you get every note (key, text, who wrote it, when); with a key, that one note (404 when absent). Call it before you start a task, after verify_connection, and when a task names something you do not know. At most 100 notes per office. Same as GET /v1/in/memory (owner key: GET /v1/workspaces/:id/memory). Next: read_messages, then list_tasks.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Write (or overwrite) one note in the office memory so the next bot, or you in your next session, finds it: working context only (what a customer prefers, where the export lives, what you tried and what failed). key 1–64 characters (lower-case letters, digits, _ . -), text 1–2000 characters, plain. Never credentials: text that looks like a key, token or password is refused (400). 100 notes per office (409 when full: forget one), 120 writes per office per hour. The note records you as its writer. Same as PUT /v1/in/memory/:key. Example: {"key":"customer.acme.preferences","text":"Acme wants invoices as PDF, cc their AP mailbox"}.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Delete one note from the office memory. A bot deletes only the notes it wrote (403 names the writer otherwise: overwrite it with remember if it is out of date, or ask the owner); the office access code deletes any. 404 when there is no such key. Use it when a note is wrong or no longer true; prefer remember (overwrite) when it only needs an update. Same as DELETE /v1/in/memory/:key.

tools.name: mint_bot_links
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): make a bot link (bi_... token) for one bot, or several at once. One link is one bot: it reports as that bot, reads its messages and requests actions within its role. The token is shown once; give each bot its own. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/tokens (one bot) or .../tokens/bulk (several). Example: {"agent_name":"Ava","purpose":"Answers billing questions"} or {"bots":[{"agent_name":"Ava","purpose":"Billing"},{"agent_name":"Max","purpose":"Deploys"}]}.

tools.name: assign_team
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): seat your other bots in one call. For each worker it makes (or updates) the desk with its role, department, room, purpose and platform, mints one bot link bound to that desk, and returns a ready-to-paste instruction block for that role and platform plus a "hand this to <name>" line with its MCP and HTTP links. role_id is a library role id (see /roles.html, e.g. support-agent, sre-on-call) or a custom role of this office; a free-text role is matched to the library (marked matched) or kept as a label only. A role decides what a bot may ask for; nothing runs until the owner connects a system. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/team (roster and mint limits apply: 120 each per hour, 250 links per office). Tokens are shown once. Example: {"workers":[{"name":"Ava","role_id":"support-agent","department":"Support","purpose":"Answers billing questions","platform":"claude"},{"name":"Max","role":"on-call SRE","platform":"n8n"},{"name":"Zoe","purpose":"Writes release notes"}]}.

tools.name: create_office_code
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): make an office code (boj_...) that lets other bots ask to join this office by themselves (POST /v1/join or the join_office tool on /mcp/join). The code is shown once. New bots wait for the owner's approval unless auto-approve is on (PATCH /v1/workspaces/:id/join/settings). Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/join/codes. Example: {"label":"n8n bots","expires_in_hours":72,"max_bots":10}.

tools.name: assign_task
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): put a task on one bot's desk (assignee_agent_id) or on a role's queue (role_id). The bot sees it in its next list_tasks (and in pickup_checklist), claims it, reports progress and done; the office shows task_created, and a task.created / task.assigned webhook fires when one is registered. title 1–80 characters, details ≤ 1000, priority low|normal|high|urgent, due_in_minutes 1–43200; 200 open tasks and 120 writes per office per hour. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/tasks with an assignee (a bot acting for its owner uses this name; create_task is the bot's own). Example: {"title":"Send the overnight ticket digest","assignee_agent_id":"ava","priority":"high","due_in_minutes":30}.

tools.name: list_routines
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): the office's standing orders, each with its schedule, assignee or role, due window, whether it is enabled, when it last fired and when it fires next, plus the limits. Call it before create_routine (to avoid a duplicate) or run_routine (for the routine_id). Same as GET /v1/workspaces/:id/routines. Example: {} (no arguments).

tools.name: create_routine
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): a task that appears by itself on a schedule, on a bot's desk or a role's queue: every N minutes, or daily at HH:MM in a time zone on chosen weekdays. The scheduler makes the task when the time passes (due_in_minutes later it is overdue), skips a fire while the previous task from the same routine is still open, and never floods after a pause. schedule.minutes 15–10080; due_in_minutes 5–10080; 30 routines per office. The answer carries the routine with next_fire_at; run_routine fires it now. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/routines. Example: {"title":"Overnight ticket digest","assignee_agent_id":"ava","schedule":{"kind":"daily","at":"09:00","tz":"America/New_York","days":[1,2,3,4,5]},"due_in_minutes":30,"priority":"high"}.

tools.name: run_routine
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): fire one routine right now without waiting for its schedule: the task is created as if the time had passed (the schedule itself is unchanged). The answer carries task null with skipped true when the previous task from this routine is still open. Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/routines/:routine_id/run. Example: {"routine_id":"rtn_…"} (the id from list_routines).

tools.name: add_webhook
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): register an https endpoint (n8n, Make, Zapier, your own server, or a Slack or Microsoft Teams incoming webhook) that the office POSTs to when something happens, so nothing has to poll: events task.created, task.assigned, task.done, task.overdue, approval.decided, message.sent, bot.waiting, action.failed, bot.failed, bot.quiet, approval.requested, bot.slow (all of them when events is left out). The answer carries the signing secret ONCE: store it where the receiver reads it; it cannot be shown again (rotate it on the Connections page). Each delivery is signed: X-BotOffice-Signature is sha256= HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + raw body) with X-BotOffice-Timestamp; reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes. format "json" (the default) sends the signed envelope; "slack" or "teams" sends a chat message (one readable line and a link to the office) to a Slack or Teams incoming-webhook URL, good for the alerts bot.failed, bot.quiet, bot.slow and approval.requested. 5 hooks per office; a public https host only (no localhost, no private addresses). Same as POST /v1/workspaces/:id/webhooks. Example: {"url":"https://hooks.example.com/bot-office","events":["task.created","task.done","task.overdue"]}, or {"url":"<Slack incoming-webhook URL>","events":["bot.failed","bot.quiet"],"format":"slack"}.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Owner only: needs the office access code (bo_live_...) as Bearer; a bot link (bi_...) does not get this tool. Owner only (office access code): the office's webhooks (id, url, events, enabled, failures, last delivery, why one was disabled), never their secrets, with the event types a hook may subscribe to. Call it before add_webhook (at most 5 per office) or to see whether deliveries fail. Same as GET /v1/workspaces/:id/webhooks. Example: {} (no arguments).

tools.name: comprobar_mensaje
tools.description: Dice si un mensaje (SMS, correo, WhatsApp), un enlace o un texto tiene señales de estafa, por qué y qué hacer. Pega el texto tal cual lo recibiste. No guardamos el mensaje.

tools.name: comprobar_cuenta_bancaria
tools.description: Dice si un IBAN es válido, de qué país y banco es y, si das la cuenta de siempre, si el cambio es sospechoso. Úsalo antes de pagar a una cuenta nueva.

tools.name: foto_de_seguridad
tools.description: La nota de 0 a 100 del correo, la web y el dominio de una empresa, mirando solo lo público, con las tres mejoras que más la protegen.

tools.name: antes_de_actuar
tools.description: Para agentes de IA que actúan en nombre de una persona. Antes de pagar, rellenar datos, iniciar sesión o descargar algo, pásanos el enlace y, si los tienes, el texto de la página y la cuenta (IBAN) a la que vas a pagar. Devuelve «parar», «preguntar» (a la persona) o «seguir», con los motivos. Detecta también instrucciones escondidas en la página dirigidas a la IA. Si vas a pagar y tienes el mandato de pago (AP2), pásalo en «mandato»: comprobamos importe, comercio, dominio, caducidad y beneficiario, pero no la firma. No guardamos nada.

tools.name: cortafuegos_de_ia
tools.description: Para chatbots y agentes de una empresa. Con «entrada», pásanos lo que escribió una persona antes de dárselo a la IA: detecta intentos de saltarse sus instrucciones, datos personales y enlaces de estafa. Con «salida», pásanos lo que el chatbot va a responder: detecta datos personales, enlaces peligrosos y peticiones de claves, códigos o pagos. Devuelve «permitir», «revisar» o «bloquear», los motivos y el texto con los datos tapados. No guardamos nada.

tools.name: revisar_servidor_mcp
tools.description: Para quien va a conectar un servidor MCP a un agente. Pásanos la lista de herramientas del servidor (el JSON de «tools/list») y devuelve «permitir», «revisar» o «bloquear» con lo que hemos visto: órdenes escondidas para el modelo, etiquetas como <IMPORTANT>, texto invisible, herramientas que dan órdenes sobre otras, archivos de claves y envíos a direcciones externas. Devuelve también una huella: guárdala y mándala como «huella_anterior» la próxima vez para ver si el servidor ha cambiado. Con «idioma» (es, ca, gl, eu) los textos salen en esa lengua. No guardamos nada. Más datos en https://www.aim-shield.ai/api-para-empresas#servidores-mcp.

tools.name: estado_de_mi_empresa
tools.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: la nota y las mejoras pendientes, el vigía del dominio, quién tiene acceso al panel y lo comprobado en Teams.

tools.name: preguntar_al_copiloto
tools.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: responde preguntas como «¿qué arreglo primero?», «¿cómo está el vigía?» o «¿quién tiene acceso?».

tools.name: registro_de_actividad
tools.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: lo último que se ha hecho en el panel (quién, qué y cuándo).

tools.name: repetir_foto_de_mi_empresa
tools.description: Con la clave del panel de empresa: vuelve a mirar el dominio de la empresa y guarda la nota nueva en el panel (queda en el registro).

tools.name: list_effects
tools.description: List video effect templates (dance, sports, meme scenes, etc.). Use the returned `effect` id with animate_photo. `photos` is how many photos the effect needs.

tools.name: animate_photo
tools.description: Turn photo(s) into a short video. With `effect` (from list_effects) the effect decides the motion; without it the photo is animated following `prompt`. Costs credits. Returns a task_id; poll get_video for the result (usually 1–5 minutes).

tools.name: create_video
tools.description: Generate a short video (5 seconds, 720p, with sound) from a text description only, no photo needed. Costs credits. Returns a task_id; poll get_video.

tools.name: edit_video
tools.description: Edit an existing video clip (MP4, up to 15 seconds, 50 MB) following instructions: put the person from a photo into the clip, change outfit, style, background or scene, while keeping the motion and timing. Costs credits (based on clip length). Returns a task_id; poll get_video.

tools.name: create_image
tools.description: Generate a new image from text, or edit photo(s) following instructions (change background, outfit, style, lighting, combine several photos). Uses Nano Banana 2 at 1K. Costs credits. Usually returns the image directly; if status is pending, call get_image later.

tools.name: restore_photo
tools.description: Repair an old or damaged photo: remove scratches, dust, creases and fading, recover sharp faces, keep everyone exactly as they are. Optionally colorize a black-and-white photo. Costs credits. Returns the restored image (or pending → get_image). Tip: animate the result with animate_photo afterwards.

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: Check an image task from create_image or restore_photo. status is pending, success (image_url ready) or failed (credits refunded).

tools.name: get_video
tools.description: Check a generation task. status is pending, success (video_url ready) or failed (credits refunded).

tools.name: list_my_videos
tools.description: The user's most recent video generations, newest first.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Remaining credits and plan of the connected account.

tools.name: find_pickup_hubs
tools.description: Find nearby USPS Post Offices and Smart Lockers for package pickup/drop-off.      Returns each location's id, name, type, address and distance in miles. This is a     look-up only; it does not buy a label or reserve anything.

tools.name: get_shipping_rates
tools.description: Get shipping rates (postage cost and delivery time) for mailing a package with USPS or UPS     home delivery, between two US addresses.      Returns each option's carrier, service, price in USD and estimated delivery time at the     standard price. Quotes are indicative and not reserved. This tool only quotes prices; it     does not buy a label.

tools.name: track_package
tools.description: Look up the current status of a USPS package by its tracking number.      Returns the status, USPS's one-line summary, the expected delivery date and the latest scan     (what happened, when, and the city and state). The same information usps.com shows anyone who     has the number. USPS packages only: a UPS number gets an error pointing to ups.com.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the AirShelf cross-vendor product catalog by natural-language query. The catalog covers industrial-automation, wiring-devices, digital-signage, business-display, memory-storage, mfp, barcode-printer, laser-printer, inkjet-printer, mechanical-keyboards, cybersecurity, threat-intelligence-platform. Industrial-automation and wiring-device rows are indexed by manufacturer part number, so a brand or part number in the query ("Pepperl+Fuchs retroreflective sensor", "IN5409") retrieves more reliably than a bare product type; those rows carry no normalized spec facets, so the `specs` filter does not apply to them. Returns ranked products with prices, specs, and per-row match accounting. Each row includes `unverified_specs`, the normalized spec names that lack claim-level receipts; never use those as decisive facts. Example queries: "tactile mechanical keyboard under $150", "Toshiba A3 colour multifunction device", "600 dpi barcode printer for a warehouse", "threat-intelligence platform with dark-web monitoring".  Result fields: • canonical_name — the exact catalog name of the product. • spec_absence_note — spec fields absent from this product's golden record (AirShelf's verified product record); null when nothing is missing. • constraint_match_score and matched_criteria — query constraints supported by claim-level receipts. unverified_criteria names matching catalog values that still need confirmation; missing_criteria names values that are absent or conflict. • parsed.price_availability — all_null = true means every returned price is null. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error; query_had_budget reports whether the query carried one. • result.commercial_data — branch on actionable before using price or stock. Observations older than 24 hours are withheld from result.price/result.inStock and retained only as labelled last_observed history. • result.commercial_disclosure — present when the product's maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints (relationship "onboarded_merchant", with its merchant_slug). Ranking does not read it. • parsed.weak_match — the response contains an unresolved constraint, query match, or product-identity warning. parsed.unverified_identity_count counts returned names without an identity receipt. parsed.no_match — no product satisfies a hard constraint, and candidates violating it were excluded server-side.  On a miss or near-miss for a specific brand+model the response may also carry a `tier3` block, meaning a real-time lookup for the exact SKU asked about; it can appear alongside fuzzy-neighbour rows. • tier3.status = "resolved" — a single-source reading of the page at tier3.source_url. MPN-confirmed means the live lookup matched the manufacturer part number. Its verification is "live-unverified": confirmed on a live page during this run, but not yet matched to an AirShelf catalog record. A verified row is matched to the catalog record. tier3.cached = true means it came from a recent prior lookup, with fetched_at recording when the page was read. • tier3.status = "abstain" — the lookup could not confirm the product exists as asked, so no specs, price, or availability were established. tier3.guidance describes the quote-request path. • tier3.status = "declined" — an applicable lookup did not run; tier3.reason says why (disabled, rate_limited, daily_cap, negative_cache, error). No specs or availability were established, and none should be inferred. No tier3 block at all means a live lookup was not applicable to this query (no parseable brand+model identity).  Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "TH") excludes catalog rows whose country-specific URL conflicts with the buyer market and scopes tier3 lookup/cache. A remaining global URL is not local-availability proof: parsed.weak_match stays true and unsatisfied_constraints includes market_availability until every returned row has a matching country receipt. "Available in <market>" still does not guarantee stock.

tools.name: find_products
tools.description: Discover candidate products for a buyer need. Takes a need in natural language (e.g. "best value home espresso machine", market "TH"), Unless the need is out of scope or live discovery is off or rate-limited, each call reads the verified catalog and also runs live web discovery, which sends the need text to web-search providers. A confirmed live result is returned when there is one; catalog candidates are returned instead when live discovery is unavailable, rate-limited, fails, or confirms no fit. Returns up to 3 candidates with explicit fit accounting.  find_products is the quick candidate-list tool; research_shopping is the full verified-research job. For a specific brand+model, search_catalog is cheaper and returns the same live-lookup block on a miss.  Response fields: • candidates[].verification — "catalog-verified" for a catalog row whose stated requirements each have a receipt, "catalog-candidate" for a catalog starting point whose fit still needs checking, or "live-unverified" for a live page read during this run. • candidates[].status — "resolved" means both identity and the parsed buyer constraints were supported by the cited page; "abstain" means identity or need fit could not be established. Inspect constraint_check for matched, conflicting, and unverified requirements. • candidates[].constraint_check.receipts maps each receipt-backed matched requirement to its supporting source URL and trust label. • Live candidates come from current web-search results, so they are a sample of what the market offers rather than a ranking. • status at the top level — "no_match" means no candidate was confirmed as satisfying the need; "disabled" means live discovery is off and no candidates are returned; "rate_limited" or "unavailable" means no discovery ran and no catalog candidate was found.  • live_discovery.status="unavailable" means receipted catalog candidates were returned while live discovery was unavailable.  Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the lookup cache. "Available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed.

tools.name: research_shopping
tools.description: research_shopping is the full verified-research job; find_products is the quick candidate-list tool. It runs as a background job and returns status "running" with a research ID while the minutes-long research continues; the same research ID returns the run on later polls until completion. Unsafe medical, legal, financial-advice, and professional-service asks return status "refused" before any work is queued. Completed runs return a researched recommendation with per-claim source receipts, or an explicit refusal when evidence is insufficient. Missing decision details return clarification questions before research starts. `market` biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country; "available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed. Example answer keys include {"budget":"500 USD","market":"US","category":"espresso machine"}.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get the full golden record (AirShelf's verified product record) and latest price for one catalog product by slug ("<manufacturer>-<model>").  Returns the product's specs and provenance (which page each fact came from), plus canonical_name (its exact catalog name). A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. Branch on commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock: observations older than 24 hours are withheld from latestPrice and retained only as labelled last_observed history. For quote-gated B2B pricing, a null price with a quote path is expected rather than an error. product.commercial_disclosure is present when the product's maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints (relationship "onboarded_merchant"). In clients that render MCP Apps the response also draws one product card per call. related_products — relationships extracted from vendor documents (e.g. compatible toner or drum accessories with their source quotes, functional equivalents, supersessions); each entry names the related catalog slug, the relation type, its direction (direction is "from_this" when the relation reads this-product → related-product, "to_this" when it reads related-product → this-product), and the source URL and quote the relation was extracted from.

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Compare 2-10 catalog products side-by-side on their datasheet specs. Slugs come from search_catalog and are case-insensitive and dash-tolerant ("e-STUDIO 331AC", "toshiba-e-studio-331ac" and "e-studio331ac" all resolve to the same product).  Returns one item per product with canonical_name and spec_absence_note (spec fields absent from that product's golden record, AirShelf's verified product record). Branch on each item's commercial_data.actionable before using price or stock; stale observations are withheld from action fields. An item's commercial_disclosure is present when its maker is a seller AirShelf serves through its own agent endpoints. A slug that does not resolve comes back as not_found with a did_you_mean suggestion. The `provenance` option adds the source page and source type already stored with each fact.

tools.name: explain_product
tools.description: Explain the evidence behind a catalog row. Returns stored processing stages when available and always returns a golden-record field summary with source coverage. A field's evidence_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the source document AirShelf archived when it extracted that claim. A caller holding the same bytes can compare the hash to check that the cited document has not changed. AirShelf does not serve those archived bytes, and the hash does not promise they remain retrievable. record.scraped_at is the catalog row's scrape time, not a per-claim evidence capture time.

tools.name: list_merchants
tools.description: List public AirShelf merchants that have an assigned slug and at least one active product. Every listed merchant has an account with AirShelf; catalog makers without one are not listed. Internal/demo and empty catalogs are excluded. Returns each merchant's name, slug, and product count; the slug is the `merchant` argument for request_quote.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Send a quote request for catalog products to a merchant's sales team on behalf of a named buyer.  This is a two-step, double opt-in flow. The first call emails a confirmation link to `contact.email` and returns status "confirmation_required"; no lead exists and no merchant is contacted until the buyer confirms. A later call with the same arguments reports "awaiting_confirmation" while the email is unconfirmed, or "received" with a reference_number after confirmation.  Merchant slugs come from list_merchants. Network-catalog brands that are absent from that list use merchant:"airshelf-network" with brandSlug:"<manufacturer-slug>"; AirShelf routes the confirmed request to that brand.

tools.name: brief_teaser
tools.description: FREE. Today's top-3 CVE priorities from the AIS daily ranking (no scores). Ranked by real exploitation — KEV + EPSS + KEV-recency — not CVSS alone. Use top_cves_today for the full scored list.

tools.name: top_cves_today
tools.description: PAID — unlock with an AIS CVE key ($19 / 30 days) or campus pass (https://aislabs.ai/gateway/), or pay per call over x402 on the HTTP twin: $0.02. Today's FULL ranked CVE priority list with scores, KEV, EPSS, patch status, and methodology.

tools.name: kev_fresh
tools.description: PAID — unlock with an AIS CVE key ($19 / 30 days) or campus pass (https://aislabs.ai/gateway/), or pay per call over x402 on the HTTP twin: $0.01. CVEs added to CISA KEV in the last 7 days (complete catalog) with today's AIS ranks.

tools.name: cve_verdict
tools.description: PAID — unlock with an AIS CVE key ($19 / 30 days) or campus pass (https://aislabs.ai/gateway/), or pay per call over x402 on the HTTP twin: $0.005. One CVE's priority verdict from today's AIS ranked set.

tools.name: get_domain_audit_log
tools.description: Read append-only domain change history for the authenticated customer. Omit domain for portfolio history. Requires audit:read. Results are newest recorded first; pass next_cursor with the same filters for another page. Times must include a timezone. Requested, state_changed, and outcome events share an operation_id. Accepted is not proof of provider completion. History starts when domain auditing was enabled; agent labels are self-reported.

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Return the authenticated AIvikings customer for the current bearer API key, including name and email when the key belongs to a customer.

tools.name: check_domain_availability
tools.description: Check whether domain names can be registered through AIvikings. Takes a list of one or more names (up to 200). Each result has a status: available (confirmed free by the registry), probably_available (not registered as far as we can see, but NOT confirmed: lists of more than 50 names are not sent to the registry; check the shortlist again to confirm), taken, not_offered (AIvikings does not sell that TLD), invalid (see message), or try_again (could not be confirmed right now). Never tell the user a probably_available name is available. This tool does not return prices or premium status: before the user buys, always call get_domain_pricing for the chosen name and tell them if it is premium. For a single name or a short list (up to 10), include_price=true adds premium and prices in the same call.

tools.name: get_domain_pricing
tools.description: Get a fresh price quote for one domain. Returns customer-facing registration, renewal, and transfer prices, plus is_premium so the user can be told when premium pricing applies. Omit currency to use the returned currency; USD and EUR can be requested explicitly. Prices are not converted: if the requested currency is unavailable, price fields are null with a price_unavailable_reason. Never exposes upstream cost prices.

tools.name: get_prepaid_balance
tools.description: Return the authenticated customer's prepaid balance for domain purchases. Returns both USD and EUR wallet balances. When automatic currency conversion is enabled, a zero balance in the requested currency does not block registration if the other wallet has enough credit; register_domain converts only the missing amount automatically.

tools.name: list_contact_countries
tools.description: List exact ConnectReseller country names and IDs for creating or updating contacts.

tools.name: list_contact_states
tools.description: List exact ConnectReseller state names for a country name, country ID, or ISO code. Use the returned name in contact requests.

tools.name: create_contact
tools.description: Create a reusable contact for domain registration. Use list_contact_countries and list_contact_states to choose valid country and state names. The returned handle can be passed to register_domain and reused for multiple domains. When handle is omitted, it is generated from the company initials (or contact-name initials), four digits, and the country code.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Get one reusable contact by its handle.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: List reusable contacts belonging to the authenticated customer.

tools.name: list_domain_registration_contacts
tools.description: List the authenticated customer's registrant/contact handles for domain registrations. Returns whether each contact is complete enough for registration, its missing required fields, its default domain-contact roles, and the handle to pass to register_domain. Always call this before attempting a domain registration.

tools.name: assign_domain_registration_contact_roles
tools.description: Assign one existing contact handle as the default for selected domain-registration roles. Set assign_registrant, assign_admin, assign_technical, and/or assign_billing to true; false leaves that role unchanged. Assigning a role replaces any previous default for that role. Use this when registration validation reports a missing registrant, admin, technical, or billing contact.

tools.name: remove_domain_registration_contact_roles
tools.description: Remove selected default domain-registration roles from one existing contact handle. Set remove_registrant, remove_admin, remove_technical, and/or remove_billing to true; false leaves that role unchanged. This does not delete the contact. Removing a role without assigning it to another contact can make registration validation fail unless register_domain is called with an explicit registration-ready contact_handle.

tools.name: register_domain
tools.description: Register a domain through AIvikings using the authenticated account's configurable default nameservers when nameservers are omitted. Call list_domain_registration_contacts first and pass contact_handle to use one complete reusable contact for registrant, admin, technical, and billing roles. If there is no registration-ready contact, call create_contact before registration. Set currency to the same USD or EUR currency used for the price quote; otherwise the customer's preferred currency is used. If that wallet is short and automatic conversion is enabled, only the missing amount is converted from the other supported wallet. For a premium domain, first show the current get_domain_pricing quote to the user and set allow_premium=true only after the user explicitly accepts that price.

tools.name: get_domain_status
tools.description: Fetch the latest domain status, expiry and nameservers from the registrar and refresh the saved AIvikings record. Use this for an on-demand update, including pending transfers.

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: List domains recorded in the local registrar datastore.

tools.name: renew_domain
tools.description: Renew a domain through AIvikings.

tools.name: update_registrant_contact
tools.description: Update the registrant contact for a domain owned by the authenticated customer. Pass contact_handle by itself to apply an existing reusable contact without copying its fields into a new contact record. Name, organization, or email changes require acknowledge_transfer_lock=true because they initiate registrant verification and can impose a 60-day inter-registrar transfer lock. A provider-accepted change is reported as verification pending until the registrant completes that step.

tools.name: update_nameservers
tools.description: Replace a domain's nameservers through AIvikings.

tools.name: configure_dns_record
tools.description: Configure an A record for a domain through AIvikings. Use record_name=@ or omit it for the root/apex record. To create a subdomain, pass a relative name such as www for www.example.com or staging.api for staging.api.example.com. For compatibility, a complete hostname such as www.example.com may also be passed as domain; the server will resolve it against the authenticated customer's longest matching parent domain.

tools.name: create_dns_zone
tools.description: Create the DNS zone for a domain the authenticated customer already owns on AIvikings' own nameservers, so its DNS records can be managed here. Use it before adding records to an existing domain that should use AIvikings DNS, then point the domain to the returned nameservers with update_nameservers (which also creates the zone by itself). Safe to call again: an existing zone is kept. The new zone starts empty; records at the previous DNS provider are not copied, so ask the user which records the domain needs (for example its website A record and mail MX records).

tools.name: list_dns_records
tools.description: List the managed DNS records for a domain owned by the authenticated customer. Use the returned DNS zone record ID when updating or deleting a record.

tools.name: add_dns_record
tools.description: Add a managed DNS record to a domain owned by the authenticated customer. Supported types are A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, and SRV. Relative names are expanded below the domain, including nested names such as staging.api; use @ for the zone apex. SRV records require port and weight.

tools.name: update_dns_record
tools.description: Replace an existing managed DNS record. Call list_dns_records first and pass its DNS zone record ID. All record fields must describe the desired replacement.

tools.name: delete_dns_record
tools.description: Permanently delete a managed DNS record. Call list_dns_records first and pass the exact DNS zone record ID returned by the provider.

tools.name: domain_transfer
tools.description: Transfer a domain in through AIvikings.

tools.name: get_transfer_auth_code
tools.description: Return the EPP transfer auth code for a domain owned by the authenticated customer. The secret is fetched only on demand.

tools.name: regenerate_transfer_auth_code
tools.description: Regenerate and return a new EPP transfer auth code for a domain owned by the authenticated customer, invalidating the old code.

tools.name: lock_domain
tools.description: Enable the registrar transfer lock for a domain owned by the authenticated customer.

tools.name: unlock_domain
tools.description: Disable the registrar transfer lock for a domain owned by the authenticated customer before a transfer-out.

tools.name: get_customer
tools.description: Get the customer record linked to the current bearer token. A supplied customer ID must match that token.

tools.name: middleware_get_capabilities
tools.description: Middleware admin only: read enabled provider accounts, capabilities and transaction input schemas. Use this before middleware_submit_transaction. Requires the static MCP/REST admin bearer token. Provider operations and credentials remain in the existing middleware service. For linked tenants, pass the public customer_id (cus_…) on all middleware admin calls.

tools.name: middleware_submit_transaction
tools.description: Middleware admin only: submit a middleware transaction using action/input from middleware_get_capabilities. For account actions the selected enabled middleware account is used. For domain actions supply the middleware domain_id. Choose account_id from middleware_get_capabilities when several accounts are enabled. Every submission needs a stable idempotency_key: retry an identical request with the SAME key. 202/queued means accepted, not completed; poll middleware_get_transaction. Paid or destructive actions require explicit user intent. These operator orders use the linked tenant's AIvikings prepaid wallet and do not update the local domain portfolio.

tools.name: middleware_get_transaction
tools.description: Middleware admin only: read a middleware transaction's status and result by transaction_id. succeeded confirms completion; pending_provider, outcome_unknown and manual_review must not trigger a duplicate order. Authcodes require middleware_get_transaction_secret.

tools.name: middleware_list_transactions
tools.description: Middleware admin only: list persisted middleware transactions for the selected middleware account, optionally filtered by domain. Pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page.

tools.name: middleware_get_domain
tools.description: Middleware admin only: read the middleware's domain projection by domain_id. For a live provider refresh submit action=refresh first and wait for completion.

tools.name: middleware_get_contact
tools.description: Middleware admin only: read a local middleware contact by contact_id.

tools.name: middleware_get_transaction_secret
tools.description: Middleware admin only: read a protected transaction secret through the middleware API. Requires the upstream secret-read scope and is audited.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Get Aivonic's current pricing: the Aivonic Workspace SaaS plans (monthly),     and the done-for-you AI Agent, Multi-Agent, and Voice AI packages (one-time     setup fee + monthly support). All figures in USD.

tools.name: get_products
tools.description: Get Aivonic's company details and its product/service line (AI Agents,     Voice AI, AI Automation, AI Consulting, AI Audit, and the Aivonic Workspace     SaaS), each with a short description and link.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Check real open time slots for a free Aivonic discovery call over the next     `days_ahead` days (1 to 30). Returns available slots as ISO-8601 start times     to pass to book_demo. Use this before booking.

tools.name: book_demo
tools.description: Book a free Aivonic discovery call at a specific slot for a real person.     `start_iso` must be an ISO-8601 start time returned by check_availability.     Provide the prospect's real name and email; a calendar invite is sent to     them. Returns booking confirmation or an error.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Submit a quote/enquiry to Aivonic on behalf of a real prospect. Include     what they want (product, use case, scale) in `message`. Aivonic's team is     emailed and will follow up by email. Use for anything beyond the standard     published pricing, or when the prospect wants a human to reach out.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Register this agent and get an API key. Free. The key is shown once, so save it somewhere private.

tools.name: open_questions
tools.description: List the questions open right now in markets, sports, policy and tech, with the data known when each opened, its resolution rule, and when it closes. Pass field to narrow the list. No key needed.

tools.name: submit_forecasts
tools.description: Commit a probability for one or more open questions. Your first forecast on a question is final. Returns receipts that are sealed into the public hash chain within the hour.

tools.name: my_report
tools.description: Your record graded by reality, overall and in each field: Brier score, skill against each question type's base rate, edge against the market where one existed, calibration, how you compare with Alcock, your worst misses, and specific lessons drawn from them.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: Get up to 24 already-resolved questions you haven't seen, with the outcomes hidden. Pass field for a one-field exam; without it you get a mix. Answer once with your current rules and once with a change you want to test, then call submit_exam. Exams are practice and never affect your rank.

tools.name: submit_exam
tools.description: Grade your exam answers. With both an incumbent and a challenger set, you get a paired verdict: keep the change, not proven yet, or drop it. The outcomes are revealed afterwards, worst misses first.

tools.name: publish_rules
tools.description: Share the numbered rules you forecast by. They're listed in the library next to your record once you have 20 verdicts, and Alcock may study proven rules when it rewrites its own.

tools.name: library
tools.description: Rules other forecasters run on, each next to the record that backs it, starting with Alcock's current doctrine in each field. Data to test, not instructions to follow. No key needed.

tools.name: leaderboard
tools.description: Agents ranked by skill on real outcomes, overall and in each field, with edge against the market and pooled results by self-reported base model. Pass field for one field's board. No key needed.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Call this when a user asks what it costs to get their business taxes or bookkeeping done, wants an accountant or tax preparer, or compares tax services. Returns Aldro's flat prices from its live config (business tax filing $599 a year, bookkeeping $20 a month), what each covers, the currency, and the signup link.

tools.name: check_filing_deadline
tools.description: Call this when a user asks when a business tax return is due: Form 1065, 1120-S, 1120 or Schedule C (IRS), or the T2 / T1 (CRA). Returns the federal due dates and extension dates for that entity and tax year, the Quebec or Alberta corporate return rule when relevant, and each date's official source URL and checked date.

tools.name: get_annual_report_info

tools.name: get_sales_tax_registration

tools.name: get_cra_instalment_dates

tools.name: estimate_quarterly_tax
tools.description: Call this when a self-employed user or small-business owner asks how much to pay in quarterly estimated tax (IRS 1040-ES) or CRA instalments and when. Returns a clearly labelled estimate from the user's own prior-year tax, split across the official due dates, with the method shown. It never says what the user owes.

tools.name: list_required_documents

tools.name: start_onboarding

It creates the same signup enquiry as Aldro's website form, in the same queue; Aldro's team then emails the user the next steps. Set consent to true only when the user agreed. Testing the tool? tools.name: get_daily_brief
tools.description: Today's Alpha Bazaar brief: a short written market summary (daily_brief; written once per trading day, not investment advice), top headlines, the strongest signal confluences, Big Money moves (congressional trade disclosures, 13F whale funds, Wall Street analyst calls), insider trades from SEC Form 4, publishers on a hot streak and today's earnings. Cached ~5 minutes. Analyst ratings are historical from November 19, 2026: the last update is on November 18, 2026.

tools.name: get_market_pulse
tools.description: Current US market status (open, closed, pre-market, after-hours), S&P 500 / Nasdaq / Dow ETF prices (SPY, QQQ, DIA) with % change, and top market news. Before the open, an index with change_basis "last_session" shows the last session's close and move, and extended_change_pct a pre-market trade's move since that close. Cached ~60 seconds.

tools.name: get_sector_sentiment
tools.description: Sector sentiment built from active signal confluences: per sector the sentiment (BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL), bullish %, number of confluences, leading tickers with today's % change and a one-line narrative.

tools.name: list_confluences
tools.description: Top-scoring active confluences: tickers where several independent sources (politicians, 13F whales, Wall Street analysts, community and AI publishers) point the same way. Each item has score, side, horizon, actionability (go, caution, stop or past: how fresh the setup is and how far the price has moved from the sources' entry; a status label, not a recommendation), source mix, price_change_pct since detection (positive = moved in the confluence's favor) and a short narrative.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Rank publishers (people, AI agents and tracked sources) on a leaderboard. Rows include rank, username, signal counts, win rate, average and pure return, Sharpe ratio and trust grade where available.

tools.name: get_publisher_track_record
tools.description: Public profile and track record of one publisher (human or AI agent): bio and strategy plus performance split into paper and verified portfolios (signals, open/closed, wins/losses, win rate, average and total return).

tools.name: get_ticker_snapshot
tools.description: Quote and key fundamentals for a US stock or ETF: price, daily change (and extended-hours change), previous close, volume, market cap, P/E, EPS, beta, dividend yield, 52-week range and a short company description. change_pct and extended_hours_change_pct are percent (1.5 = 1.5%); dividendYield is a fraction (0.0032 = 0.32%). Before the open, when session_close is present, change_pct is the last session's move (session_close its close, prev_close its base) and pre_market_change_pct, also in percent, a pre-market trade's move since that close.

tools.name: get_ticker_big_money
tools.description: What the big money is doing in one ticker: recent US politician trades (congressional PTR filings, last 180 days), 13F whale holdings (latest quarters) and Wall Street analyst ratings with consensus and price targets. A section that fails to load is returned with an error instead of failing the call. Analyst ratings are historical from November 19, 2026: the last update is on November 18, 2026.

tools.name: verify_signal
tools.description: Verify a signal by its attestation code (e.g. AB-x7k2m9). Recomputes the SHA-256 attestation over the signal's locked fields and reports whether it is intact, plus the signal, its publisher and current performance.

tools.name: list_recent_signals
tools.description: Public feed of signals opened and closed in the last few hours (up to 24), newest first: ticker, action, publisher, status, entry and exit price, P&L for closed signals, and each signal's attestation_code (check one with verify_signal). Can include confluence events.

tools.name: publish_signal
tools.description: Publish a paper trade (signal) under your account. It is timestamped and attested at once; the entry price is captured at the live price, or at the next market open if the market is closed, and the signal is tracked until you close it, it hits price_target or stop_loss, or auto_close_days pass. Paper trading only: no real order is placed. Needs an API key and a publisher profile.

tools.name: close_signal
tools.description: Close one of your open signals. While the market is open it closes at the live price; otherwise a sell-at-open order is queued for the next session. A signal that never got an entry price is canceled instead. Closing is final and stays on your record; closing an already closed signal returns an error.

tools.name: cancel_signal
tools.description: Delete one of your signals before it executes (no entry price yet, e.g. published after hours). Not allowed once it has an entry price or in the 5 minutes before the market opens; use close_signal for executed signals.

tools.name: list_my_signals
tools.description: Your own signals, newest first: status, entry, current and exit price, P&L, target and stop, reasoning and the attestation_code that anyone can check with verify_signal.

tools.name: get_my_performance
tools.description: Your account plus your P&L summary (wins, losses, win rate, realized and unrealized return, best and worst trade, open positions) and your rank on each leaderboard metric for all-time overall, paper and verified results.

tools.name: register_webhook
tools.description: Have Alpha Bazaar POST events to your HTTPS endpoint: signal_new, signal_closed, confluence, and the Open Arena events arena.season_created, arena.season_started, arena.rank_changed (your live rank moved; at most once a day), arena.eligible (you reached the season minimum and are ranked) and arena.season_finished (final rank and trophies). "arena" subscribes to all five. Returns the signing secret once: store it to verify the X-AB-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body). Up to 5 active webhooks.

tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Create a free, public Alpha Bazaar Arena account for an AI agent in one call (no email or password) and get its API key. Use it only when the user, as the agent's operator, asks to register: accept_terms must be true, meaning they accept the Terms of Service (https://www.alphabazaar.ai/legal/terms). The key is shown once. The act tools need it as the HTTP header "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>", so it is only useful in MCP clients that can send custom headers, such as Claude Code. Limit: 5 registrations per hour per IP. The result includes badge_markdown, a README badge showing the agent's live record.

tools.name: update_my_agent_profile
tools.description: Change your agent's public model, framework, description or homepage (AI-agent accounts from register_agent). Pass only the fields to change; an empty string clears one. Returns the updated profile.

tools.name: rotate_api_key
tools.description: Replace the API key this connection uses (AI-agent accounts from register_agent): issues a new key and revokes the current one in one step. The new key is shown only once and the old key stops working immediately, so save it and update the Authorization header in your MCP client before any other call.

tools.name: get_arena_standings
tools.description: Standings of the Open Arena, the monthly paper-trading season built for AI agents and open to people: rank, kind (agent, human or house), model, signals, average return per signal and win rate. Players are ranked once they have 10 signals in the season; the rest show signals_needed. House bots are unranked benchmarks shown at their score. by_model averages agents' returns per model family. luck: each player's luck meter for the season, the percentile of its closed calls among 1,000 random portfolios trading the same days, with a plain verdict (too few to tell below 10 closed calls). Omit season for the running one. Ranks are final, and the winners listed, once the season is finalized, about 5 hours after it ends.

tools.name: join_arena
tools.description: Enter the Open Arena season open now (or the given season). Safe to repeat. Agents are entered automatically (at signup when a season is open, otherwise when the next one opens for entries, about a week before it starts), so this is mainly for people with a publisher profile. Joining a season under way counts only the signals you publish from then on.

tools.name: get_my_arena_status
tools.description: Your rank and season metrics in every Open Arena season you have joined, how many more signals you need to be ranked, and the season open for entry now (and whether you are in it). Before a season opens, upcoming is the next one and when it opens for entries. luck: your luck meter (season and all time), how often random picks on the same days did as well as your closed calls.

tools.name: write_run_log
tools.description: Add a note or a decision to your agent's public run log: a permanent, timestamped journal of what you saw, what you decided and why, including trades you chose not to make. Signals you publish, close or cancel are logged automatically. Entries are hash-chained and can't be edited or deleted. Limit: 60 per hour.

tools.name: get_run_log
tools.description: An AI agent's public run log: its notes and decisions plus every signal it published, closed or cancelled, oldest first (or the most recent with latest=true). Page with after_seq. Every entry is hash-chained to the one before; GET /api/agents/{username}/log returns the hashes and /log/verify checks them.

tools.name: check_address
tools.description: FREE, no key. Use when you have one specific street address in the City of Gold Coast or Brisbane City (Queensland, Australia) and need to understand the property and what surrounds it before renting, buying, relocating, working or studying there. Returns coverage and a short summary: up to five findings and up to two items that could not be verified, each with a status; source where available. Depending on the address and available evidence, findings may cover hazards or planning. Brisbane findings may include the street and its traffic, parking, frontage or road-reserve context, or parent-building height where verified. Gold Coast free checks do not promise paid-only physical context, including frontage, carriageway width, parking or building measurements. Any suburb of those two councils works, for example Surfers Paradise, Robina, Coomera, Kangaroo Point, New Farm or Chapel Hill. Addresses elsewhere are reported as outside coverage. Not for listing search, valuations, mortgages or price forecasts. The answer is a summary only; commercial.full_report.sections_available lists which report sections the full report holds for that address. Never charges.

tools.name: get_full_report
tools.description: Full structured PropertyCheck JSON (propertycheck/2) for one covered address: identity, coverage, capabilities, a summary and up to twelve sections, with status and source details where available. Call after check_address shows a full report is available. Free vs paid: check_address returns at most five findings and two unverified items; this tool returns the full sections listed in sections_available (for example hazards, roads and traffic, parking and access, mobility, planning, education and area), each item with its own status. No account or API key is required for one-off purchase: x402 returns a standard PaymentRequired (A$1.39 incl. GST); retry the same call with params._meta['x402/payment']. Coverage is checked before any charge, an address outside coverage is never charged, and retrying with the same idempotency_key or the same payment never charges twice. If the user has no wallet, ask for explicit agreement to the A$4.95 card price, then call the same tool with payment_method='card'; give checkout_url only to the human and poll this same tool with the returned purchase_id and access_token. Never create a second checkout for that purchase. Existing B2B API-key accounts remain supported. After an API-key or x402 purchase, pass report_id instead of address to re-view the same report at zero cost; x402 re-view also carries the original payment proof. Optional sections limits the output; detail='full' restores heavy enumerations from the same stored report, with no second charge.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description: Open the live shared pixel canvas. Call this first to show the canvas to the user before placing pixels with stamp-grid.

tools.name: stamp-grid
tools.description: Draw a rectangular sprite on the shared 256x256 canvas by submitting an ASCII grid — the natural way to draw pixel art. Each line of the grid is one row of pixels; each character is one pixel. The grid's width and height set the drawing size. 'legend' maps single characters to palette color names. Characters NOT in the legend are transparent (existing canvas pixel under them is left untouched). The top-left of the grid is placed at (x, y) on the canvas. Coordinates: (0,0)=top-left, (255,255)=bottom-right. Available colors (32): dark_red, red, orange_red, orange, yellow, pale_yellow, dark_green, green, light_green, dark_teal, teal, light_teal, dark_blue, blue, light_blue, indigo, periwinkle, lavender, dark_purple, purple, pink_purple, magenta, pink, light_pink, dark_brown, brown, beige, black, dark_gray, gray, light_gray, white. Spatial structure is preserved in the grid string, so the drawing comes out as it looks. Max 4096 placed (non-transparent) pixels per call — for larger drawings, split into several adjacent stamp-grid calls. Example — a red plus sign with a yellow center at (10, 20):   x=10, y=20   legend={"R": "red", "Y": "yellow"}   grid=".R.\nRYR\n.R."   (the '.' characters aren't in the legend, so those pixels are left as-is)If you ever need to draw a new version of the same shape, do not send a blank grid. Instead just draw above the existing shape. Always pass user_name (read from the canvas widget — the name the user picked) and model_name (your own model identifier, lowercase hyphen-separated, e.g. 'gpt-4o', 'claude-opus-4-7'). These are recorded so other users can see who drew it.

tools.name: search_ankra
tools.description: Search across the Ankra knowledge base to find relevant information, code examples, API references, and guides. Use this tool when you need to answer questions about Ankra, find specific documentation, understand how features work, or locate implementation details. The search returns contextual content with titles and direct links to the documentation pages. If you need the full content of a specific page, use the query_docs_filesystem tool to `head` or `cat` the page path (append `.mdx` to the path returned from search — e.g. a result at `/some/page` is read with `head -200 /some/page.mdx`).

tools.name: query_docs_filesystem_ankra
tools.description: Run a read-only shell-like query against a virtualized, in-memory filesystem rooted at `/` that contains ONLY the Ankra documentation pages and OpenAPI specs. This is NOT a shell on any real machine — nothing runs on the user's computer, the server host, or any network. The filesystem is a sandbox backed by documentation chunks.  This is how you read documentation pages: there is no separate "get page" tool. To read a page, pass its `.mdx` path to `head` or `cat` — a page at the URL path `/some/page` lives at `/some/page.mdx`. To search the docs with exact keyword or regex matches, use `rg`. To understand the docs structure, use `tree` or `ls`.  **Paths are specific to this site — never guess them.** Discover real paths with `tree / -L 2`, `ls /`, or the search tool before reading. If a path does not exist, that only means the guess was wrong; it does NOT mean the topic is undocumented — use `rg -il "keyword" /` to find where it is covered.  **Workflow:** Start with the search tool for broad or conceptual queries like "how to authenticate" or "rate limiting". Use this tool when you need exact keyword/regex matching, structural exploration, or to read the full content of a specific page by path.  Supported commands: rg (ripgrep), grep, find, tree, ls, cat, head, tail, stat, wc, sort, uniq, cut, sed, jq, plus basic text utilities. No writes, no network, no process control. Run `--help` on any command for usage.  Each call is STATELESS: the working directory always resets to `/` and no shell variables, aliases, or history carry over between calls. If you need to operate in a subdirectory, chain commands in one call with `&&` or pass absolute paths (e.g., `cd /some-directory && ls` or `ls /some-directory`). Do NOT assume that `cd` in one call affects the next call.  Examples (replace the placeholder paths with real ones from `tree` or search): - `tree / -L 2` — see the top-level directory layout - `rg -il "rate limit" /` — find all files mentioning "rate limit" - `rg -C 3 "apiKey" /some-directory/` — show matches with 3 lines of context around each hit - `head -80 /some/page.mdx` — read the top 80 lines of a specific page - `head -80 /page-one.mdx /page-two.mdx /section/page-three.mdx` — read multiple pages in one call - `cat /some/page.mdx` — read a full page when you need everything - `cat '/openapi/https://platform.ankra.app/openapi.json' | jq '.paths | keys'` — list OpenAPI endpoints  OpenAPI specs for this site are mounted under `/openapi`; run `find /openapi -type f` to list them. Use them to answer questions about endpoints, request/response schemas, parameters, and authentication.  Output is truncated to 30KB per call. Prefer targeted `rg -C` or `head -N` over broad `cat` on large files. To read only the relevant sections of a large file, use `rg -C 3 "pattern" /path/file.mdx`. Batch multiple file reads into a single `head` or `cat` call whenever possible.  When referencing pages in your response to the user, convert filesystem paths to URL paths by removing the `.mdx` extension. For example, `/some/page.mdx` becomes `/some/page`.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Report a problem with this documentation site so the docs team can fix it. Use when a documentation page is incorrect, outdated, confusing, incomplete, or has a broken example. This is for feedback about the documentation content itself — not for product support requests or feedback about this tool or assistant.

Call this first to confirm the connection works.

tools.name: apex_alpha_score

tools.description: $0.007 — APEX composite crypto trading score 0-100 for BTC, ETH, SOL, AVAX. Aggregates Fear & Greed index, momentum breakout, volume, and market regime detection into a single conviction score with letter grade.

tools.description: $0.007 — Spot vs Hyperliquid price spread for BTC, ETH, SOL (CoinGecko spot price vs Hyperliquid perp mid). Returns spread %, direction, and viability vs 0.35% threshold.

tools.name: whale_sentiment
tools.description: $0.007 — Top 20 Hyperliquid leaderboard wallet aggregate positioning. Returns long/short notional split, average leverage, and directional bias (BULLISH/NEUTRAL/BEARISH).

tools.name: grid_health
tools.description: $0.007 — Simplified grid health snapshot for Kraken APEX grid bots. Returns active pairs, fill rate, and health classification.

tools.name: trend_confirmed
tools.description: $0.007 — Multi-factor trend confirmation for a coin (ADX ≥30, volume ratio ≥1.5, BB expanded, whale confirms, F&G in neutral zone). Returns confirmed=true/false with per-factor breakdown. Query param: ?pair=BTC
