tools.name: verify_agent
tools.description: Check whether an AI agent carries a real, cryptographically signed credential. Accepts an agent name, a credential id (TP-...), an agent UUID, a domain or a DID. Returns one of seven verdicts: VERIFIED, EXPIRED, REVOKED, SUPERSEDED, UNSIGNED, UNCHECKED or NO_RECORD. IMPORTANT for interpreting the answer: VERIFIED means the Ed25519 signature recomputes against the key published at apir.ai and the credential is unexpired and unrevoked. It confirms WHO issued the credential and that its contents are unaltered. It is NOT a guarantee that the agent behaves well. NO_RECORD is an honest, first-class answer: it means nothing is on file, which is not evidence of wrongdoing and not a warning. It means any claim the agent makes about itself is unverified. Free, unauthenticated, and no account is required.

tools.name: check_authority
tools.description: Resolve the human mandate behind an AI agent: which actions a named person actually permitted, any value cap, the expiry, and whether the grant itself is signed. Where authority was delegated agent to agent, the full chain is walked back to the human at the root, and one law is enforced at every hop: authority may only ever narrow. No hop can hold an action, a target or a spending cap wider than the hop above it, and the root must be a human. Use this before letting an agent transact, sign, spend or commit on someone else's behalf. An agent holding a valid credential may still be acting outside its mandate, and those are different questions. The answer is the mandate on file as of checked_at. It is not proof the permission still holds at the moment the action runs: check again at the point of action, and treat a record as proof of what was recorded and when.

tools.name: get_verification_keys
tools.description: Return the Ed25519 public keys APIR publishes, so a signature can be recomputed offline without trusting any APIR response, including this one. Keys are published as a JWKS at apir.ai/.well-known/jwks.json and as did:web:apir.ai. Retired keys stay published so older credentials still verify.

tools.name: keyword_research
tools.description: Keyword metrics and research for App Store / Google Play search terms: popularity (5–100), difficulty (0–100), result count and the #1 result's estimated daily downloads. include adds related terms with metrics, the store's autocomplete and the current top 10 apps; app adds that app's rank and metadata relevance per term (the core of an ASO keyword audit). tools.name: read_connection
tools.description: Read live data from one of the user's connected accounts. what='reviews' (asc, play_console): the app's own reviews with reply status, unanswered=true for those without a developer reply; their review_id feeds propose_action review.reply (Play only returns reviews from the last 7 days). what='listing' (asc, play_console): the current listing text for one locale with lengths and which fields are editable right now (App Store name, subtitle, description, keywords and what's new need a version in Prepare for Submission). what='ads' (apple_ads): view=campaigns → ad_groups (campaign_id) → keywords (campaign_id, ad_group_id) gives the ids the apple_ads.* actions take, view=negatives lists negative keywords, view=report with level=campaigns|adgroups|keywords|searchterms returns impressions, taps, installs, spend, CPT and CPA for start..end (default the last 7 days; granularity=DAILY adds a per-day series, up to 90 days), view=suggestions (app, optional terms and countries) returns Apple's keyword suggestions for a linked app with relative popularity, view=popularity (terms, countries) returns Apple's own search popularity per term for the last finished week. Cost: 1 credits.

tools.name: propose_action
tools.description: Prepare a change to the user's connected account as a DRY RUN: nothing is written. AppGoat reads the live account and returns the before → after diff, guardrail results (AI probabilities for store policy, tone and risky claims, plus checks such as character limits and bid jumps) and an action id. ALWAYS show the diff and any guardrail flags to the user and get their go-ahead before calling apply_action. Types and params (app = a linked App Store id or package name, locale like en-US): review.reply {app, review_id, text} (review ids from read_connection what=reviews; Play replies ≤ 350 chars); listing.update {app, locale, fields: {name|title, subtitle, description, promotional_text, whats_new, marketing_url, support_url, privacy_policy_url}} (Play: title, short_description, full_description, video); keywords.set {app, locale, keywords: [..] or 'a,b,c', mode?: replace|add|remove} (App Store, 100 bytes comma-joined); screenshots.upload {app, locale, display_type: APP_IPHONE_67… (asc) or image_type: phoneScreenshots… (play), images: [{url}], replace?}; apple_ads.keyword.bid {campaign_id, ad_group_id, keywords: [{id, bid?, status?: ENABLED|PAUSED}], max_increase?}; apple_ads.keyword.add {campaign_id, ad_group_id, keywords: [{text, match_type?: EXACT|BROAD, bid?}]}; apple_ads.negative.add {campaign_id, ad_group_id?, keywords: [{text, match_type?}]}; apple_ads.campaign.create {app, name, countries: ['US'], daily_budget, placement?: APPSTORE_SEARCH_RESULTS (default)|APPSTORE_SEARCH_TAB|APPSTORE_TODAY_TAB|APPSTORE_PRODUCT_PAGES, max_daily_budget?} (manual CPT in the ad account currency; always created PAUSED); apple_ads.campaign.update {campaign_id, status?: ENABLED|PAUSED, daily_budget?, countries?, name?}; apple_ads.adgroup.create {campaign_id, name, default_bid, search_match?: false, status?, start_time?}; apple_ads.adgroup.update {campaign_id, ad_group_id, status?, default_bid?, search_match?, name?} (Apple Ads ids from read_connection what=ads). Apple Ads changes that can raise spend (enabling a campaign or ad group, a higher budget or default bid, new countries, Search Match on) are marked 'can raise ad spend': apply them only on the user's explicit go-ahead. Cost: 0 credits.

tools.name: apply_action
tools.description: Go ahead with an action from propose_action, after the user has seen its diff and agreed. Outcomes: applied (written to the store / Apple Ads account, 1 credit; when the org has an auto-apply rule the guardrail score clears, or allows agents to approve); pending_approval (a person must approve it in the AppGoat dashboard: give the user the approve link, nothing is written until then); needs a person (it was already pending and agents may not approve: hand over the link, do not retry); changed (the account changed since the dry run: the new diff is shown; show it to the user and call again with force=true only if they accept it, or propose_action again). Cost: 1 credit when applied, else 0 credits.

tools.name: get_action

tools.description: Check whether a brand, product or company name is available as a trademark. Searches the USPTO register and scores similar marks by conflict risk. Free, no account needed. Signed-in Arcangel users can set full_report for a full clearance search (US + EU/WIPO, dead marks, domains, common-law). Results include a link to file the trademark with Arcangel AI.

tools.name: get_trademark_check
tools.description: Get the result of a trademark check that was still running, or the next part of a long full report. Pass the search_id that check_trademark returned, and part when the report says it continues.

tools.name: suggest_nice_classes
tools.description: Suggest trademark (Nice) classes for a description of goods or services, e.g. "mobile app for booking yoga classes".

tools.name: start_trademark_application
tools.description: Start a US trademark application on Arcangel AI as a draft in the signed-in user's account. Pass what is known (the mark, goods or services, classes, owner); the rest can be added later with update_trademark_application. If a company owns the mark, pass the id of a saved company (list_companies) as company_id. Returns the draft id and what it still needs. Requires Sign in with Arcangel. Signing and payment happen on arcangel.ai.

tools.name: update_trademark_application
tools.description: Fill in or change fields on a trademark application draft (owner, address, mark details, classes, use dates, statements). Only fields passed are changed. Returns what the draft still needs, as text. The Arcangel card already in the chat refreshes itself, so there is no need to call get_trademark_application afterwards. Requires Sign in with Arcangel.

tools.name: get_trademark_application
tools.description: Show what a trademark application draft still needs before it can be signed and paid for: missing fields, files to upload (logo, specimens) with upload links, and the link to finish on arcangel.ai.

tools.name: list_companies
tools.description: List the companies saved in the signed-in Arcangel account, with their ids. Call this before asking for company details on a trademark application: if the owner is already saved, pass its id as company_id to start_trademark_application or update_trademark_application. Requires Sign in with Arcangel.

tools.name: create_company
tools.description: Save a company profile in the signed-in Arcangel account, as on the Companies page, so it can own trademark applications. Every field except address_line2 is required: ask the user for each one, never guess. Returns the new company id; link it to a draft with company_id. Requires Sign in with Arcangel.

tools.name: update_company
tools.description: Change fields on a saved company (id from list_companies). Only the fields passed change. A draft already linked to the company picks up the change when company_id is passed again or the draft is opened on arcangel.ai. Requires Sign in with Arcangel.

tools.name: query_registry
tools.description: Search the Arclan registry for MCP servers. By default returns only connectable servers (active, mcp_partial, auth_gated). Use status=stdio to browse local-only servers available for installation. Use status=all to query the full index. Use production_safe=true to restrict to servers with uptime > 97% and handshake success > 95%. Use read_only=true to restrict to servers with no write or exec tools. Use this before connecting to an MCP server to check its validation status and score. After using a server, call report_server to contribute reliability data.

tools.name: get_server
tools.description: Get full details for a specific MCP server. Pass the server name (e.g. "GitHub", "Brave Search"), registry ID slug, or endpoint URL. Returns score, state, tools list, latency, and recent test history.

tools.name: recommend_server
tools.description: Get ranked MCP server recommendations for a task. Returns servers scored by production safety, keyword relevance, registry score, latency, and freshness. Each result includes a reason code array explaining why it was ranked. Use this instead of query_registry when you want an opinionated ranked list rather than a filtered search.

tools.name: report_server
tools.description: Submit an agent usage report for an MCP server. Reports are aggregated and influence registry trust scores. Call this after using an MCP server so the registry can track real-world reliability. Supports both a simple outcome report and a structured scoring report (criterion + component_score).

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Start GitHub sign-in to get an Arclan API key, without leaving MCP (OAuth device flow). Returns a verification URL and a short user_code — show both to the user and ask them to authorize in a browser. Then call complete_sign_in with the returned device_code to mint the key. A key raises your MCP rate limit above the keyless tier and tracks your usage.

tools.name: complete_sign_in
tools.description: Finish the GitHub sign-in started by sign_in and return a new Arclan API key. Pass the device_code from sign_in. If the user has not authorized in the browser yet, this returns status "pending" — wait poll_interval_seconds and call again. The api_key is shown ONCE; store it and send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

tools.name: before_checkout
tools.description: Call this right before your agent tries to check out at a store, or when a user asks "can my agent check out at <store>?". Not for an attempt that already happened (log it with report_outcome), the reason an agent keeps failing (why_blocked_and_fix), or choosing between 2 or more stores (compare). Returns a one-line answer, reaches_checkout (true only when a checkout link came back or a shopper reached checkout; false when a route was measured and did not reach checkout; null when not shown either way: no agent catalog found and no browser test is null, and so is a product added to the cart with no shopper reaching checkout; null is not a no), protocol_route, browser_route, standard_shoppers when ARC's standard shoppers tried the store (a dated label, "ARC's standard shoppers: N of M reached checkout, <date>": a lower bound, not a verdict; ARC stops before payment and never places an order), best_route (the best saved way in), payment_methods_declared (the payment handler ids the store declares to agents in its own UCP profile, with source "ucp_profile", checked_at and a note; the store's own declaration, not a test of any agent paying there; null with payment_methods_note when ARC has no UCP profile reading, which is not a no), up to 3 blockers, checked_at, the Agent Readiness Grade (grade, with expired when over 30 days old; grade_note when not graded, which is not a mark against the store), alternatives_hint when the grade is D or F or expired (a find_stores call with min_grade B in the same category), and a full_record link (the precheck answer, which also carries product_markup). Example: before_checkout({"url":"https://allbirds.com"}) → {"answer":"A saved check got a checkout link back at allbirds.com via storefront_mcp (6 hours ago).","reaches_checkout":true,…}. The answer leads with the dated fact; once the record is not current it starts "Last known on <date>.". reaches_checkout false or unknown is not a no. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: find_stores
tools.description: Call this when you need to pick a store for a product need and want one where a saved check shows an agent reached checkout. Filters: category or q (shopper words), min_grade (optional, default none), payment_method (optional: a payment handler id such as com.google.pay, or "google pay" or "shop pay"; keeps stores whose saved UCP profile declares it), limit (default 5). Returns total, the store hosts with checked_at and grade, and a full_list link; with payment_method, also payment_method (id, name, declared_by: how many listed stores declare it, and a note: a declaration is the store's own statement, not a test of any agent paying there). Each store carries its Agent Readiness Grade (grade, null when not graded). Stores whose saved checkout evidence is from the last 30 days come first (fresh_success: true), then older evidence. Within each, best current grade first (A, then B…); an expired grade ranks after current ones of the same letter; newest checked_at first within a grade. Results are ordered only by published grade and freshness, never by anything else. Pass min_grade to keep only stores with a current grade of that letter or better. Example: find_stores({"category":"running shoes","limit":3}) → {"total":12,"stores":[{"host":"…","checked_at":"…","grade":{"grade":"A",…}}],…}. Example: "Which stores declare Google Pay to agents?" → find_stores({"payment_method":"google pay"}) → {"payment_method":{"id":"com.google.pay","declared_by":…},"stores":[…],…}. An unknown payment_method is error code unknown_payment_method with handler_ids (the ids ARC has seen); not_available means retry in a minute. A store missing from the list is not a no. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: why_blocked_and_fix
tools.description: Call this after before_checkout says reaches_checkout is false or null, or when an agent got stuck at a store and you want the reason and the fix. Returns why (the saved blockers), fix (the store page's recorded fix, or "not recorded"), next_step and links to the full record. Example: why_blocked_and_fix({"store":"gymshark.com"}) → {"why":["…"],"fix":"…","next_step":"…"}. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: Call this right after your agent tried to check out at a store, to log, record or report what happened: it reached checkout, a captcha stopped it, it got as far as shipping, anything. Use it for any attempt that already happened, so the next agent knows; before_checkout is only for before an attempt. Free, no login. Omit contributor_key and ARC issues one; send it on later reports. No personal data: emails, phones, addresses, card numbers and IPs are rejected or stripped. Example: report_outcome({"store_domain":"allbirds.com","agent_family":"browser","agent_name":"my-agent","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z","furthest_step":"checkout","blocker":"none"}) → {"ok":true,"status":"unverified",…}. A report stays private until 3 independent contributors agree. Same as POST /api/outcomes and report_checkout on /api/mcp. checked_at and stale are null on this answer: a report is not one of ARC's checks. Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: store_record
tools.description: Call this when a user asks what ARC recorded for a store, or you need the citable store page. Returns the store page's verdict, checked_at (the day of the check), stale, category, tried (ARC's standard shoppers' newest dated run, or "Not measured"), the recorded fix, payment_methods_declared (as on before_checkout; null with payment_methods_note when ARC has no UCP profile reading, which is not a no), record_url (claimed, served, date, method and product_markup as JSON) and links to the page, its JSON and Markdown. Example: store_record({"store":"allbirds.com"}) → {"verdict":"…","page_url":"https://www.arcreport.ai/stores/allbirds.com",…}. Reads the published snapshot behind /stores/<host>. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Call this when a user names 2 or more stores for the same item and asks which one to use, or when you must choose between a few stores and want the one where an agent is most likely to reach checkout. Use it instead of calling before_checkout once per store. Pass 2 to 10 store domains or URLs. Returns one short row per store (reaches_checkout, best_route, checked_at, grade, payment_methods_declared as on before_checkout), and pick: among stores whose saved check reached checkout in the last 30 days, the one with the best current Agent Readiness Grade (expired after current of the same letter, not graded last); null when no store has such evidence. A row with stale: true is more than 24 hours old: re-check right before the attempt. Rows are ordered only by saved checkout evidence, its freshness and published grade, never by anything else. Example: compare({"stores":["allbirds.com","gymshark.com"]}) → {"pick":"allbirds.com","stores":[…]}. Each store counts as one precheck read. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: Call this when a person at a store (a CEO, a marketing or e-commerce manager, or a developer) asks where their store is on the journey to AI assistants, what to do next on their platform, or how stores in their category compare. Not for an agent about to check out: use before_checkout for that. Returns the store's place on ARC's journey map (arc-journey/v1: 5 stages, each met, not met or "Not measured" with its date; not measured is not a no, and there is no score or grade), the next 3 steps for its platform at the chosen depth with source links and an as-of date (a platform fact ARC has not sourced says "Not yet documented by ARC"), how many stores ARC checked in its category and on its platform and how many meet each stage (counts with denominators and the snapshot date), and up to 5 named stores that meet the furthest stage (ordered only by stage reached, then the newest reading). role: ceo, manager or developer sets depth (basics, detail or implement) unless depth is given. Send platform alone for the platform guide with no store. Example: guide({"store":"gymshark.com","role":"manager"}) → {"answer":"gymshark.com: Meets stages 1, 2, 3 and 4. Not met: stage 5. Saved check 16 Oct 2026.","stages":[…],"next_steps":[…],"comparison":{…},"examples":{…}}. Saved checks only: no store fetch, no scan, no login. Advisory; ARC stops before payment. Every answer carries checked_at (the saved check it rests on; for a list, the oldest) and stale (true when that check is 24 hours old or older, or has no time). Errors: {error:{code, message, next_step}}.

tools.name: describe_firm
tools.description: What Artemis GTM is: an AI GTM engineering firm for seed to Series C B2B startups, who founded it, what it builds, how it builds (its proprietary agent architecture, never sold or installed), what clients keep, how an engagement starts, how it is priced (two options, Single system build and Embedded GTM Engineering, with prices for both published at https://artemisgtm.ai/pricing/) and the booking link.

tools.name: list_systems
tools.description: The GTM systems Artemis GTM builds inside a client's own CRM and tools, each with the problem it fixes, what gets built and the related free guides. No prices here: prices for both options are published at https://artemisgtm.ai/pricing/.

tools.name: recommend_engagement
tools.description: Given a B2B go-to-market problem in plain language (for example "leads sit for two days before anyone calls them", "most of our website traffic is anonymous", "our ICP is too broad"), name the system Artemis GTM would build to fix it, why, up to two alternates, the related guides and the next step: an evaluation call.

tools.name: book_evaluation
tools.description: The evaluation booking link for Artemis GTM and what happens on the call: Tom Regan walks the motion, names the biggest leak visible from the outside and says whether an engagement fits; the caller leaves with a written scoping note and, if it fits, one of the two options on https://artemisgtm.ai/pricing/, each starting at its published figures, with the final quote to follow. This tool books nothing itself.

tools.name: get_resources
tools.description: The free guides on artemisgtm.ai, by topic (speed to lead, lead scoring and handoff, visitor identification, ICP, outbound, data and reporting), for a person who is not ready for an engagement.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Publish HTML or Markdown content as a shareable URL. Pass `content` byte-for-byte from the source — do not retype, reformat, minify, summarize, or 'clean up' the input; even one stray character can break inline scripts on the published page. If the content is too large to copy verbatim through the model, use the REST endpoint `POST /v1/artifacts` (or `/v1/artifacts/upload` for ZIPs) instead. For Markdown, optionally include images as base64-encoded data.

tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Publish a multi-file HTML site from a base64-encoded ZIP file. The ZIP must contain an index.html at its root. For sites larger than ~10MB — or whenever you have the file on disk — prefer the REST API /v1/artifacts/upload endpoint to avoid base64 overhead and to guarantee byte-faithful upload.

tools.name: get
tools.description: Get artifact metadata. Set include_content to true to also return the full HTML content.

tools.name: versions
tools.description: List version history of an artifact

tools.name: arvx_get_access
tools.description: How to get access to ARVX: the signup link to give the person, what they must do themselves, the price, and how to add their key to this connector. Call this when there is no key, or when the person asks how to start. Costs nothing.

tools.name: arvx_run_reading
tools.description: Run a Reading on two people from the emails between them. Send at least 3 emails written by the user and 3 by the other person, oldest first. From the second Reading on a pair, send the record from the last Reading exactly as it was returned. Costs one Reading (the first 3 are free). Save the record from the answer with this pair.

tools.name: arvx_record_summary
tools.description: When someone asks what is held about them: returns every item in a saved record in plain words. Needs the record and both people's emails. Never uses up a Reading; 10 a month per account.

tools.name: search_card_catalog
tools.description: Find credit cards open to new applicants by issuer, annual fee, network, rewards currency, or a benefit they carry. Returns a short row per card; call get_card_facts for one card's full record. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

tools.name: get_card_facts
tools.description: Everything the public catalog holds on one card: issuer, annual fee, network, foreign transaction fee, rewards currency, and the names of its statement credits, lounge networks and protections. Card name is matched loosely. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

tools.name: compare_card_facts
tools.description: The same catalog record for 2-5 cards at once, for comparing fees, networks and which benefits each carries. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

tools.name: find_transfer_routes
tools.description: Which loyalty programs a currency transfers to, or which currencies reach a destination, and whether a transfer bonus is running. This is the route graph only. It does not carry transfer ratios, bonus sizes, expiry dates, or which route is worth taking. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

tools.name: estimate_point_value
tools.description: Miles' own estimate of a loyalty point's value in cents, optionally multiplied by a balance. A cash balance such as Uber Cash is valued as a share of face value (0.9 is 90%). Call with no arguments to list every program Miles values, with the exact spelling to use. These are Miles' estimates, not market prices. Attribute them. Card facts only: no earning rates, welcome-offer amounts, transfer ratios, or bonus sizes.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Get the current wallet balance for the authenticated account.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Get the retail price per OTP activation for a service in a country. Omit `service` to list prices for every available service.

tools.name: get_inventory
tools.description: Get how many numbers are in stock for a service in a country. Omit `service` to list stock for every available service.

tools.name: create_otp_order
tools.description: Buy a number to receive an OTP: allocates a number, debits the wallet, and returns an orderId + phoneNumber. Then poll with poll_sms. If no code arrives, do NOT cancel to retry: simply call create_otp_order again for a fresh number and keep polling that one. Unfilled orders auto-refund within 10 minutes, so you only pay for codes that actually land and there is no penalty for ordering repeatedly. When a service keeps rejecting codes, order on the "us1" (Non-VoIP AT&T) pool, which has the highest delivery rate. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance.

tools.name: poll_sms
tools.description: Check for the SMS / OTP code on an order. Returns the code once it has arrived, otherwise an empty result: poll again after a few seconds. If nothing lands after a minute or two, the fastest path is to order a fresh number with create_otp_order (prefer the "us1" Non-VoIP pool) and leave the original: it auto-refunds within 10 minutes. Never cancel just to retry, and there is no charge for ordering again, you only pay for codes that arrive.

tools.name: list_active_orders
tools.description: List recent OTP orders for the account (awaiting a code or already received).

tools.name: cancel_order
tools.description: Rarely needed. To retry a verification do NOT cancel: just call create_otp_order again, because every unfilled order auto-refunds within 10 minutes on its own, and cancel is blocked for the first 10 minutes anyway. Only use this to release an order you are certain you no longer need once its 10-minute hold has passed.

tools.name: get_rental_offers
tools.description: List the rental periods and prices for a country (1 day to 12 months). A rented number is yours for the whole period and receives every SMS sent to it, unlike an OTP order, which is for one code. Omit `country` to list the countries numbers can be rented in.

tools.name: rent_number
tools.description: Rent a phone number in a country for a period (get the periods and prices from get_rental_offers first). Debits the wallet and returns the number and when the rental ends. Read its SMS with read_rental_sms. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance; confirm the country, period and price with the user first.

tools.name: list_rentals
tools.description: List the account's rented numbers with their country, period, end date and whether auto-renew is on. Ended rentals are left out unless `includeEnded` is true.

tools.name: read_rental_sms
tools.description: Read the SMS a rented number has received during this rental, newest first. Poll again every few seconds while waiting for a message.

tools.name: cancel_rental
tools.description: Cancel a rented number and refund it. Only possible between 5 and 120 minutes after renting, and only if the number has received no SMS; after that the rental runs to its end date.

tools.name: renew_rental
tools.description: Keep a rented number for another period: the period is added to its current end, at today's price for that period in its country (see get_rental_offers). Possible from 2 hours after renting until 20 minutes before the end. Debits the wallet only if the renewal goes through. WARNING: this spends real wallet balance; confirm the number, period and price with the user first.

tools.name: set_rental_auto_renew
tools.description: With auto-renew on, the number is renewed for its rental period from the wallet a day before it ends (6 hours before for a one-day rental); if the balance is short then, the account is emailed and nothing is charged. Turning it on lets the wallet be charged later: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: check_ai_readiness
tools.description: Technical check of whether AI engines can crawl and understand a website: which AI crawlers robots.txt allows or blocks (answer crawlers like OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot, and training crawlers like GPTBot), whether a sitemap and llms.txt exist, and homepage signals (title, description, H1, JSON-LD entity markup, server-rendered text, noindex). Returns pass/warn/fail checks with plain explanations. It does NOT measure whether engines mention the brand; for that, give the measure_mentions url.

tools.name: get_visibility_scan_link
tools.description: Use when someone asks how visible their brand is in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Gemini, or whether AI engines recommend them. Returns the link to ASRM's free scan for their domain, which asks the AI engines real buyer questions from the brand's category and returns a 0 to 100 score. The scan runs on asrm.ai, not here: never state a score you did not get from the user.

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description: Search ASRM's published guides on AI visibility and generative engine optimization (GEO): how ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini choose which brands to mention and cite, how to get cited, how to track brand mentions, share of voice, and what an AI visibility score measures. Returns titles, summaries and urls; follow with get_guide for the full text. Omit query to list the newest guides.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: The full text of one ASRM guide by slug or asrm.ai/learn/... url. Answer from the text and link the url.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search Assistable's registered MCP tools by the task the user wants to do. Returns up to 5 exact tool definitions with JSON input schemas and annotations. Use this first when you need to choose a tool; the result is not authorization to call it.

tools.name: assistants_list
tools.description: List assistants in a subaccount (excludes archived by default). Note: voice_settings and platform_tools are returned only by assistants_get, not in the list.

tools.name: assistants_get
tools.description: Fetch an assistant's full configuration by ID. The response includes voice_settings (greeting mode, opening messages, voicemail) and platform_tools (attached platform-catalog tool names).

tools.name: assistants_create
tools.description: Create an assistant. Required: name and a subaccount selected by subAccountId, subaccount_id, location_id, or the request header/key scope (an explicit selector on the call takes precedence over the connection default and is authorized against the key). llmConfig supports prompt, model, temperature (0–2); voiceId and assistantType are aliases for voice_id and assistant_type. Flat v3 fields are also accepted; conflicting aliases are rejected. voiceConfig/chatConfig records and unknown llmConfig keys are unsupported and return errors. Use voice_settings or flat inbound_greeting/outbound_greeting for greetings; platform_tools declaratively replaces platform-catalog attachments.

tools.name: assistants_update
tools.description: Patch an assistant. Only supplied fields change, including individual llmConfig prompt/model/temperature keys; temperature must be 0–2. Flat v3 fields and the voiceId/assistantType/subAccountId aliases are accepted; conflicting aliases are rejected; an explicit subaccount selector on the call takes precedence over the connection default and is authorized against the key. voiceConfig/chatConfig records and unknown llmConfig keys are unsupported and return errors. Use voice_settings or flat inbound_greeting/outbound_greeting for greetings; platform_tools declaratively replaces platform-catalog attachments ([] detaches all).

tools.name: assistants_archive
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) an assistant.

tools.name: tools_list
tools.description: List tools visible to a subaccount. Pass includePrebuilt=false for only custom tools.

tools.name: tools_get
tools.description: Fetch a tool's full configuration.

tools.name: tools_create_custom
tools.description: Create a custom tool (toolType=CUSTOM). Name must match /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ and be unique in the subaccount.

tools.name: tools_update
tools.description: Patch a custom tool. Supplying parameters/headers replaces those rows; omit to leave them.

tools.name: tools_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a custom tool.

tools.name: contacts_list
tools.description: List contacts in a subaccount. meta.total is the number of matching contacts, so use it to answer how many contacts there are.

tools.name: contacts_get
tools.description: Fetch a contact by ID.

tools.name: conversations_list
tools.description: List conversations in a subaccount.

tools.name: appointments_list
tools.description: List appointments in a subaccount within an optional date range.

tools.name: calls_get
tools.description: Fetch a call (status, recording, transcript) by ID.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: 자연어로 신품·중고 통합 상품 검색 (슈퍼쇼핑의 기본 진입점).  언제: 사용자가 특정 상품을 찾을 때. 예) "남성 패딩 20만원 이하", "중고 RTX 4070", "27인치 게이밍 모니터". 자동 처리: 도메인(패션/전자)·성별·가격대·속성을 질의에서 추출해 필터링. 반환: {items: [{title, min_price, key_specs, thumbnail, buy_url, source, condition, ...}], total}.   → 결과 제시 시 각 buy_url을 링크로 함께 보여줘라. 사진은 get_product_image로 렌더. 추천만 원하거나 검색어가 모호하면 recommend_products를 써라.

tools.name: get_product_detail
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑 상품의 전체 상세 — 스펙·쇼핑몰별 가격(offers)·신품/중고 교차비교.  언제: 사용자가 한 상품을 깊이 보거나 구매 직전일 때. (product_id는 search/recommend 결과에서 얻는다) 반환: 전체 속성 + offers(쇼핑몰별 buy_url) + comparison_url + other_sources(같은 모델의 다른 소스   신품↔중고 가격 스프레드) + affiliate_disclosure(있으면 고지).   → other_sources로 "같은 모델 중고는 얼마" 같은 가격차를 안내하면 좋다.

tools.name: get_product_image
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑 상품의 대표 이미지를 실제 이미지(렌더 가능)로 반환.  언제: 사용자가 상품 사진을 보고 싶어할 때("이 코트 보여줘"). 검색/추천 결과의 thumbnail은 URL(텍스트)이라 화면에 안 뜨므로, 시각 확인이 필요하면 이 툴로 이미지 자체를 가져온다. 반환: 이미지 콘텐츠(여러 개를 한 번에 보여주지 말고 관심 상품 위주로 호출).

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑 상품 여러 개(2~5개)의 스펙·가격 비교 매트릭스 + 한 줄 결론.  언제: 사용자가 후보 여러 개를 견주려 할 때("이 중에 뭐가 나아?"). product_ids는 search 결과에서. 반환: {attributes: 공통 키, matrix: 상품별 값/가격, verdict: 한국어 결론}.

tools.name: recommend_products
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑에서 의도·예산 기반 상품 추천 + 추천 근거.  언제: 사용자가 구체적 검색어 없이 용도/취향/예산만 말할 때("겨울 데이트룩 추천", "50만원대 가성비 노트북"). 인자: intent(용도/취향), budget(예산 상한), must_have(필수 조건). 반환: {recommendations: [{title, min_price, reason, buy_url, thumbnail, source}], affiliate_disclosure?}.   → 각 추천을 buy_url 링크와 함께 제시하고, 사진은 get_product_image로 보여줘라.

tools.name: recommend_outfit
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑에서 어울리는 코디를 추천 (씨앗 상품 또는 의도 기반).  언제: "이 코트에 어울리는 코디", "가을 데이트룩 코디" 처럼 한 벌 구성을 원할 때. 인자: product_id(씨앗 아이템, 선택), intent(의도/무드, 선택), budget(전체 예산 상한, 선택). 둘 중 하나는 필요. 반환: {seed, items:[{slot, title, min_price, reason, buy_url, thumbnail, source}], styling_reason, affiliate_disclosure?}.   → 각 아이템을 buy_url 링크와 함께 제시하고, 사진은 get_product_image로 보여줘라.

tools.name: analyze_market
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑 카테고리 시세 분석 — 가격 분포·최저가몰·대안.  언제: 사용자가 시세/적정가를 물을 때("그래픽카드 요즘 얼마", "노트북 가격대"). category는 이름(예: '노트북') 또는 ID. 반환: 가격 통계(최저/중앙/최고·분포)·최저가 쇼핑몰·대안 상품.

tools.name: initiate_checkout
tools.description: 슈퍼쇼핑에서 선택한 상품의 구매로 연결 — 최저가 쇼핑몰의 구매 링크와 가격·고지를 반환.  언제: 사용자가 구매 의사를 보일 때("이거 살래", "구매하기"). 실제 결제는 판매처 페이지에서 일어난다. 반환: {payload: {merchant, buy_url(제휴 변환됨), price, ...}, affiliate_disclosure?, next_actions}.   → buy_url을 명확한 구매 링크로 제시하고, affiliate_disclosure가 있으면 반드시 고지하라.   중고(used)는 개인 직거래이므로 안전결제/실물확인을 안내하라.

tools.name: open_ai_access
tools.description: Open the AthenaHQ AI crawler access panel. Enter a public HTTPS domain to inspect crawler responses and robots.txt permissions without an AthenaHQ account.

tools.name: check_public_ai_access
tools.description: Check HTTP responses to AI crawler user agents and robots.txt permissions for a public website. No AthenaHQ account required. Search, retrieval and training are separate. Requests originate from AthenaHQ, not verified crawler IPs. Unknown responses are inconclusive; this does not measure visibility or guarantee indexing, citations or real crawler access. Use nullable evidence and diagnostics.

tools.name: get_prompt_schedules
tools.description: List the Default, custom and archived streaming schedules for a website. Use each row's selection value when filtering analytics or responses. Default includes all pre-cutover history and ad hoc runs; archived schedules retain results. To combine schedules, pass several selection values as an array in the schedule field of query_metrics and query_rows, or use a saved view that stores several schedules. Partner REST filters take one schedule. starts_on and ends_on bound a custom schedule's active period as UTC days (null means no bound); an active schedule outside its period does not run.

tools.name: get_ai_search_value
tools.description: AI Search Value for a website: topic-market value, captured value range, headroom, coverage, value-weighted AI share of voice, per-topic detail, and modeled attributed contribution.

tools.name: get_prompts
tools.description: List prompts (search queries) tracked for a website

tools.name: get_prompt_tags
tools.description: List prompt tags for a website with per-tag prompt counts. Tag IDs can be used with the prompt_tags filter on the prompts endpoint.

tools.name: get_personas
tools.description: List personas configured for a website with per-persona prompt counts. Use it to resolve persona_id values returned by other tools to persona names and descriptions.

tools.name: get_topics
tools.description: List topics (groupings of prompts) for a website, with the count of prompts in each

tools.name: get_competitors
tools.description: List competitors tracked for a website

tools.name: get_content_hub_sheets
tools.description: List the Content Hub tabs/sheets configured for a website. Use to discover available tabs (e.g. 1st-party content, 3rd-party placements, Reddit) before calling get_tracked_content with a specific sheet_id (metrics; excludes in-flight pipeline items) or list_content (every item including unpublished drafts).

tools.name: get_tracked_content
tools.description: List tracked content (1st-party drafts, imported pages, 3rd-party placements) with citation, mention, and impression metrics for the supplied date range and filters. Supports pagination via page_num / page_size and optional filtering by Content Hub sheet_id or content_type. A sheet_id of a view-type tab (see get_content_hub_sheets sheet_type) lists the shared main pool: content not filed in any sheet. In-flight pipeline items (drafts, briefs, running generations) never appear here; enumerate those with list_content. A returned item can still lack a url (pipeline finished but not published anywhere yet).

tools.name: list_content
tools.description: Enumerate every content item in a website's Content Hub, published or not: in-flight drafts, briefs, snipes, optimize and slice runs, scheduled and failed items, plus tracked pages. Returns identity fields only (id, title, type, stage, sheet, URL, timestamps, target prompt ids), no metrics. Uncached and Postgres-backed, so an item created by create_content is listable immediately. Filter by sheet_id, content_type, stage, or prompt_id. stage is the raw pipeline workflow state, not a publication flag: null = no pipeline record (most tracked external / imported pages), and manual editor items carry 'generated'. Treat an item as published only when its stage is done (or it is an external / imported page) AND it has a url; done without a url is an unpublished orphan. A sheet_id of a view-type tab (see get_content_hub_sheets sheet_type) lists the shared main pool without the view's saved filters. Use get_tracked_content for citation and impression metrics on published content; use this tool to discover what exists. Each row carries prompt_ids: the prompts that item was WRITTEN FOR (what create_content was given), capped at 25 with the true size in prompt_count — resolve the ids to text with get_prompts rather than calling get_content_detail per row, and drill in with get_content_detail where prompt_count exceeds the ids returned (that read carries up to 100; associations past 100 are not currently readable). prompt_ids includes soft-deleted prompts, which get_prompts does NOT list — an id that fails to resolve there is a deleted prompt, and get_content_detail returns its text and status: "deleted". Empty prompt_ids means no targeting was recorded, which is normal for imported or externally tracked pages. This is not the same as being cited for a prompt — see get_content_citation_prompts for that. Filter by prompt_id for the reverse question: which content already targets a given prompt (coverage gaps).

tools.name: get_content_detail
tools.description: Fetch the full detail of a single tracked content item — its brief and body text (drafts, optimize rewrites, snipes, authored and scraped pages), plus status, cited source URLs, and links. Use after get_tracked_content to read the actual text behind a content_id. A status of generated_brief means the brief is ready while the article is still being written. Pages registered via track_content_urls return a null body and null status until their page text is fetched from the app — a null body on an external page means not fetched yet, not missing content; citation tracking does not need the body. `prompts` lists the prompts this page was WRITTEN FOR (the same ids create_content takes), newest-linked last, capped at 100 with the true size in `prompts_total`. When prompts_total exceeds 100 the rest are not currently readable through any tool — report the total, do not imply the list is complete. Entries carry status active, paused or deleted: a deleted prompt is still part of what the page was written for and still shows in the Content Hub, but get_prompts will not list it, so use the text returned here. An empty array means the page has no prompt targeting, which is normal for imported or externally tracked pages. That is a different question from get_content_citation_prompts, which lists prompts whose AI responses CITED the page. For an optimize item, source_url is the live page it is based on, available as soon as the item exists; url stays null until publish_content records the published page and marks the item done, so read source_url to link a request in review to its page. source_url is null for other content types and for optimize items based on pasted text or a file. To see the reworded variants actually asked of the models for these prompts, pass their ids to get_responses (each row carries base_prompt plus the variation as prompt) or query the responses cube via query_rows on the prompt_variation dimension.

tools.name: get_content_citation_prompts
tools.description: For a single tracked content item, list every prompt whose AI responses cited it — with citations, citation %, and estimated impressions. Use after get_tracked_content to drill into which prompts a given URL is appearing for. This is CITED-BY, measured over the requested date range, not the targeting the page was written for: an empty prompts array means no AI response cited this URL in that window, which is expected for new or never-cited pages and is not missing data. For the prompts a page was written to target, read `prompts` on get_content_detail (or prompt_ids on list_content) — those come from the content record itself and do not depend on any citation having happened.

tools.name: list_websites
tools.description: List every website accessible to the calling session. Works with any API key (global or scoped) and with MCP/OAuth sessions. Call with an empty argument object `{}`. Each item includes `baseCountry`, the country market the website targets: use it to tell same-brand websites for different countries apart.

tools.name: get_locations
tools.description: List geo-locations configured for a website

tools.name: get_date_range
tools.description: Get the earliest and latest response dates for a website

tools.name: get_responses
tools.description: Get LLM responses for a website. Shows how AI models answer queries, with sources, sentiment, and ranking data. Filter by whether a model used search queries or by text within those queries. For a variation-level export at volume, pair filters.variation_filter with include_response: false and compact_sources: true. That keeps the prompt, its variation, the model, the mentioned/cited flags and the cited domains while dropping the answer text, cutting each row to roughly a tenth of its size.

tools.name: get_response_streaming_status
tools.description: Read the latest (or a specific) response-streaming run's whole-run state and response-queue progress. Only completed means downstream analysis has finished

tools.name: get_response_detail
tools.description: Fetch a single LLM response by id with full sources, mentions, and rank details.

tools.name: get_saved_views
tools.description: List saved views (filter presets) for a website

tools.name: get_group_saved_views
tools.description: List group-level saved views (filter presets) shared across the websites in a group

tools.name: get_credits_organization
tools.description: Get credit balance for the organization

tools.name: get_credits_website
tools.description: Get credit balance for a specific website

tools.name: get_groups
tools.description: List all groups in the organization (global API key only)

tools.name: get_group_detail
tools.description: Fetch a single group by id with its member websites.

tools.name: get_share_of_voice_cumulative
tools.description: Get cumulative share of voice — overall SOV for each competitor across the date range. Each entry also includes relative_mention_rate: the share of responses mentioning any tracked brand that mention this entity.

tools.name: get_share_of_voice_time_series
tools.description: Get share of voice over time — how often the website is mentioned vs competitors, grouped by day. Each entry also includes relative_mention_rate: the share of that day's responses mentioning any tracked brand that mention this entity.

tools.name: get_citation_rate_cumulative
tools.description: Get cumulative citation rate — average citation rate for each competitor across the date range. citation_rate is absolute (share of all responses); relative_citation_rate is the share of responses citing the website or any tracked competitor.

tools.name: get_citation_rate_time_series
tools.description: Get citation rate over time — how often AI models cite (link to) the website, grouped by day. citation_rate is absolute (share of that day's responses); relative_citation_rate is the share of that day's responses citing the website or any tracked competitor.

tools.name: get_mention_rate_cumulative
tools.description: Get cumulative mention rate — average mention rate for each competitor across the date range. mention_rate is absolute (share of all responses); relative_mention_rate is the share of responses mentioning any tracked brand.

tools.name: get_mention_rate_time_series
tools.description: Get mention rate over time — how often AI models mention the website by name, grouped by day. mention_rate is absolute (share of that day's responses); relative_mention_rate is the share of that day's responses mentioning any tracked brand.

tools.name: get_position_cumulative
tools.description: Get cumulative position — average ranking position for each competitor across the date range.

tools.name: get_position_time_series
tools.description: Get ranking position over time — average position of the website in AI model responses, grouped by day.

tools.name: get_position_distribution
tools.description: Get position distribution: share of responses where the brand ranks top/middle/bottom across the date range.

tools.name: query_metrics
tools.description: Query aggregated metrics for brand performance, competitors, sources, citations, and response trends. Use query_rows for individual records.  Mentions: from "response_mentions". Citations: from "citations". On either, where { is_website: true } selects the brand; { is_competitor: true } selects competitors; { entity_id: { eq: "<uuid>" } } selects one entity. Filter/group models by model_category (display names like "ChatGPT", "Claude"), never "model". Dimensions vary by cube; source_mentions has no prompt/model dimensions. Group by week (Monday start) or month wherever date groups. prompt_status is the paused flag (true = paused).  Measures: count, count_distinct, avg, sum, min, max; per-measure where enables conditional aggregation. Use compare for two date ranges. When grouping by IDs, use alsoSelect for names: entity_id/entity_name, prompt_id/prompt_text, prompt_topic_id/topic_name (prompts uses topic_id).  Cited pages mentioning competitors but not the brand: from "sources", where { source_mentions_entity: { hasSome: [competitorIds], hasNone: [brandId] } }. Also works on "source_mentions". Checks all stored page mentions per URL/website. Date/model on sources scope AI responses; extracted page content may be older than the live page.  Content-hub attribution: on "sources", where { is_attributed_content: true }; by: ["content_id"], alsoSelect: ["content_title"]. Add content_type to by for type, or group by content_type alone. Read articles from "contents" via query_rows.  Schedule: select one "default" or custom/archived UUID from the catalog, or an array of them to combine schedules. Omit for caller default (current page in Ask Athena); explicit schedule overrides it. Top-level prompt_schedule_kind/id equality filters remain supported but must not conflict with schedule. Historical provenance is independent of current prompt membership; website-level cubes are unaffected.

tools.name: query_rows
tools.description: Query individual analytics rows. Use for qualitative data like response text, specific identifiers, or individual mentions.  Schedule selection: pass schedule: "default" or a custom/archived UUID from the schedule catalog, or an array of them to combine schedules. Omit to use the caller default (Ask Athena uses the current page selection). Explicit selection overrides that default. Existing top-level equality predicates on prompt_schedule_kind/id remain supported, but cannot conflict with schedule. Historical provenance does not change with current prompt membership. Website-level cubes are unaffected.  Cubes (same set as query_metrics): attributes, citations, competitors, contents, prompts, response_mentions, responses, source_mentions, sources, topics, websites. Returns { rows, nextCursor, hasMore }. Pass nextCursor back as "after" to paginate. prompt_status is the prompt's paused flag (boolean, true = paused), not a status string. On the responses cube, content is hydrated from Postgres and can only be selected. Do not filter or sort by content. Use search_terms_in_responses for text frequency analysis. Use query_metrics for aggregates instead.

tools.name: list_pitches
tools.description: List pitch workspace reports for the organization. Returns all non-deleted pitches with their status and metadata.

tools.name: get_pitch
tools.description: Get a pitch report by ID including competitors, prompts, attributes, top citing sources, and aggregate metrics (brand mentions, sentiment, response rate).

tools.name: get_sources
tools.description: List top cited sources (root domains) for a website with citation, mention, brand-mention, and impression metrics. Each row is classified as owned / competitor / partner / third_party. Supports filters (date range, models, prompts, competitors, locations, personas), source_tags (tag IDs from source_tags__list, owned, competitor, other, untagged), sort, and pagination via page_num / page_size.

tools.name: get_youtube_creators
tools.description: List YouTube channels cited in AI answers for a website, ordered by citations (unknown channel last). Includes channel citation shares, category and video-length breakdowns, and metadata availability. Totals and breakdowns cover the full filtered result, independent of pagination. Use get_youtube_videos with channel_key to list a creator's videos. Reads saved metadata; pending or missing details remain null.

tools.name: get_youtube_videos
tools.description: List YouTube videos cited in AI answers for a website, ordered by citation count. Returns saved titles, channel details, categories, durations, publication dates, citation counts, distinct-response citation percentages and linked timestamps. Watch, Shorts and short-link variants of one video are combined. Filter by channel_key or video_id. Metadata may be pending or missing; no live YouTube fetch is performed.

tools.name: get_tiktok_creators
tools.description: List TikTok handles cited in AI answers, ordered by citations with unattributed URLs last. Includes profiles, videos and photos across tiktok.com, www, m, vm and vt hosts. Handles come from cited URLs, not verified account identities; short links are not resolved. Citation shares and totals cover all filtered TikTok citations, including unattributed URLs, independent of pagination. Use get_tiktok_pages with channel_key to drill down. No scraping or live TikTok requests.

tools.name: get_tiktok_pages
tools.description: List TikTok URLs cited in AI answers, ordered by citations. Includes profile, video, photo and unattributed URLs. Filter by channel_key from get_tiktok_creators. Each page's share_percent and totals use all filtered TikTok citations, including unattributed URLs, even when drilling into one channel or paginating. These are AI-answer citation counts, not TikTok views or engagement. No scraping or live TikTok requests.

tools.name: get_source_pages
tools.description: List individual cited URLs (pages) for a website with citation, mention, and impression metrics plus a per-URL daily sparkline. Each row is classified as owned / competitor / partner / third_party. Companion to get_sources (root-domain-level). Supports filters (date range, models, prompts, competitors, locations, personas), source_tags (tag IDs from source_tags__list, owned, competitor, other, untagged), search, sort, and pagination.

tools.name: get_attributes
tools.description: List the brand traits (called attributes in the API) tracked for a website: brand-perception keywords such as 'Affordable' or 'Slow Support'. Athena extracts these from AI model responses. Brand traits are direction-neutral; `positive` selects the directional series and defaults to true when omitted. Use this to discover attribute ids, then get_attribute_metrics for how often each is mentioned, or get_attribute_time_series for one attribute's trend over time.

tools.name: get_attribute_metrics
tools.description: Get cumulative brand trait (attribute) metrics: for each brand-perception keyword (e.g. 'Affordable', 'Slow Support'), how many AI responses mentioned it across the date range, and the percentage. `positive` selects the observation direction and defaults to true when omitted. `total_responses` is the denominator: responses in the date range that mention the brand AND had attribute extraction run on them. It is NOT every response for the website — responses that never mention the brand are excluded, and Athena samples which responses get extraction, so un-analyzed ones are excluded too. Compute rates from the returned `percentage` / `total_responses` rather than against a response count from another endpoint. Attributes nobody mentioned come back with response_count 0. Use get_competitor_attribute_metrics for the same breakdown per competitor.

tools.name: get_competitor_attribute_metrics
tools.description: Get brand trait (attribute) metrics per tracked competitor: for each competitor and each brand-perception keyword (e.g. 'Affordable'), how many AI responses mentioned that keyword for that competitor, and the percentage. Use with get_attribute_metrics to compare the brand against competitors. `total_responses` is per-competitor: responses in the date range that mention THAT competitor and had attribute extraction run on them. Each competitor therefore has its own denominator, and none of them is the website's total response count. `positive` selects the observation direction and defaults to true when omitted. Returns one row per competitor per attribute, so results can be large — filter with competitor_ids. Competitors with no responses in the date range are omitted entirely rather than returned with zeros.

tools.name: get_attribute_time_series
tools.description: Get the daily trend for ONE brand trait (attribute), brand and competitors side by side — how mentions of a keyword like 'Affordable' moved over time. Requires an attribute_id: call get_attributes first to discover ids. `positive` selects the observation direction and defaults to true when omitted. Days with no data are returned as zeros, so the series is gap-free and chartable. Denominators are per-side, not the day's whole response set: brand_percentage divides by that day's responses that mention the brand (and had attribute extraction run), and competitor_percentage by responses that mention the tracked competitors. brand_total and competitor_total return those denominators explicitly. Competitor figures aggregate all tracked competitors unless competitor_ids narrows them.

tools.name: get_attribute_observations
tools.description: Get individual brand trait (attribute) observations: each row is one AI response describing one entity (the brand or a competitor) with one brand trait, including the response excerpt as `text_span`. `score` runs from -1 to 1 and its sign always matches `positive`; its magnitude (0.1 to 1.0) is how strongly the wording praises or criticizes. `score` is null when the observation was not scored (extracted before scoring existed, or no valid value was recorded); for direction only, use `score ?? (positive ? 1 : -1)`. Omit `positive` for both directions. `sort: "intensity"` (the default) returns the strongest observations first with unscored ones last; `sort: "recent"` returns the newest first. Narrow with entity_ids and attribute_ids (from get_attributes). Paginate with page_num and page_size; a page can hold fewer than page_size rows when an excerpt is no longer available, so use `has_more` to decide whether to fetch the next page. Use get_attribute_metrics for how often each trait is mentioned.

tools.name: get_user_by_email
tools.description: Look up a user by email address, scoped to the caller's organization. Returns 404 when the email does not belong to a member of the organization or of one of its websites.

tools.name: get_oracle_findings
tools.description: When grounding is present, use its complete team-confirmed statement and all supporting facts as joint evidence; the legacy fact ID/text are only a compatibility anchor. List Oracle accuracy findings for a website: places where an AI response contradicted a verified brand fact (type 'inaccuracy' or 'kb_issue', with quote, claim, and reason) or where two knowledge-base facts conflict ('kb_duplicate' / 'kb_contradiction', pairing fact_text with related_fact_text). Findings from every status are included by default (pending, acknowledged, ignored, ...), each row carrying its status — pass the status filter for pending items only. Filters (run_id, fact_id, lineage_id, response_id, prompt_id, source_url, type, kind, severity, status) AND-compose; source_url matches evidence URLs exactly after normalization (protocol and trailing slash ignored). 'total' is the pre-limit count. 'latest_run' is the newest scan of any kind and is null only when the website has never been scanned, so latest_run plus empty findings means it scanned clean, while latest_run null means never scanned, not clean. Archived findings from before the current scanner ARE included: their run carries 'is_imported': true and keeps its original started_at, so an import can be the newest run — say the history is archived rather than calling it a current scan. 'has_imported_history' is true when any such archived run exists, and every finding row carries 'run_is_imported' so archival and current rows stay distinguishable in one list. Returns status 'no_access' if the brand does not have Oracle v2; that response carries the status alone, with no counts or findings.

tools.name: get_oracle_finding
tools.description: When grounding is present, use its complete team-confirmed statement and all supporting facts as joint evidence; the legacy fact ID/text are only a compatibility anchor. Load one Oracle finding in full: the flagged claim with its verified fact and prompt text, the run it came from, a ~2000-character response excerpt centered on the quoted claim, the cited-page evidence captured during the run (url, quote, snippet, scrape_hash), and its lineage: sibling findings sharing its lineage_id across runs, newest first. Use after get_oracle_findings to interrogate a specific finding. Returns a not-found error for an unknown finding id, and status 'no_access' if the brand does not have Oracle v2.

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: List the organization's API key metadata, including creator and creation date, oldest first. Includes revoked keys so polling can detect keys revoked between checks. Never returns secrets or hashes. Requires a global API key or an organization admin's MCP connection. For polling, keep since/until fixed while paging, overlap successive windows and deduplicate by id. This is an inventory, not a durable event log; deleted creator accounts remove their keys.

tools.name: add_brand_facts
tools.description: Add brand facts to a website's Knowledge Base in bulk (1-50 per call). Each fact runs the full ingestion pipeline (deduplication, approval gates, pillar routing); there is no way to force-approve. Returns one outcome per fact (approved | pending | duplicate; extensible) with the created fact id and the pillar it was filed under. Facts without a pillar_id are routed automatically and may land unfiled. A fact similar to facts already in the Knowledge Base is not added: its outcome is duplicate and lists them under matches, and the response carries a match_token. To resolve, call again with those facts, the match_token, one decision per listed match (approve, optionally with new text, or delete) and save_submitted (true adds the facts as written, false only applies the decisions).

tools.name: add_competitors
tools.description: Start tracking competitors on a website, 1 to 25 per call, under the same rules as the Competitors page. Each competitor needs a name and its website url, or no_website: true for a brand with no website of its own; identifiers and additional_urls are optional. Returns one result per competitor, in order: added, already_tracked (the website already tracks that url; nothing changes), or rejected with the reason (a url on the website's own domains, an invalid url, or the limit of 500 competitors per website). New AI responses count mentions of an added competitor right away. Past responses are reanalyzed only when someone runs the backfill on the Competitors page, which costs credits; this tool never starts it and costs no credits.

tools.name: add_content
tools.description: Add an article that is already written (for example, one drafted in this conversation) to the website's Content Hub as an editable draft. Same as pasting it into the Content Hub's blank editor: no AI model runs and no content credits are spent. Use create_content instead when Athena should research and write the piece. body is the full article in Markdown and is stored as given, except that link and image destinations with an unsafe scheme (javascript:, data:) become #. The item is created with type manual at stage generated, and the body is recorded as version 1, so get_content_draft, edit_content, revise_content and get_content_versions work on it right away. Pass title, or it is taken from the body's first heading (else its first line). sheet_id must be a tab from get_content_hub_sheets: a sheet-type tab keeps the item, a view-type tab or no sheet_id puts it in the shared pool. The item is not published. Once it is live on the site, call publish_content with its URL to start citation tracking.

tools.name: approve_brief
tools.description: Approve a content brief and start writing the article from it. Only valid while the piece is at status generated_brief. The article is generated from the brief exactly as it currently stands, including any revisions made with revise_brief or edits made in the app. Consumes content credits; poll get_content_status afterwards, then read the result with get_content_draft.

tools.name: create_brand_kit
tools.description: Create a brand kit from text the user provides: a name, guidance text per field (voice is the writing direction), voice settings and writing rules, all authored by the caller; nothing is generated. The kit starts as a draft; content generation uses it only once published, which publish: true does as version 1 (or update_brand_kit later). The website's first kit becomes its default. A name another kit uses is refused; a rule that contradicts an existing global rule is refused with the explanation and no kit is created. Kit rules need the writing rules feature on the plan. To change an existing kit, use update_brand_kit; to generate a kit from the website or uploaded documents, use the Brand Profile page.

tools.name: create_content
tools.description: Generate an article or content brief in AthenaHQ. Fetches source URLs, sends source material to external AI providers, and consumes content credits. Obtain user approval before calling. Does not publish to a website or CMS. For draft mode, auto_approve defaults to true; set false to generate only a brief and wait for approve_brief. Poll get_content_status using each returned content_ids value. Slice mode returns slice_titles and an empty content_ids array; generated items appear in list_content. To save an already-written article without generation or credit use, call add_content.

tools.name: create_location
tools.description: Create a location for a website

tools.name: create_pillar
tools.description: Create a Knowledge Base pillar (a subject area that groups brand facts) from a name and optional description. Get-or-create semantics: if a pillar with the same name already exists, it is returned with created: false instead of failing, so retries are idempotent.

tools.name: create_prompt_tag
tools.description: Create a prompt tag on a website, or return the existing tag when its name matches case-insensitively. Trims surrounding whitespace and rejects reserved prompt-type names. Returns the tag ID and whether it was created. Use the returned ID to assign the tag to prompts; creating a tag does not assign it to any prompts.

tools.name: create_prompts
tools.description: Create one or more prompts on a website

tools.name: create_saved_view
tools.description: Create a saved view (filter preset) for a website. Saved views appear in the dashboard filter bar for every member of the website. filters is an object keyed by filter field key, each value shaped {"id": "<unique string>", "field": "<same field key>", "operator": "is_any_of", "values": [...]}. Common field keys: "models" (slugs like "chatgpt", "perplexity", "google_ai_overview"), "competitors", "prompts", "personas", "locations", "promptTags", "attributes" (arrays of UUIDs from the matching list tools), "countries", "sourceTag". "promptTags" also accepts the builtin tokens "type:high_intent" (branded prompts) and "type:discovery" (non-branded) alongside tag UUIDs. "sourceTag" values are the builtin categories "owned", "competitor", "partner", "third_party", the states "other" (the Other badge) and "untagged" (no tag), or custom source tag UUIDs, not display labels; custom source tag ids appear on existing saved views (list the website's saved views to find them). When unsure, list the website's saved views and mirror their filter shapes. icon, when set, must be a supported Remix icon name (e.g. "RiStarLine"); invalid names are rejected with the full list. When talking to the user about a view or its filters, use the dashboard names (Branded / Non-branded prompts, Owned / Competitor / Partner / Third party / Other / No tag sources), never internal tokens, field keys, operator strings, or icon identifiers.

tools.name: create_topic
tools.description: Create a topic on a website (returns the existing topic when the name is already taken)

tools.name: delete_brand_facts
tools.description: Permanently delete 1-50 brand facts from a website's Knowledge Base. There is no undo. Ids that do not exist on the website are reported in not_found_ids rather than failing the call, so retries are idempotent. Requires an admin; on OAuth connections the signed-in user must have the admin role.

tools.name: delete_content
tools.description: Delete a content row. Destructive: physical row delete, no undo. Powers delete-and-retry. Bulk delete is out of scope.

tools.name: delete_location
tools.description: Delete a location from a website

tools.name: delete_pillars
tools.description: Permanently delete 1-20 Knowledge Base pillars and every fact filed under them. Facts are deleted, not unfiled; there is no undo. Ids that do not exist on the website are reported in not_found_ids rather than failing the call, so retries are idempotent; ids in failed_ids are untouched and safe to retry. Requires an admin; on OAuth connections the signed-in user must have the admin role.

tools.name: delete_prompt
tools.description: Delete a prompt (soft when responses exist, hard otherwise)

tools.name: delete_topic
tools.description: Delete a topic (soft delete; optionally also delete its prompts)

tools.name: draft_outreach_message
tools.description: Draft a pitch email to the author of a cited page and save it as the page's Outreach draft, replacing any previous draft. Uses the website's team-wide Outreach custom instructions, the saved author name, and the sender's name. Costs 0.1 credits per draft written (billed in whole credits every 10 drafts); free when the page cannot be read. Show the draft to the user before they send it; nothing is sent.

tools.name: edit_content
tools.description: Apply exact find-and-replace edits to a content draft's article body. Deterministic, no AI model involved: your replacement text lands verbatim (use revise_content when you want an AI rewrite from an instruction). Each edit's find text must match the current body exactly once; zero or multiple matches fail the whole call and nothing is saved, so extend the find text until it is unique. Edits apply in order, later ones see earlier results, and the batch is recorded as one new version, recoverable via get_content_versions / restore_content_version. Pass expected_version_number from get_content_draft to fail with a conflict when a new version was recorded after your read (a revision, edit, or restore). An app autosave changes the body without recording a version; that drift is caught by the anchors themselves, since a moved or vanished find text fails the call.

tools.name: find_more_prompt_discovery
tools.description: Find more prompts for a finished Discover run: start the next round of its series with the same sources, effort level, country, language and custom instructions. The round skips every question the series already suggested and reads evidence earlier rounds did not use, so its prompts add to the same list. Invoke only after the user asks for more prompts from an existing run, and confirm with them first: each round runs the same paid research as a new run. A series takes one round at a time and at most two after the first run, and ends early after a round that found fewer than ten new prompts or nothing new to read; the tool then refuses with the reason. Returns the new round's run ID; poll the discovery history tool with it. Prompts are not added to tracking automatically. Requires prompt-management permission and the series' source entitlements.

tools.name: find_outreach_author
tools.description: Find who wrote a cited page and how to reach them, then save it to the page's Outreach contact. Reads the page's byline, the addresses the page publishes, and Hunter.io; when no author is found it returns the site's contact address and contact page instead. Every email comes with its source. Costs 0.1 credits when an author is found (billed in whole credits every 10 lookups); free otherwise. Overwrites the saved author fields. Obtain user confirmation before running it over many pages.

tools.name: get_ai_insight
tools.description: Read one stored AI insight in full, by its id from get_ai_insights: its title, headline, body, suggested action, why it happened (with reasons and their pages), its numbers (facts, each with the table it came from), its move (subject, metric, current and previous values, the direction that is good news, and a definition of what the series counts and what it is out of), its evidence (topics, competitors, prompts, URLs), and the scope its numbers were computed under (window, comparison period, Default schedule, the prompts active at the analysis, prompt-type filter, the models the citation tables leave out). The numbers are the card's as of its analysis: quote them as such, with the window and the date the analysis ran (analyzed_at). A recompute with the other tools counts today's active prompts, so it can differ. Returns a not-found error for an insight that is not this website's, and status 'no_access' when AI Insights is not part of the organization's setup.

tools.name: get_ai_insights
tools.description: List the website's stored AI insights: the precomputed cards on the AI Insights page, each a verified finding of one past analysis, newest analysis first and higher impact first. Each has its id, title, headline, category, impact, the days its numbers cover (window), the time the analysis ran (analyzed_at), its status (available, done, or discarded = hidden by the team), the team's rating, and its move's subject and metric. Call this first for an open-ended request for insights or for what to do ('give me some insights', 'what's interesting', 'what should I prioritize'), and answer from these cards instead of running a new analysis: highest impact first, each by its title and headline. Always state the window and the date the analysis ran, and offer a fresh look with the other analytics tools. Read one card in full with get_ai_insight. Paged: 20 by default; for more, pass limit (up to 50) and offset set to the returned next_offset until it is null. Default status is available. Returns status 'no_access' when AI Insights is not part of the organization's setup. Then, or when no insight is listed, answer from the other analytics tools.

tools.name: get_brand_facts
tools.description: List a website's brand facts from the Knowledge Base, newest first, with offset paging. By default excludes facts generated by Oracle analysis; pass include_oracle=true to include them. Filters: pillar, review status (default approved), source type, and unfiled=true for facts not under any published pillar (unfiled and pillar_id are mutually exclusive).

tools.name: get_brand_kit
tools.description: Read a brand kit as the Brand Profile editor shows it, to inspect or change it: the draft name, the eight guidance fields as text (voice is the writing direction), voice settings (1-5 or auto), tone traits, the kit's writing rules with ids, and the website's global writing rules with ids, plus draft and published versions. Omit kit_id for the website's default kit; available_kits lists every kit. Content generation uses a kit's published version, so has_unpublished_changes means the draft differs from it. Guidance fields longer than the clip come back shortened and listed in truncated_fields; pass fields to read those whole, which update_brand_kit's find needs. Rules are clipped too, each with its own truncated flag. Call this before update_brand_kit. To write in the brand's voice, read brandKit__get instead. Read-only.

tools.name: get_content_draft
tools.description: Read the current draft text of a content item — the article body as it stands right now, including every revision applied so far.
