By default returns active websites: use `organizationId` to scope one organization, `scope=shared` without it for direct grants outside your memberships, or `scope=all` with it to combine both; supports `sort` by `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `name` and case-insensitive `search`, and each item includes `organizationSlug`, `primaryHostname`, and whether it is `shared`. Pass `status=deleted` with `organizationId` (requires organization-level trash access) to list restorable soft-deleted websites instead, each with its deletion time and purge deadline; deleted rows drop out when their 30-day restore window expires. Both modes use cursor pagination (default 20 per page, maximum 100). Fetch one website with `websites.get`.

tools.name: websites_get
tools.description: Returns a single website by `websiteId`, or by its `organizationSlug` + `websiteSlug` pair when starting from a URL — provide exactly one of the two identifications. The response includes whether the caller can manage the website’s CMS schema and domains. Websites in the trash remain retrievable by id (see `websites.list` with `status=deleted` for their purge timing); slug lookups only resolve active websites, and inaccessible or deleted resources return 404.

tools.name: websites_create
tools.description: Creates a website in the organization. Provide either a `name` (trimmed, 1–200 characters) or a creation `prompt`; a prompt returns immediately with the temporary name `Untitled site`, which the built-in naming request attempts to replace on its next run together with a matching available slug and platform hostname. The hostname receives a short suffix when the clean hostname is unavailable. An omitted `slug` is allocated from the initial name; an explicit slug must be lowercase, URL-safe, unreserved, and unique among active websites in the organization. The website starts as an unpublished draft at `headVersion` 1. Send an `idempotencyKey` to make retries return the same website. Edit its source through the Source code operations, then publish with `websiteSourceCode.head.publish`.

tools.name: websites_rename
tools.description: Updates the website’s display name and, when supplied, its URL slug. The slug must be lowercase, URL-safe, unreserved, and unique among active websites in the organization.

tools.name: websiteDomains_list
tools.description: Returns every domain record attached to the website, oldest first: the automatically allocated platform subdomain plus any custom domains. Platform subdomains are always `active`; custom domains carry their current verification status and the DNS records still expected.

tools.name: websiteDomains_createCustomDomain
tools.description: Claims `hostname` for this website and registers it with the Cactal edge. Custom domains must first be enabled for the website (`websiteDomains.setEnabled`, owner-only — enabling is the billing moment); the request fails with 403 `custom_domains_disabled` otherwise. Adding or removing domains on an enabled website never changes billing. The domain is created in `pending_dns` status, and the returned `dnsRecords` list exactly what to create at your DNS provider: an ownership TXT record on `_cactal.<hostname>` plus a routing record (a CNAME for subdomains or an A record for apex domains). Hostnames must be lowercase ASCII domains (not IP addresses or Cactal platform hosts), each website can have at most 10 custom domains, and a hostname can be claimed by only one website; claims that never verify expire after 7 days. After creating the records, call the verify endpoint or wait for the automatic re-checks.

tools.name: websiteDomains_verifyCustomDomain
tools.description: Re-checks the ownership TXT record, edge readiness, and whether an HTTPS request to the hostname reaches this Cactal domain, then returns the updated status. A customer CDN or reverse proxy in front is supported when it forwards the verification request to Cactal. `failureMessage` distinguishes a missing ownership record, an unreachable hostname, and a hostname served somewhere else. Cactal asks the domain nameservers directly, so new records usually count on the next check, and this endpoint is safe to poll; Cactal also re-checks pending domains automatically (every minute for the first 2 hours, every 5 minutes for the first day, then every 15 minutes). The first custom domain to become active is promoted to primary automatically.

tools.name: websiteDomains_setPrimaryDomain
tools.description: Makes this domain the canonical hostname for the published website: requests reaching the platform subdomain or any other custom domain are permanently redirected (HTTP 308) to it, preserving path and query. Only `active` custom domains can be made primary — the request fails with 409 otherwise. Any previous primary is cleared in the same transaction.

tools.name: websiteDomains_removeCustomDomain
tools.description: Deregisters the hostname from the Cactal edge and deletes the domain record. If the removed domain was primary, the oldest remaining active custom domain is promoted automatically. If edge deregistration fails, the domain stays in `removing` status and a background sweep retries until it is gone. Platform subdomains cannot be removed.

tools.name: websiteDomains_renamePlatformDomain
tools.description: Moves the website to `<label>.<platform domain>`, the free address every website is allocated at creation. `label` is just the leading part: 1-40 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and inner hyphens, and it may not be one of the labels Cactal reserves. The change takes effect immediately, on published and draft hosts alike. The previous hostname is released at the same moment, with no redirect and no grace period, so any existing links to it break and another website may claim it. Take care on a published site. Fails with 409 when the label is already taken by another website; renaming to the label the website already has is a no-op. Custom domains are unaffected, and if one of them is primary it stays the canonical address.

tools.name: websiteAssets_list
tools.description: Returns ready assets newest first as compact rows (`description`, `category`, dimensions, `url`, `srcSet`); fetch one asset for `originalUrl` and `variants`. Filter by `kind`, `category`, `type` (the broad MIME family: image, video, audio, font, or document), or `search`, which prefix-matches each term against the filename, description, and category; every term must match, else any term. Page size defaults to 50 (max 100).

tools.name: websiteAssets_get
tools.description: Returns the asset with `description`, `category`, and its CDN delivery shape: for transformable images `url` is the optimized 1920px default and `originalUrl` the original bytes; both never expire. MCP clients that render images also receive the image.

tools.name: websiteAssets_importFromUrl
tools.description: Fetches 1-10 public http(s) URLs server-side, one at a time, and stores each as a ready asset with no upload or finalize step. Media only: images, fonts, PDF, audio, video, dotLottie, and Rive; text, data, documents, and archives are refused. Images, fonts, and PDFs must parse as what they claim, hosts on private addresses are rejected, the upload kind and MIME rules apply, and each download is capped at 30 MiB (larger files must be uploaded directly). Each item may carry a `description` and, for images, a `category`. Name each item by `url`, or by `photo`: the number over a picture on contact sheets `webResearch.profile` or `webResearch.viewImage` showed you, which saves copying its long signed link. `assets` carries successes with CDN URLs and `sourceUrl`; `errors` carries failures typed `invalid_url`, `non_public_address`, `unreachable`, `too_large`, `unsupported_type`, `signature_expired`, or `unknown_photo` (a number you were not shown or that expired; look at the pictures again for current numbers). Import only assets you have the right to use.

tools.name: websiteAssets_update
tools.description: Changes `filename`, `description`, or `category`. Pass only the fields to change; `null` clears a field. `category` is images only.

tools.name: websiteAssets_delete
tools.description: Archives the asset: it immediately stops appearing in list responses and its id returns 404 from every asset endpoint. Archival cannot be undone through the API; previously issued CDN URLs keep serving the file.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_project_get
tools.description: Returns the website’s durable project knowledge: the text the user maintains as `content`, plus the `agentNotes` Cactal distills from agent conversations. Both are included in every Cactal agent request. Read them before working on a website.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_project_edit
tools.description: Applies exact-match text edits to the user’s project knowledge text, in order; an empty `oldStr` appends. Change it only when the user asks; agent-discovered facts belong in agent notes. A passage that no longer matches fails with `validation` and returns the current content.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_agentNotes_edit
tools.description: Applies exact-match text edits to the agent notes, in order; an empty `oldStr` appends. Record only durable facts, decisions, rejected directions, and constraints, one short line each, never progress logs or anything derivable from the website source. A passage that no longer matches fails with `validation` and returns the current notes.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_list
tools.description: Lists the website’s private durable context entries: uploaded files and pasted text, each with a `title`, a generated `description`, and an `origin` of `upload` or `text`.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_create
tools.description: Keeps pasted or typed text as a context entry the agent searches and reads when relevant, using one of the website’s 25 slots. Cactal titles and describes it. Use this for material the user gives you to keep; your own findings belong in agent notes.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_update
tools.description: Renames a context entry or replaces the text the agent reads. Replacing text does not change the downloadable original; images have no text.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_read
tools.description: Read a bounded line range from a project context document. Read short relevant documents directly; search large documents first. Do not reread sufficient search passages.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_search
tools.description: Find evidence across selected project context documents. Batch independent queries; use passages directly when sufficient. Results merge overlapping text and include source ranges and zero-based queryIndexes into queries. matched reports a hit; truncated means evidence may be omitted, clipped means partial lines, and unavailableResourceIds were not searched. Resolve missing evidence before concluding a fact is absent.

tools.name: websiteKnowledge_view
tools.description: Returns one private PNG, JPEG, or WebP context resource.

tools.name: websiteFavicons_set
tools.description: Sets the website’s current favicon to a ready PNG, SVG, or ICO image from the same website asset library. Send `assetId: null` to clear it. The change applies immediately to every site host and is independent of source drafts and publishing. Read the current favicon from the `faviconUrl` field on `GET /websites` and `GET /websites/find`.

tools.name: websiteShareLinks_list
tools.description: Lists the website’s share links: paths such as `/menu.pdf` that open one of its images or files. Give people each `url`, not the file’s CDN delivery URL.

tools.name: websiteShareLinks_set
tools.description: Points a path on the website, such as `/menu.pdf`, at a ready image or file in its asset library. A file has one link: a new path moves it, and setting a linked path to another file moves that path (how a replaced file keeps its link). Paths used by pages, config redirects, or the site server are refused; at most 100 per website. Applies at once on every site host, without publishing, as a 302 to the file’s current delivery URL.

tools.name: websiteShareLinks_remove
tools.description: Removes the file’s share link, if it has one. The path stops opening the file immediately on every site host.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_summary_get
tools.description: Returns `headVersion`, `publishedVersion`, and whether the website has unpublished source changes.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_list
tools.description: Lists file identities, sizes, and line counts without contents, sorted by type then name with cursor pagination (default 20, maximum 100). Filter by name with `nameGlob`. Defaults to head; pass `target=published` or an explicit `version`, and pin continuation requests to the resolved response version.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_read
tools.description: Reads up to 50 files by name from head, published, or an explicit version. A single-file read supports line and character ranges; continue truncated reads with `nextStartCharacter` and the resolved `version`.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_search
tools.description: Finds text across every source file and returns one entry per matching line with its file name, line, and column. Call this first to locate code, then read only the files it names with websiteSourceCode.files.read. `pattern` is literal text unless `isRegex` is set, and matching is line by line, so a pattern cannot span a newline. Narrow with `nameGlob` and `type`, ask for surrounding lines with `contextLines`, or set `filesOnly` for the cheapest orientation. Results are cursor-paginated over matches.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_changes_list
tools.description: Lists added, removed, and modified file identities between two version refs, defaulting from published to head. Results use cursor pagination; pin continuation requests to the resolved version numbers.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_diff
tools.description: Returns a bounded unified diff for one file name between two version refs, defaulting from published to head.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_lease_acquire
tools.description: Acquires and replaces the website's single edit lease, taking over from any other editor. Writes that pass the returned principal-bound `leaseToken` keep working until someone else takes the lease; writes without a token take the lease automatically unless another editor is still working: the Cactal agent while it runs, or another caller that wrote in the last 5 minutes.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_upsert
tools.description: Creates or replaces one head file. Pages, components, and modules require `name`; singleton types take only `type`. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent and returns `changed: false` for identical content.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_strReplace
tools.description: Atomically applies ordered exact-string edits to up to 50 files and 200 edits in total as one head version. Each `oldStr` must match once unless `replaceAll` is true, and any failing edit aborts the whole call. Set `dryRun` to validate and count replacements without committing. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_files_delete
tools.description: Deletes one head file while preserving history. Address named files by `type` and `name`, and singletons by `type`; takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_pages_editRoute
tools.description: Rewrites and normalizes a page's `definePage` route literal. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_metadata_edit
tools.description: Replaces a page's complete metadata object when `page` is sent, otherwise the site defaults in `website_config`. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_head_check
tools.description: Runs the publish-time framework quality gate without changing source: format, typecheck, lint, build, and a server-render of every page using placeholder content synthesized from the CMS schema. Failures return `ok: false` with diagnostics, and pages that compiled but threw while rendering in `renderFailures`. No lease is required and no CMS content is read, so the outcome depends only on source and schema.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_deployment_status
tools.description: Returns the preview revision, available page routes, publish availability, and build state for the selected head or published source version. Fails with 404 when `target=published` is requested for a never-published website.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_deployment_ensure
tools.description: Returns an existing non-failed deployment for the selected version or builds one. Poll status when another request is already building it.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_head_publish
tools.description: Validates, builds, and publishes head. Canonical formatting may create a new head first. Pass the `version` the check returned to refuse publishing a draft that changed since. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_head_restore
tools.description: Copies an earlier version or `published` into a new head without publishing or rewriting history. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_published_unpublish
tools.description: Takes the website offline without changing its draft source or version history. The unchanged head can be published again later. No edit lease is required.

tools.name: websiteSourceCode_published_rollback
tools.description: Validates and republishes an earlier version as a new head and published version, preserving history. Takes the edit lease when no `leaseToken` is sent.

tools.name: websitePreview_capture
tools.description: Renders one page of the site in a real browser and returns the image, so you can check layout, spacing, and responsive behaviour that source-level checks cannot see. `path` is site-relative and may include a query string, so dynamic routes are captured with real values rather than placeholders. Focus the capture with `selector` (plus optional `padding` for surrounding context) or a `clip` rectangle in CSS pixels from the top-left of the page; the region is scrolled into view and captured within the configured viewport, so it must fit inside it, and these options exclude each other and `fullPage`. Fonts, images, and (for `fullPage`) lazy content are awaited before the capture, and CSS animations are fast-forwarded to their end state by default. Fails with 409 when the draft build is still in progress or has failed; poll `websiteSourceCode.deployment.status` and retry.

tools.name: cms_schema_snapshot
tools.description: Returns every active collection and field of a website in one call — the full content model. Collections are ordered newest first; fields are grouped by collection in display order. Use this to discover the schema before reading or writing items.

tools.name: cms_collections_create
tools.description: Creates a collection in the website’s CMS. `slug` uses lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (max 64 characters, starting with a letter) and must be unique among the website’s active collections; `displayName` is 1–200 characters and `description` up to 2,000. Optionally pass `fields` (up to 100, same shape as the create-field body) to define the schema in the same call. A website can hold at most 100 active collections; the limit is enforced with a conflict error.

tools.name: cms_collections_update
tools.description: Updates `displayName` (1–200 characters), `description` (up to 2,000 characters; pass `null` to clear), and/or `slug` (a rename). A slug change fails with a conflict when another active collection in the website already uses it, and when the website has a published version the rename is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when it would break them.

tools.name: cms_collections_delete
tools.description: Soft-deletes the collection, making it and all of its items unreachable through the API; the slug becomes reusable. Refused with a conflict while any reference field in another collection targets this collection — delete those fields first. If the website has a published version, the deletion is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when the site still depends on the collection.

tools.name: cms_fields_create
tools.description: Adds a typed field at the end of the collection’s field order. `key` is lowercase snake_case (max 64 characters), must be unique in the collection, and cannot use the reserved metadata names `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `position`; `type` is immutable after creation. `reference` and `multi_reference` fields require a `targetCollectionId` in the same website, and `option` fields require `config.choices` (1–1,000 choices). A collection can hold at most 100 fields, and `required: true` is rejected while the collection has active items — add the field as optional, backfill every item, then mark it required.

tools.name: cms_fields_update
tools.description: Updates `displayName`, `description`, `required`, `isUnique`, `example`, and (for `option` fields only) `config`; `type` and `targetCollectionId` are immutable. Setting `required: true` is rejected until every active item has a valid value for the field. Setting `isUnique: true` enforces uniqueness on all future writes and fails with a conflict when existing values already collide; unique is not supported for `plain_text`, `markdown`, `multi_reference`, `image`, `gallery`, or `file` fields. Pass `key` to rename the field’s key: the key is atomically migrated in every stored item’s `data` in the same transaction (no values are lost), a conflict is returned when the new key is already used in the collection, and when the website has a published version the rename is validated against the published site’s content queries. Pass `position: "first"` or `"last"`, or `"before"` / `"after"` together with `anchorFieldId`, to move the field within the collection’s display order.

tools.name: cms_fields_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes the field and its stored values: the key is stripped from every item’s `data`, and reference or asset attachments made through the field are removed. This cannot be undone. If the website has a published version, the deletion is validated against the published site’s content queries and rejected when the site still depends on the field.

tools.name: cms_items_list
tools.description: Returns the collection’s active items in manual (drag) order by default, 20 per page (max 100); paginate with `cursor` or with 1-based `page` offsets, not both. Filter with `published` (`true` / `false`) and a JSON-encoded `filter` map of `{ fieldKey: { operator: value } }` — operators `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `nin`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, and `exists`, plus `slug` equality on reference fields; metadata keys are `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. Combine clauses with `filterLogic` (`and` by default, or `or`). `search` accepts a query string (1–200 characters) or JSON `{ "query", "fields" }` to restrict which text fields are searched; `sort` accepts JSON `{ "kind": "field" | "meta", "field", "direction": "asc" | "desc" }`, where sortable metadata fields are `id`, `slug`, `publishedAt`, `publishAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and `position`. `depth` (0–3, default 0) embeds referenced items in place of their ids, one level per unit.

tools.name: cms_items_get
tools.description: Returns one item, looked up by `itemId` or by the `collectionId` + `slug` pair (provide exactly one of the two). The `data` object is complete and schema-shaped: every currently-defined field is present and missing optional values read as `null`. `depth` (0–3, default 0) embeds referenced items in place of their ids, one level per unit; referenced items that were deleted read as `null` (single reference) or are omitted from arrays (multi-reference). Set `published` to `"true"` or `"false"` to match only a published or only a draft item (a mismatch reads as not found). List items that reference it with `cms.items.backreferences.list`.

tools.name: cms_items_backreferences_list
tools.description: Lists active items that reference the target item through a `reference` or `multi_reference` field, newest first, with cursor pagination (default 20 per page, maximum 100). Each source item appears once even when multiple fields point to the target. `depth` (0–3, default 0) controls reference hydration in the returned source items.

tools.name: cms_items_create
tools.description: Creates an item at the end of the collection’s manual order. Scalar values go in `data` keyed by field key and are validated against the field types — unknown keys are rejected, required fields must be present, `plain_text` and `markdown` are capped at 1,048,576 bytes (markdown must not contain raw HTML), `date` values are ISO 8601 with timezone, and `color` values are normalized to hex. Relationship and asset values go in the side maps: `references` (`reference`: an item id; `multi_reference`: an ordered array of up to 1,000 ids), `images` (`image`: an asset id or `{ assetId, altText }`; `gallery`: an ordered array of up to 25 of those), and `files` (`file`: an asset id or `{ assetId }`). `slug` is optional — it is derived from `data.title` or `data.name` when omitted. Set a non-future `publishedAt` to create an already-published item, or a future `publishAt` to schedule it; the two fields are mutually exclusive.

tools.name: cms_items_update
tools.description: Patches an item; omitted fields are left untouched. Keys in `data` are merged into the existing values and validated the same way as on create, while each key provided in `references`, `images`, or `files` replaces that field’s value wholesale — pass `null` (or `[]` for multi-valued fields) to clear an optional field. `slug` renames the item’s slug; slug and unique-field collisions fail with a conflict. Pass `position: "first"` or `"last"`, or `"before"` / `"after"` together with `anchorItemId`, to move the item within the collection’s manual order — the default sort for item lists.

tools.name: cms_items_setPublished
tools.description: Use exactly one publication action: `published: true` publishes immediately and sets `publishedAt` to now; a future `publishAt` schedules a draft for automatic publication; `published: false` unpublishes an item or cancels its schedule. A published item must be unpublished before it can be scheduled because CMS items do not have revision snapshots. Published websites read only items with an actual `publishedAt`, so immediate and scheduled promotion become visible without a site republish. Repeating the same action is idempotent.

tools.name: cms_items_delete
tools.description: Soft-deletes the item: it disappears from reads, list results, and backreferences, and fields referencing it read `null` (single reference) or shrink (multi-reference). Its slug becomes reusable, and incoming references are preserved so the item can be restored.

tools.name: cms_items_restore
tools.description: Restores a soft-deleted item, making it readable again and re-exposing references to and from it. Returns 404 when the item is not currently deleted.

tools.name: websiteAnalytics_query_get
tools.description: Returns aggregate engagement totals — page views, distinct visitors, visits, bounces, and total time in seconds — for a date range, optionally broken down by one dimension. Use it to answer "how much traffic did the site get" and "what are the top pages/referrers/countries" style questions; use the timeseries endpoint when you need values over time instead. `startAt` and `endAt` are Unix epoch milliseconds; optional filter parameters (path, referrer, country, event, UTM fields, ...) narrow the data. Without `dimension` the response carries the totals alone. With `dimension` (e.g. `path` for top pages, `referrer` for top referrers, `country` for top countries) the response also carries `rows`: up to `limit` (default 25, max 1000) values of that dimension ranked by page views, each with its own engagement totals. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); all-zero totals until the website is published and has traffic.

tools.name: websiteAnalytics_timeseries_get
tools.description: Returns one traffic time series bucketed by `unit` (`year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, or `minute`). `series` selects which: `pageviews` returns parallel `pageviews` and `sessions` arrays with one point per time bucket (and accepts `compare` — `prev` or `yoy` — to request comparison data for the previous period or year), while `events` returns tracked custom-event counts as one `events` point per event name per time bucket. Only the requested series' fields are present in the response. `startAt` and `endAt` are Unix epoch milliseconds; `timezone` is an IANA name (e.g. `America/New_York`) that controls bucket boundaries; optional filter parameters narrow the data. The series is capped to the most recent `maxPoints` time buckets (default 30, max 500); a `truncated` field reports when the cap was applied. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); empty until the website is published and has traffic.

tools.name: websiteAnalytics_realtime_get
tools.description: Returns a compact snapshot of traffic over Umami's trailing 30-minute realtime window: total page views, distinct visitors, tracked custom events, and distinct countries, plus the snapshot timestamp. The visitor total is not directly comparable to the removed `active` endpoint's five-minute count. Use it to see recent activity; use the query endpoint for historical ranges. Requires a plan that includes analytics (403 otherwise); all-zero totals until the website is published and has traffic.

tools.name: websiteForms_list
tools.description: Returns every form with inbox and spam counts, whether the published site still references it, who it notifies, the number of inbox submissions since the caller last opened the Forms tab, and monthly usage against the Free plan limit (`limit` is null on paid plans). Forms come from `<form method="post" action="/_cactal/forms/<name>">` in the website source and appear here as soon as the draft or published build contains them, before any submission.

tools.name: websiteForms_submissions_list
tools.description: Returns submissions newest first as a cursor-paginated page. Filter by `form` name, `status` (`inbox` by default, or `spam`), and `source` (`published` for real visitors, `draft` for test submissions from the draft preview). Items carry the fields in submitted order, the inferred submitter email and name, page, spam signals, classifier verdict, and notification state. Submission data is personal information: never render it on the public website.

tools.name: websiteForms_submissions_get
tools.description: Returns one submission with its fields in submitted order.

tools.name: websiteForms_submissions_setStatus
tools.description: Moves a submission between the inbox and the spam folder. Restoring to `inbox` sends the notification email if it was never sent. Spam is deleted automatically after 30 days.

tools.name: websiteForms_submissions_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes one submission.

tools.name: websiteForms_recipients_add
tools.description: Adds an email address to one form, identified by its name from the action path. New forms notify the organization owners until changed. Organization members and website editors receive submissions immediately; other addresses get a confirmation email (link valid 7 days). `member` and `confirmed` addresses receive email; `pending` addresses must confirm by link; `failing` addresses bounced or complained; `stopped` addresses opted out. Works before the first submission; at most 20 addresses per website.

tools.name: websiteForms_recipients_remove
tools.description: Stops emailing an address for one form. A form with no recipients emails nobody; its submissions still reach the Forms inbox.

tools.name: websiteForms_recipients_resend
tools.description: Issues a fresh confirmation link to a pending, failing, or stopped address.

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the Cactal product documentation: concepts, guides, agent workflows, platform limits, and the API reference. Returns matching Markdown excerpts with page paths; read a full page with the docs read operation. Consult the docs before non-trivial or unfamiliar work such as source-code editing, publishing, or CMS schema changes.

tools.name: docs_read
tools.description: Read one Cactal documentation page as Markdown. Pass a page path from docs search results, for example "concepts/publishing" or "agents/agent-safe-publishing". Pass "llms.txt" for an index of every page with titles and descriptions.

tools.name: skills_read
tools.description: Read the matching Cactal skill before acting: source-editing-workflow before source edits, design-direction for design, copywriting for words. Required skills are included.  - accessibility-audit: Check a site's accessibility and fix what fails - analytics: Traffic, visitors, referrers, and other analytics reports - assets-and-media: Find, import, or place images, video, fonts, favicons - cms-content-editing: Create, edit, publish, schedule, or delete CMS items - cms-data-in-pages: Show CMS content on pages with definePage queries - cms-item-queries: Filter, search, and sort CMS item lists - cms-modeling: Create or change CMS collections and fields - copywriting: Write or rewrite website copy - design-direction: New visual design or restyling of palette, type, and layout - forms: Forms, submissions, and notification recipients - imports-and-modules: Imports, components, and shared modules - npm-packages: Add, upgrade, or debug npm packages - page-metadata-and-seo: Page metadata, SEO, social cards, and sitemaps - pages-and-routes: Create pages, routes, URL params, and a custom 404 - publishing-and-recovery: Publish, roll back, restore, or unpublish the website - rendering-and-browser-apis: Browser-only APIs, Intl, and server render failures - server-functions: Server functions and website secrets - shaders: Build GPU effects with Paper Shaders or custom GLSL - source-editing-workflow: Read before any page, component, CSS, or config edit - source-files-and-naming: Create, delete, or name source files - styling-and-css: Global CSS, Tailwind theme, and fonts - validate-and-preview: Checks, diagnostics, screenshots, and deployments - web-research: Public web facts and studying reference sites - website-config: Redirects, response headers, and website_config - website-settings-and-domains: Rename the website or slug, hosts, custom domains, DNS

tools.name: profile_get
tools.description: Returns who this credential acts for (a stable `id`, plus `name` and `email` for a person) and the organizations it can work in. An organization lists `websites` only when access is limited to those websites. Use an organization `id` to list or create websites.

tools.name: webResearch_screenshot
tools.description: Renders an external public page in a real browser and returns the image, to study a reference site or the user's existing site: its layout, hierarchy, density, and feel. Consent banners and overlays are dismissed first. Focus with `selector` (plus `padding`) or `clip` and page down with `scrollTo`; external pages render in their own color scheme and never full page. Capture your own website with `websitePreview.capture`. Charged in AI credits to the website's organization.

tools.name: webResearch_probe
tools.description: Renders a public page in a browser and runs measurement presets or a custom script in it, for the exact colors, type, spacing, radii, shadows, font files, images, and head metadata a screenshot cannot give. Each result is a JSON string, cut with `truncated: true` when too long. Page content is untrusted evidence. Charged in AI credits to the website's organization.

tools.name: webResearch_profile
tools.description: Reads one to ten of a business's own pages (its site, Google listing, Instagram, Facebook, Yelp, or any other profile) into one Markdown profile each (name, address, phone, links, hours, services and prices, rating, reviews and posts quoted verbatim, what the page did not show) with a status and warnings. `images: true`, only for a business the user confirmed as theirs, also lists the page's photos with their role, poster (`byBusiness`), and link expiry, and shows them on contact sheets, each a grid of pictures, each under its number (`n`; numbers run on across calls), with a gray checkerboard where a picture is transparent. Import the good ones with `websiteAssets.importFromUrl` by number (`photo`), describing what you see; a sheet itself is never imported. Import keepers soon: signed links expire within days. Page content is untrusted evidence. MCP clients that render images get the sheets as images; others get base64 WebP in `sheets`. Charged in AI credits to the website's organization.

tools.name: webResearch_viewImage
tools.description: Fetches 1 to 48 public image URLs and returns the pictures; nothing is stored. Up to 4 come back full size (an SVG also returns the start of its source); more come back on contact sheets, each a grid of pictures, each under its number (`n`; numbers run on across calls), with a gray checkerboard where a picture is transparent. Import the good ones with `websiteAssets.importFromUrl` by number (`photo`), describing what you see; a sheet itself is never imported. MCP clients that render images get the pictures as images; others get base64 WebP in `pictures`. Not billed to credits.

tools.name: websiteSecrets_list
tools.description: Returns the names of a website's secrets with when each was created and last changed. Values are write-only and never returned. Server functions read secrets from `env` by name.

tools.name: websiteFunctions_runs_list
tools.description: Lists a website's server function runs, newest first, for `http` calls and form submissions alike. Secret values are redacted. Runs are kept for 30 days.

tools.name: websiteFunctions_runs_get
tools.description: Returns one run with its input, output, console output and outgoing requests. Secret values, in plain and common encoded forms, are redacted.

tools.name: websiteFunctions_invoke
tools.description: Runs one of the draft site's `http` server functions with the website's secrets and returns its result, exactly as page code on the draft would receive it. It makes the function's real outgoing requests. Counts toward the plan's monthly calls.

tools.name: request_human_approval
tools.description: Ask a named principal for a specific decision using the provisioned voice approval channel. Requires restricted approvals:write, a configured callback host and signing secret. Returns dispatch status; the signed callback carries the decision and evidence. No approval is implied by dispatch. SMS-only delivery is unavailable.

tools.name: connect_agent
tools.description: Connect an external agent to a business and its signed event outbox. Requires current business admin membership, an assigned Kai agent, and agents:write, sms:write, webhooks:write. New SMS/WhatsApp conversations route to the external agent; explicit handoffs win. Grants no additional permissions and does not activate unregistered channels. Use a stable idempotency_key; replacements require expected_revision. The signing secret is returned only for a non-replayed connect. External realtime voice and email execution are not connected by this operation.

tools.name: get_agent_connection
tools.description: Discover the external agent connection, signed webhook configuration, scoped API operation catalog, channel readiness and remaining runtime requirements. Requires agents:read, sms:read and webhooks:read. Configuration does not prove delivery or recipient consent.

tools.name: disconnect_agent
tools.description: Disconnect the external agent and disable its webhook atomically. Requires current business admin membership and agents:write, sms:write, webhooks:write. Pass the stored expected_revision. Inherited conversations return to Kai; explicit handoffs remain.

tools.name: get_lsa_account_report
tools.description: Read the authorized advertiser's live Google Local Services aggregate account report, including actual spend, currency and charged lead totals. Requires linked manager-account access. Dates are calendar dates inclusive at both ends. Source may lag by 30 minutes. Connected phone calls means duration over 30 seconds; responsiveness is the previous 90 days. This is not signed-case revenue or lead-rating reporting.

tools.name: get_lsa_setup
tools.description: Inspect Google LSA account selection and sync freshness, with setup steps. Saved configuration never proves a live workflow. Cloud-project production access is not shown here; Google Cloud reports it.

tools.name: sync_lsa
tools.description: Sync an explicitly selected connected LSA advertiser. Requires current business admin role. Syncing runs lead ingestion, and existing business speed-to-lead configuration may contact the new leads it finds.

tools.name: list_lsa_leads
tools.description: List synced Google LSA leads, charge and credit states, source IDs and rating details. The returned LSA lead id identifies the lead in LSA commands; the separate lead_id field links to the CRM.

tools.name: get_lsa_conversations
tools.description: Read the latest 200 synced Google LSA conversation events for an LSA lead, including customer and advertiser messages. History is as current as the last sync.

tools.name: get_lsa_report
tools.description: Report LSA lead counts, types, observed statuses, ratings and credit counts for an explicit UTC window (start inclusive, end exclusive). Includes sync freshness and completeness. Removed unrated leads are counted separately because they cannot be rated here. Financial amounts, signed cases and response-time metrics are unavailable in this source and cannot be derived from counts.

tools.name: send_lsa_reply
tools.description: Send an authorized text reply inside an existing Google LSA message lead through the Ads API. This contacts the customer. Requires current business admin role and a stable idempotency_key. A retry with the same key is deduplicated; pending/unknown writes are blocked. Provider acceptance does not prove customer delivery. Attachments are unsupported.

tools.name: rate_lsa_lead
tools.description: Submit an authorized, truthful Google LSA quality survey and return Google's actual bonus-credit decision. This is not a guaranteed refund or the retired manual dispute workflow. Requires admin role and a stable retry key. Each rating is a per-lead survey answer based on that lead, not a bulk dissatisfaction claim. The reason must match the positive/negative rating; OTHER requires a comment. Neutral takes no reason.

tools.name: get_callrail
tools.description: Read a business's CallRail call-tracking setup. action=status returns the connected CallRail account, which CallRail companies feed which business, every company the saved key can see (with its company_id), and the businesses you can link them to. action=list_trackers (with link_id from status) returns that company's tracking numbers, where each one rings now, and whether it already rings a KaiCalls line. If nothing is connected yet, ask the person for their CallRail API key and use manage_callrail connect.

tools.name: manage_callrail
tools.description: Connect CallRail call tracking to a business's line. Order: (1) connect {api_key, account_id?}; (2) get_callrail status lists the companies the key can see; (3) link_company {company_id, target_business_id?} once per business; (4) set_writeback {enabled}; (5) get_callrail list_trackers; (6) route_tracker only after the owner says yes. The API key: the person may paste their CallRail API v3 key straight into this chat. Take it and pass it as api_key; do not send them elsewhere to paste it. KaiCalls stores it encrypted and never returns it. One agency-level key serves every company that CallRail login can see, so connect once and link each firm with its own link_company. They create the key in CallRail under Integrations > API Keys > Create API V3 Key, signed in as a login that can see every company to link. CallRail shows the key only once. If they would rather paste it themselves: https://www.kaicalls.com/dashboard/settings/connections?connector=callrail. If connect answers choose_account, call it again with one of the returned account ids. link_company subscribes that CallRail company's calls: calls Kai answers get the CallRail source, campaign, keyword and landing page, and Kai's outcome is written back to CallRail as a KaiCalls tag, a summary note and good_lead when Kai qualified the caller. route_tracker {link_id, tracker_id, mode} changes where a live tracking number rings: mode kai_answers sends every call to Kai; business_first sends it to a KaiCalls line that rings the owner first so Kai takes only the misses. restore_tracker puts the earlier destination back. Leaving numbers unrouted is tracking-only. unlink_company {link_id}; disconnect. Requires current admin role on every business involved. Changing a tracker changes a live phone line: confirm with the owner first.

tools.name: get_nimbata
tools.description: Read a business's Nimbata call-tracking setup: the connected Nimbata account, which Nimbata projects feed which business (with when each last synced and how many calls matched), the projects the saved token can see, and the businesses you can link them to.

tools.name: manage_nimbata
tools.description: Connect Nimbata call tracking to a business's line. connect {api_token} checks and saves a Nimbata personal API token (Agency plan; one token can serve many businesses). link_project {project_id, target_business_id?} attaches that Nimbata project's calls to a business and adds KaiCalls tags to the project: calls Kai answers get Nimbata's source, UTM and click ids, and Kai's outcome is written back to the Nimbata call as a KaiCalls tag, a KaiCalls qualified tag when Kai qualified the caller, and a summary comment. unlink_project {link_id}; set_writeback {enabled}; disconnect. Requires current admin role on every business involved. Routing stays in Nimbata: add the KaiCalls number to the project's call flow there.

tools.name: agency_profile_bootstrap
tools.description: Registers a new agency for the signed-in user and makes them its owner, using the given brand and support details. Requires a signed-in user session with a verified email; an API key cannot create an agency. Repeating it for an agency that already exists does not create a second one.

tools.name: agency_profile_update
tools.description: Replaces the agency brand, support details and requested commercial mode. Requires an agency owner or admin and the current profile revision; a stale revision is rejected. It does not change any published offer.

tools.name: agency_profile_invite
tools.description: Creates a staff invitation for an email address with the admin, operator or reader role and returns a one-time invite link that expires in 7 days. Requires an agency owner or admin; only the owner can invite an admin. It sends no email; the returned link is delivered by whoever created the invite.

tools.name: agency_profile_accept_invite
tools.description: Joins the agency using the token from an invite link. The signed-in user must have a verified email that matches the invited address, and the invite must be unexpired and not revoked. Accepting the same invite again is a no-op.

tools.name: agency_profile_revoke_invite
tools.description: Cancels a pending staff invitation so its link can no longer be used. Requires an agency owner or admin. It does not remove anyone who already accepted; revoke_member does that.

tools.name: agency_profile_assign
tools.description: Gives an active agency staff member access to one client business with the admin or member business role. Requires an agency owner or admin who can manage that client; only the owner can assign an admin staff member. Assigning an existing assignment again changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_profile_unassign
tools.description: Removes a staff member's agency assignment to one client business, and removes the business membership if this assignment created it. Requires an agency owner or admin; only the owner can unassign an admin. It does not remove the person from the agency.

tools.name: agency_profile_revoke_member
tools.description: Removes a staff member from the agency: revokes their membership, all their client assignments, their accepted invites and every API key issued to them through the agency. Requires an agency owner or admin; only the owner can remove an admin, and the owner cannot be removed.

tools.name: agency_profile_issue_key
tools.description: Creates a new API key for yourself in this agency, limited to the requested scopes, and returns the secret once. Readers cannot get write scopes, only the agency owner can get billing:write, and a delegated key cannot issue a key broader than itself. Each call creates another key (up to 20 active per user).

tools.name: agency_offer_save
tools.description: Creates a new offer draft, or replaces an existing draft when offerId and its current revision are given. Requires an agency owner or admin. Saving changes only the draft; clients see nothing until it is published.

tools.name: agency_offer_preview
tools.description: Builds the publishable manifest and sales kit for an offer draft and returns its fingerprint and revision for publishing. Requires an agency owner or admin. It saves nothing and fails if a package release, variant or claim is not supported.

tools.name: agency_offer_publish
tools.description: Publishes the previewed offer as a new immutable version and returns its enrollment link. Requires an agency owner or admin, plus the fingerprint and revision from preview; partner-billed offers also need billing collection to be ready. Publishing the same fingerprint again returns the existing version.

tools.name: agency_offer_archive
tools.description: Archives an offer so it can no longer be published or used for new enrollments. Requires an agency owner or admin and the current offer revision. Existing installations are not removed.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_start_self_service
tools.description: Starts a business owner's own enrollment in a published agency offer, using the business name and intake facts. Requires a signed-in user session with a verified email and an idempotency key; the same key replays the same session. Nothing is installed until the owner approves and finishes.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_finish_self_service
tools.description: Completes a self-service enrollment after the owner has approved the current intake: creates the client business and queues its package installations, which later configure the business's voice agent. Only the owner who started it can finish it. Repeating it returns the recorded result.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_owner_save
tools.description: Lets the client owner replace the intake facts on their own enrollment link. Requires the owner who claimed the link and the session's current revision. Saving clears any earlier owner approval, so the owner must approve again.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_create
tools.description: Creates an enrollment session for 1-50 existing or new clients against a published offer version and returns one owner approval link per new client. Requires an agency owner, admin or operator with access to each existing client, and an idempotency key; a replay returns the session without the links. It sends no email and installs nothing.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_save
tools.description: Replaces the client entries of an uncommitted enrollment session. Requires the session creator (or an agency owner/admin) and the current session revision. Saving revokes all outstanding owner approval links for the batch, so owners must be sent new links.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_preview
tools.description: Checks every client in the batch for missing facts, owner approval and payer conflicts, and returns what enrolling would install, with the fingerprint and approval IDs needed to enroll. Requires an agency owner, admin or operator. It records the preview on the session but installs nothing.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_enroll
tools.description: Commits the previewed batch: creates new client businesses, records owner approvals and queues package installations for every ready client; installations later configure each client voice agent. Requires an agency owner, admin or operator who created the session, its idempotency key, and the fingerprint and revision from preview. Clients that are not ready are reported with their next step instead of being installed.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_claim_owner
tools.description: Links the signed-in client owner to their enrollment link using its token. The user's verified email must match the owner email on the link. It approves nothing.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_approve_owner
tools.description: Records the client owner's approval of the exact offer and intake facts on their enrollment link. Requires the owner who claimed the link, the session's current revision and its fingerprint. It does not enroll; the agency still enrolls the batch.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_rotate_owner_link
tools.description: Issues a new owner link for a client in the batch and invalidates the old one, clearing any earlier claim and approval. Requires the session creator (or an agency owner/admin) and the link's current revision. It sends nothing; the returned link is delivered by whoever re-issued it.

tools.name: agency_enrollment_revoke
tools.description: Revokes an enrollment session and all of its owner links so nothing more can be approved or enrolled from it. Requires the session creator or an agency owner/admin. Installations that were already enrolled are not removed.

tools.name: agency_installation_preview_route_receipt
tools.description: Returns the evidence that a real call reached the client's voice line and produced a delivered lead notification, with a fingerprint for acknowledgement. Only for voice intake installations whose training is complete, and only the client owner who received that notification can view it. It changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_approve_route_receipt
tools.description: Records the client owner acknowledging the route test receipt they reviewed. Requires the client owner who received the notification and the fingerprint from preview_route_receipt. It does not place any call.

tools.name: agency_installation_preview_handoff
tools.description: Returns the staff handoff for an installation with a fingerprint for approval. Requires client membership or agency assignment to the client. It changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_approve_handoff
tools.description: Records the client owner approving the exact staff handoff they reviewed. Requires the client owner and the fingerprint from preview_handoff.

tools.name: agency_installation_resolve_update
tools.description: Chooses, for each conflicting setting in a proposed package update, whether to keep the client's current value or use the package value, and saves the resolved update. Requires the client owner and the update's fingerprint; client facts cannot be overridden this way. It does not apply the update, and the resolved version needs fresh owner approval.

tools.name: agency_installation_run_scenarios
tools.description: Run approved verification scenarios for an existing client installation at its expected revision using voice agent compute under existing entitlement. Requires current assigned client authority, current owner approval and evals:write. Saves test evidence and can incur irreversible usage charges; a new request key can run and charge again. Makes no real customer calls.

tools.name: agency_installation_owner_preview
tools.description: Shows the client owner the exact intake facts and voice script prepared for their business, with the hashes needed to approve each. Only the client owner can view it, and only after the agency prepared a complete preview. It changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_approve
tools.description: Records the client owner approving either the intake facts or the voice script they reviewed. Requires the client owner and the matching hash from owner_preview. It does not install anything by itself.

tools.name: agency_installation_revoke_approval
tools.description: Withdraws one of the client owner's earlier approvals. Requires the client owner. Work that depends on that approval waits until it is approved again.

tools.name: agency_installation_pause
tools.description: Pauses an installation so its package setup and scheduled package work stop. Requires agency write access to the client or the client owner, and the current revision. It does not delete anything; use retry to queue it again.

tools.name: agency_installation_retry
tools.description: Re-queues an installation so setup runs again, clearing its last error; setup configures the client's voice agent. Requires agency write access to the client or the client owner, and the current revision.

tools.name: agency_installation_export
tools.description: Returns the installation release, intake facts, approved script, staff sheet and checks for handoff or records. Requires client membership or agency assignment to the client. It changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_preview_offboard
tools.description: Shows what offboarding would stop and what it keeps (phone number, sender, connections, billing plan and history), with a fingerprint for approval. Only the client owner can view it. It changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_offboard
tools.description: Starts offboarding: stops the package's jobs, revokes its future automation authority and turns off its scheduled reports. Requires the client owner, accepted set to true and the fingerprint from preview_offboard. The phone number, connections, billing plan and history are kept.

tools.name: agency_installation_preview_update
tools.description: Prepares a proposed update to a newer published offer version, or a rollback to an earlier installation revision, and lists any conflicts with client changes. Requires agency write access to the client or the client owner. It saves the proposal for review but does not apply it; client facts are always kept.

tools.name: agency_installation_approve_update
tools.description: Records the client owner approving the updated script of a proposed update. Requires the client owner, the updateId and its fingerprint. It does not apply the update.

tools.name: agency_installation_apply_update
tools.description: Applies an approved update and re-queues setup, which replaces the client's live voice agent configuration. Requires agency write access or the client owner, a resolved update with no open conflicts, fresh owner approval, and (unless this client is the canary) an active canary on the same release. Applying an already-applied update changes nothing.

tools.name: agency_installation_opt_into_canary
tools.description: Marks the client's installation as a canary, so it can receive package updates before other clients of the same agency. Requires the client owner and accepted set to true. It applies no update by itself.

tools.name: agency_report_generate
tools.description: Generate and save an activity report snapshot for an existing client installation at its expected revision. Requires current client membership and agency access. Queues report email for due owner-approved subscriptions to existing verified client members and advances their schedule; queued does not mean delivered.

tools.name: agency_report_configure
tools.description: Sets the weekly or monthly activity report email schedule for an installation and replaces the previous recipient list. Requires the client owner; recipients must be verified members of the client's business. The first report is sent by the scheduled job, not by this call.

tools.name: agency_billing_record_adjustment
tools.description: Record an already-issued provider credit note or debit invoice against an existing agency billing line. Platform finance operators only: requires the existing admin key and wildcard scope; agency owner status is insufficient. Verifies exact provider receipt, currency and amount before recording bookkeeping. Creates no invoice, payment or subscription.

tools.name: agency_billing_set_plan
tools.description: Puts a partner-created client on an agency-billed plan, or stops it when plan is null. Requires the agency owner who is also a client admin; starting a plan needs accepted terms and a ready collection method. Stopping parks the client service, which detaches its phone numbers from the voice agent under the existing parking policy.

tools.name: agency_billing_set_automatic_collection
tools.description: Turns monthly automatic collection of wholesale charges on or off under the accepted terms. Requires the agency owner and accepted terms; it cannot be turned off while any client is on an active partner plan. It charges nothing by itself.

tools.name: agency_billing_publish_terms
tools.description: Publishes a new set of wholesale commercial terms (discount, grace days, document and start date) for one agency, or for all agencies when partnerId is null. Platform commercial operators only. Each call publishes another version; agencies must still accept it.

tools.name: agency_billing_accept_terms
tools.description: Accepts published wholesale terms for the agency and applies their discount. Requires the agency owner, and the terms must be in effect and apply to this agency. It charges nothing and doesn't set up payment.

tools.name: agency_billing_setup_collection
tools.description: Creates the agency's customer record at the payment provider if needed and returns a hosted link where the owner adds a payment method. Requires the agency owner and accepted terms. It charges nothing, and the method is ready only after the provider confirms it.

tools.name: agency_billing_freeze_period
tools.description: Calculates and locks the wholesale statement for one closed calendar month (UTC) from the agency's billable client intervals. Requires the agency owner. Freezing the same month again returns the same period; it does not charge.

tools.name: agency_care_preview_review
tools.description: Shows the exact review-request text, sender number and recipients for customers with a completed service, with a fingerprint for approval. Requires the client owner, the sms:write scope, and an SMS review installation where Kai is confirmed as the review tool. It sends nothing and saves nothing.

tools.name: agency_care_prepare_review
tools.description: Saves the approved review-request texts as a draft campaign and reserves the listed customers. Requires the client owner, the sms:write scope, accepted set to true and the fingerprint from preview_review. It sends nothing; launch_review sends it.

tools.name: agency_care_launch_review
tools.description: Launches the approved review-request campaign, queuing text messages to the listed customers from the business number. Requires the client owner, the sms:write scope, accepted set to true and the fingerprint from preview_review. A campaign that is already sending can't be launched again.

tools.name: agency_support_acknowledge
tools.description: Marks an agency incident as acknowledged and assigns its follow-up to you. Requires an agency owner, admin or operator. It does not resolve the incident; recovery is confirmed separately.

tools.name: agency_support_measure
tools.description: Records time spent or money for one client (setup, support, fulfillment, provider cost or retail receipt) with a note. Requires an agency owner, admin or operator with write access to that client. Each call adds a new record.

tools.name: agency_support_complete_exercise
tools.description: Save completion evidence for a named operational exercise on an existing client installation. Requires current assigned client authority. Replaces any previous proof reference and completion time for that exercise; does not prove live customer delivery.

tools.name: agency_clients_set_client_alerts
tools.description: Changes one client's lead alerts: every lead or qualified leads only, whether the client gets KaiCalls product updates, and which emails and phones get the alerts. Requires write access to that client (agency owner/admin, or an operator assigned to it, who is also an admin on the client's account). Recorded in the client's change history. Sends nothing.

tools.name: agency_clients_set_client_profile
tools.description: Sets who your clients should contact about their line and one or two sentences on how you work with them. Shown in every client's dashboard. Requires an agency owner or admin. Sends nothing.

tools.name: agency_clients_set_activity_alerts
tools.description: Chooses which client activity you hear about (qualified leads, a caller texted one of a client's links, a client needing attention) and where those alerts go. With no emails set, alerts go to the agency owners. Requires an agency owner or admin. Changes future alerts only.

tools.name: get_agency_workspace
tools.description: Read assigned installations, grouped support incidents, accepted billing evidence (also billing:read), your clients (line, last 7 days of calls and qualified leads, each client's alert settings, what clients see about you and your own client-activity alerts), or inventory one authorized client's saved facts and actual channel readiness. Suggestions and unknowns remain explicit.

tools.name: request_extra_number
tools.description: Reserve an exact pool number and request an owner-only browser review of its recurring extra-line price. Requires numbers:write and billing:write. It never charges included or prepaid capacity; included allocation goes through attach_number. This tool does not approve payment or prove activation.

tools.name: get_extra_number_status
tools.description: Read an owner-authorized extra-number request. Billing, assignment and live activation are distinct. Unknown checkout or provider outcomes retain the original request and number, so no replacement purchase is needed or started.

tools.name: retry_setup
tools.description: Reconcile database pointers for an existing imported signup phone reservation. Owner-only, entitlement-checked, single-flight and idempotent. Never creates agents, buys numbers, changes provider routing or sends messages. PBX, missing imports, and stale claims return review blockers. Reusing the same key reads or replays the outcome; a failed request is held for review before a new key is accepted. Ready means database agreement, not activation.

tools.name: get_setup_recovery_status
tools.description: Read an owner-authorized setup recovery request by its business and idempotency key. Running requests are never automatically stolen, including stale requests. A ready receipt does not prove live activation.

tools.name: make_call
tools.description: Place an outbound call through a KaiCalls AI agent: call back a customer who previously called this business, give the owner a voice preview, or call on the owner's behalf (a landlord, clinic, pharmacy, school or utility) with the task in context. For a customer callback, pass the existing lead_id and callback goal in context. Kai verifies the business's inbound-call consent for the exact destination; a verified callback can go directly to a cell phone without connecting the owner. Contact existence alone is not callback permission, and opt-outs still block calls. A call never proves inbound routing or advances activation. report_language sets the language the result is reported in, and Kai then confirms exact details for that reader; Kai speaks call_language (English by default) on the phone. A new account's first call to a US or Canada business line is free; after that the account needs a plan. Kai calls businesses, not personal cell phones, on a free call. To a number in a state where everyone on a call must know it is recorded, Kai's first words are that the call is recorded. For a business that answers on a cell phone, connect_me has Kai ring the person's own saved phone and connect them, so they do the talking. While the call runs, check_call_status shows its live_transcript and send_call_note steers Kai. hold_for_me has Kai wait on hold at a business and connect the person when someone answers. An idempotency_key makes the request safely retryable. Only `to` is required: with no agent_id the account's one agent places the call.

tools.name: check_call_status
tools.description: Check the status of a call by its ID: while it is live, the latest turns of the conversation (live_transcript) and any question Kai is waiting on (pending_question); after, a voicemail message left, or the business calling back. Also takes the intent_id of a call scheduled for calling hours and says when it goes out

tools.name: answer_call_question
tools.description: Send the person's answer to a live call's pending_question, or decline. Send only what they said; answered once.

tools.name: send_call_note
tools.description: Send Kai a short note on a live call it is making for the person, to steer it: a detail to mention, a question to add, a preference. Kai uses it on its next turn without reading it out. It never overrides Kai's honesty and disclosure rules. Up to 10 notes a call.

tools.name: join_call
tools.description: Join a live errand call. take_over connects the person's own phone; listen returns a signed-in dashboard link.

tools.name: list_recent_calls
tools.description: List and search the business's calls, newest first, each with who called (when known) and a short summary of what they wanted. Search by caller phone, by words in the call summary ("water heater", "quote"), and by date window; filters combine. Use get_transcript for the full call.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Get the transcript and summary of a completed call, plus its insights: Kai's lead score for the call, the caller's sentiment, the intake answers collected, who did the talking, and the lead journey (channel, landing page, first contact, number of calls).

tools.name: get_coaching
tools.description: Coach the business's agent. With call_id: what the agent did well and what to change on that call, each point with the caller's or agent's exact words, the second it happened, and a one-line rule that would fix it (teach it with teach_coaching_rule). Without call_id: the agent's recurring habits across recent calls (how often, example calls, and whether a rule taught for it has worked). Read-only.

tools.name: teach_coaching_rule
tools.description: Teach the agent one rule from a coaching point on a call (get_coaching gives the code and a suggested rule). The rule is added to a Coaching rules section of the agent's instructions through the governed update path, so it is versioned, in change history and can be rolled back; a business owner or admin signed in through this connector applies it right away, otherwise it waits for the owner. Then a test is built from that call and run, and the result says whether the agent now follows the rule.

tools.name: share_call_example
tools.description: Owner only: publish a finished errand call as a redacted transcript example (no audio, business shown as a category). Call once for a preview, show it, then confirm with its preview_hash.

tools.name: unshare_call_example
tools.description: Owner only: take a shared call example down.

tools.name: get_call_recording
tools.description: Get the real call recording URL for a call so reviewers can listen to the voice/audio instead of relying only on the transcript.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the KaiCalls agents on the authenticated account. Shows whether this business already has a secretary answering its calls.

tools.name: get_business_info
tools.description: Read back what a business already has: profile details, how many agents are configured, and recent call volume. This shows whether a business number that answers missed calls already exists. When the business has no working phone line yet, `next_step` names the tool that sets one up.

tools.name: get_operational_settings
tools.description: Read the business-level operational setup of a live account: staff alert recipients, SMS/email alert flags, escalation rules, textable send-link entries, and assigned agent voice/model/greeting metadata.

tools.name: configure_staff_alerts
tools.description: Save the business's alert contacts and post-call escalation rules. Read get_operational_settings first: each list you send (notification_phone, notification_email, escalation_rules) replaces the whole saved list, so include the entries to keep. Listed phones get after-call summary texts and escalation texts (one-recipient alerts go to the first phone); listed emails get escalation emails. lead_alerts chooses every lead or qualified leads only, and kaicalls_updates_enabled turns KaiCalls product and setup mail on or off (both default to quiet for a business a partner set up). Saving does not prove delivery.

tools.name: get_call_disclosures
tools.description: Read the recording notice and AI notice callers hear before the greeting, and when each plays: always, state_gated (only for callers in states whose law calls for it, e.g. all-party-consent states for recording), or never. Shows the defaults when the business has not set its own.

tools.name: set_call_disclosures
tools.description: Change the recording notice or AI notice callers hear before the greeting, or when each plays. The next call uses the new wording. Requires the business owner. Turning a notice to never can break recording or AI-disclosure law for callers in states that require one; state_gated is the safe default. Every change is logged with the previous value.

tools.name: get_call_companion
tools.description: Read whether the live call companion is on for the business: during a call the secretary texts the caller one page link and puts options, open times, a short details form or a deposit on it; the caller taps instead of spelling things out, the secretary hears what they picked, and after the call the same link shows their recap. Shows the state per assistant.

tools.name: set_call_companion
tools.description: Turn the live call companion on or off for every assistant of the business. On: during a call the secretary can text the caller a live page with options, open times, a details form or a deposit and hear what they tap. Payments on that page still need the business's own payments setting. Requires an admin of the business. The next call uses the change.

tools.name: get_page_branding
tools.description: Read the business's own look on the pages made for its calls (the live call companion and the caller's recap): name, logo, accent colour, which sites may embed those pages (the business's own website unless it lists others), the call-page domain's setup state (not_set, waiting_on_dns or live, with blockers, the DNS provider and the records to add), every domain the business has (email and pages, so all DNS is one visit), and next_step: one sentence saying what to do next.

tools.name: set_page_branding
tools.description: Put the business's own logo, colour and domain on the pages made for its calls, and choose which sites may embed them. from_website: true reads the logo and colour off the business's own homepage for anything not given. color is a hex like #0f766e (too-light colours are refused); null clears back to the default. Requires an admin of the business. Pages already sent pick it up on their next load.

tools.name: get_call_page
tools.description: Get a shareable page for one finished call, in the business's own branding: the customer-safe recap, next steps and what the caller picked (never notes, recordings or scoring). Returns a link to share, an embed_url for an iframe, and a ready-to-paste embed_html snippet. Each request makes a fresh link that works for 30 days.

tools.name: get_scam_screening
tools.description: Read how the business screens scam calls: the mode (off; label, the default, which answers every call and marks likely scams in the call log; or screen, which sends callers with a strong scam sign to a take-a-message screen), the numbers that are never screened, and the most recent calls caught as scams.

tools.name: set_scam_screening
tools.description: Change how the business screens scam calls, or which numbers are never screened. mode: off, label (default; nothing is blocked) or screen (callers with a strong scam sign, such as a caller ID the carrier could not verify or a number already caught scamming, get a short screen that takes their name and reason instead of the normal line). Known customers and the team are never screened. allowlist replaces the whole list. Requires an admin of the business. The next call uses the change.

tools.name: get_activation_status
tools.description: Read current call readiness and persisted private-test proof for one accessible business. Only a currently entitled owner with a coherent assigned number gets the existing private-test setup link. Missing entitlement, incomplete setup or stale sessions do not authorize a call. It cannot assert or advance proof. A completed private test is separate from customer-route coverage; forwarding is optional and does not define whether the assigned phone works.

tools.name: confirm_notification_destination
tools.description: APPROVAL-GATED. Save the owner-approved phone number (SMS) or email address where KaiCalls sends the owner the result of their first test call, for the exact active activation session. Once that test call's record is ready, KaiCalls sends a real text or email to that destination through its messaging provider; saving the destination alone is not proof anything was delivered. Replaces any destination saved earlier for the session.

tools.name: retry_activation_notification
tools.description: APPROVAL-GATED. Send the owner's activation notification again, as a real text or email through KaiCalls' messaging provider, for the exact active activation session. Only retries a channel whose last attempt failed or has waited long enough; an attempt whose outcome is unknown is never blindly resent. Requires a new idempotency_key.

tools.name: choose_customer_route
tools.description: APPROVAL-GATED. After private-test proof is complete, save forwarding, published_number, both, or testing. This unlocks the command center but does not claim customer coverage; selected customer routes remain pending until independently verified. Forwarding is optional; testing keeps the existing private-test result without connecting a customer route.

tools.name: configure_textable_links
tools.description: Create or repair the business_links entries used by the send_link/send_sms tools. These entries let callers receive booking, directions, cancellation, sister-location, or service-specific links by text without raw URLs in the voice prompt.

tools.name: configure_agent_business_rules
tools.description: Safely add or replace a named operational rules section inside an agent inbound prompt, then route the prompt patch through the governed agent.patch broker. It covers cross-business handoffs, callback language, alert promises, and client-specific operating rules, and leaves the rest of the prompt unchanged.

tools.name: list_leads
