tools.description: List leads for the authenticated business, with optional status/source/agent filters. Includes the latest AI lead score when available.

tools.name: get_lead
tools.description: Get full details for a single lead by ID, including the latest AI lead score and explanation.

tools.name: list_voicemails
tools.description: List recent voicemails for the authenticated business, including transcripts and recording URLs.

tools.name: list_sms_messages
tools.description: Read SMS and WhatsApp message evidence for accessible businesses (sms:read), including provider message ID, carrier status, delivery/failure timestamps and failure code. Filter by business_id, conversation or direction, and search by phone number (either side), words in the message, and date window. Provider acceptance is not delivery; delivered_at and carrier status record delivery. Uses offset pagination.

tools.name: get_inbox
tools.description: Answer "what did I miss?" in one read: the business's calls since a moment (default the last 24 hours, at most 30 days) with who called and what they wanted, every unheard voicemail with its transcript, texts that came in (needs sms:read), and open to-dos and callbacks. Read-only. Follow up with get_transcript, send_message to reply, or list_recent_calls / list_sms_messages to search further back.

tools.name: set_business_hours
tools.description: Change the business's opening hours, timezone, or one-off closed dates ("we're closed Friday the 27th"). Same change as the dashboard's hours page, admin role required. Only the days you pass change; every other day keeps what it had. A day is { open: 'HH:MM', close: 'HH:MM' } in 24-hour time, or { closed: true }. closed_dates adds dates the business is shut; reopen_dates removes them. Call routing that follows business hours uses the new hours from the next call. Returns the saved week as read back.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List outbound call campaigns for the authenticated business.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description: Create an outbound call campaign (cadence + lead batch) and optionally launch it immediately. Launching queues calls for the orchestrator; existing TCPA/consent gating still applies at dial time. Requires admin role on the business.

tools.name: launch_call_campaign
tools.description: Start or resume an existing outbound call campaign so Kai begins calling its leads. Needs campaign_id and agent_id (an agent assigned to the same business), the calls:write scope and an admin role in the business. Queues the campaign's pending calls within its call windows; real people get phone calls once it runs. A queued result does not mean any call was answered or completed. pause_call_campaign stops it. Not for email campaigns.

tools.name: pause_call_campaign
tools.description: Pause an outbound call campaign. Stops its queued and scheduled calls and cancels pending call attempts; a call already in progress may finish. Leads are kept and the campaign can be resumed later with launch_call_campaign. Needs campaign_id, the calls:write scope and an admin role in the business. Pausing an already paused campaign changes nothing.

tools.name: list_workflow_templates
tools.description: List the cadence/campaign workflow templates KaiCalls can run (standard, aggressive, nurture, custom), including each template's retry interval, defaults (call windows, days, attempts), and a ready-to-use cadence_config example. The cadence_config examples match the shape create_campaign accepts, including multi-step sequences with launch=true. Static catalog — no per-business state.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Get a dashboard summary (lead counts by status, conversion rate, call volume and duration, top agents, and business outcomes by type) over a recent time window.

tools.name: upsert_lead
tools.description: Create a new lead or update existing leads for the authenticated business, routed through the governed leads API (business access-checked, usage-logged, and audited). To create one, pass `lead` with at least one of name/phone/email plus optional status/source/notes/agent_id/etc. To update, pass `updates`: an array of { id, ...fields } for one or many existing leads (status, name, phone, email, notes, address, city, state, zip). Updates are access-checked per row and report partial success.

tools.name: send_sms
tools.description: Send a text from an agent's phone line through the governed messaging API. Provide from_agent_id, to, and message. For the immediate confirmation a customer just requested on a booking form, add purpose: booking_confirmation, the form's actual sms_consent: true, and idempotency_key; this records service consent and allows the requested confirmation after hours. Booking alerts to this business's active admin phone use purpose: booking_alert and idempotency_key. Explicit opt-outs, content controls and rate limits remain enforced. Use dispatch_policy: queue_if_needed to defer ordinary messages outside their allowed window. Optionally link lead_id; it must belong to this business and match the recipient phone.

tools.name: update_agent_config
tools.description: Edit an agent's live runtime configuration — greeting/first message, inbound or SMS prompt, the after-call summary and lead-score instructions, voice, language model, max call duration, and call-transfer settings — routed through the governed update broker so every change keeps the consent + audit trail (a versioned config snapshot and change history). Read get_agent_config first; inbound_prompt replaces the whole prompt. Each applied change is saved as a version (list_config_versions); rollback_config can restore a version's greeting, voice, prompt, model and summary/scoring, but not transfer settings or call length. Mutating changes need an idempotency_key. When the business owner or an admin is signed in through this connector, their own changes apply immediately. High-impact live changes made with an API key or on someone else's behalf queue for the owner's review instead (the owner is notified with a review link). configure_agent_business_rules edits a single named operational-rules section.

tools.name: request_emergency_address
tools.description: Set the emergency (E911) service address for one of the business's phone numbers with the phone carrier, so a 911 call from that line reaches the right dispatcher. Needs phone_number, the full street address and disclosure_acknowledged true after the owner reads the 911 notice, plus the owner's confirmed approval. Replaces any address on file for that number. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: request_transcript_webhook
tools.description: Create or update a webhook that receives the business's completed-call events (which can include transcripts) at a URL the business controls. Needs webhook_url and the owner's confirmed approval because call data leaves KaiCalls. A new webhook's signing secret is returned once. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: request_agent_update
tools.description: Change a live agent's name, greeting, prompts, voice, model, call length or call transfer through the approval-gated path, for changes made on the owner's behalf that need a recorded approval. Needs agent_id, at least one field to change and the owner's confirmed approval. Callers hear the change on their next call. Direct edits by the owner go through update_agent_config. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: request_number_purchase
tools.description: Buy a specific available phone number for the business from the phone carrier, with the owner's confirmed approval. The carrier bills the number to the business right away. Available numbers come from search_available_numbers. Optionally connects it to agent_id. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: request_config_rollback
tools.description: Put a live agent back on a saved earlier version of its configuration (listed by list_config_versions), with the owner's confirmed approval. Replaces the current live configuration; callers hear the restored version on their next call. Needs agent_id and version_number or version_id. Returns needs_user_input, needs_approval, pending_approval, executed, denied or unsupported; only executed means the change was made.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.description: Send Kai into a Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex meeting by its link. Kai joins under the agent name, takes notes, and emails the owner a summary when the meeting ends. If the meeting has a waiting room, the host must admit Kai. In the default listen mode it answers out loud when someone says its name and counts against the plan's monthly meeting minutes (a business whose plan includes none gets its first hour free, once); avatar mode joins with a talking video face and counts one avatar meeting.

tools.name: get_meeting
tools.description: List the meetings Kai was sent into (newest first), or one meeting by id with its live status, minutes used and summary, plus the plan's remaining meeting minutes this month.

tools.name: leave_meeting
tools.description: Have Kai leave a video meeting it is in, or stop trying to join one. Kai drops out of the live call for everyone in it and stops taking notes; this cannot be undone, and joining again takes a new join_meeting request. Notes taken so far are kept and can be read with get_meeting.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: List recent API usage events (endpoint, method, status code, cost) for the caller's account.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: Read the canonical public KaiCalls plan catalog, monthly USD prices and allowances. Does not select a plan, create checkout, or change billing.

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.description: Read a Stripe-verified subscription checkout receipt for a business you own. Requires business_id and session_id from checkout. Confirmed billing does not prove agent, number, or call activation; get_activation_status reports setup proof. This tool never creates checkout or retries provisioning.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send one message to a business's customer on the channel you choose: a text (sms) from one of the business's agent lines, or a WhatsApp message from its connected WhatsApp number. The same consent, Do-Not-Call, quiet-hours and rate gates as the dashboard apply, and a refusal says which one. sms needs from_agent_id; whatsapp needs a number the owner connected to WhatsApp (pass from when there is more than one) and a customer who messaged that number in the last 24 hours. Email is not sent here; draft_email_campaign drafts a campaign the owner reviews and approves. business_id is required when the account has more than one business. The result reports that the provider accepted the message, not that it was delivered.

tools.name: request_email_sender
tools.description: Set up a sending address for a business's email campaigns on a domain the business controls (for example mail.example.com). Registers the domain with the email delivery provider and returns the DNS records the owner must add where the domain is hosted. May replace an existing reply address, enabled state and sending limit, and may provision provider inbound routing, inbox and webhook. Sends no email. The sender becomes ready on its own once the records verify; check_email_sender re-checks now. Needs an admin of the business. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

tools.name: check_email_sender
tools.description: Re-check a sending domain's DNS records with the email delivery provider now and replace its saved verification proof; may finish provider inbound routing, inbox and webhook setup. Returns what is still missing; an empty list means the sender is ready. Sends no email. Any member of the business may check.

tools.name: record_email_consent
tools.description: Record that existing customers gave the business permission to email them, with evidence_ref saying where that permission came from. Pass lead_id and email for one customer, or emails for up to 200. Addresses that are not existing customers are skipped and listed. Sends no email. Needs an admin of the business. Each record states that the owner holds that permission.

tools.name: revoke_email_consent
tools.description: Take back email permission for existing customers so no campaign can email them. Pass lead_id and email for one customer, or emails for up to 200, with evidence_ref saying why. Needs an admin of the business.

tools.name: draft_email_campaign
tools.description: Save an email campaign for the business to review: a subject, a plain-text body, the customers to email (lead_ids, each with recorded email permission) and who it comes from: a verified sending domain (sender_id) or one of the business's own connected email accounts (email_account_id, listed under emailAccounts by get_email_campaign; sends at most 100 a day and 20 an hour, spaced out). Each customer gets their own email, addressed to them alone. Returns the campaign id and the fingerprint of this exact revision. Sends nothing; an owner or admin approves it with approve_email_campaign and it only goes out after launch_email_campaign. subject and text may use {{ first_name }}, {{ last_order_date }} and {{ last_order_items }} (filled per customer from the connected booking system; order_window picks which booking) or any key in lead_variables. Needs an admin of the business. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

tools.name: approve_email_campaign
tools.description: An owner or admin of the business approves one exact revision of a drafted email campaign, named by campaign_id and the fingerprint returned by draft_email_campaign or get_email_campaign. A changed draft has a new fingerprint and needs a new approval. Sends nothing; launch_email_campaign queues it. Needs an owner or admin of the business.

tools.name: launch_email_campaign
tools.description: Queue an approved email campaign for sending to real customers, within its daily limit. Needs an owner or admin of the business. Emails cannot be unsent once delivered; cancel_email_campaign stops what has not gone out yet. A queued result is not proof any email was delivered. Campaign email only goes from the business’s own verified sending domain or its own connected email account, to customers with recorded email permission who are not on the do-not-email list, within the daily amount allowed (the Kai level for a sending domain; 100 a day and 20 an hour for a connected account).

tools.name: cancel_email_campaign
tools.description: Stop an email campaign so nothing more is sent from it. Emails already delivered stay delivered. Needs campaign_id and the fingerprint of its current revision. Needs an owner or admin of the business.

tools.name: get_email_campaign
tools.description: Read a business's email campaigns: its sending addresses and their setup readiness, recent campaigns with status, revision fingerprint and outcome counts, and the customers who can be emailed (recorded consent, not on the do-not-email list). Pass campaign_id for one campaign, or sender_id for the DNS records that sending address's domain needs. Read-only; any member of the business can read.

tools.name: find_rebook_customers
tools.description: List a business's customers who booked a week last year (for example Thanksgiving week) and have not booked the same week this year, biggest last-year spend first, from the orders in the business's connected booking system. Each row has the customer's name and company, a masked phone, whether there is an email, and last year's order numbers, dates and totals. Returns email_ready_lead_ids (recorded email permission, not on the do-not-email list) to pass straight to draft_email_campaign, and call_list (name, phone, last-year total) for staff to dial by hand: Kai never calls or texts these past customers. Customers whose details have not been looked up yet show contact 'not_looked_up'; prepare_rebook_customers fills them in. Read-only; needs a connected booking system.

tools.name: prepare_rebook_customers
tools.description: For the customers find_rebook_customers lists as 'not_looked_up', read their name, phone and email from the business's booking system and save them as past customers, so the list can be emailed and called. Past customers raise no new-lead alerts and are never put in Kai call or text campaigns. Reads a few customers a minute (the booking system's limit), so one call may not finish: when remaining is above 0, call again. A customer that cannot be read stays on the list. Sends nothing. Requires an admin of the business.

tools.name: set_conversation_owner
tools.description: Set who answers a customer's text conversation. owner 'ai' (the default): Kai replies. 'human': Kai stays quiet and the business owner answers. 'external': Kai stays quiet and the business's own system answers; it receives the sms.received webhook and replies with send_message or POST /v1/messages. With external_reply_timeout_seconds (external only, 60 to 86400), Kai answers a message nothing replied to in that time. Messages are always stored and sms.received always fires. Pass conversation_id for one conversation, or phone for every conversation the business has with that customer. Re-sending the same owner changes nothing.

tools.name: get_business_verification
tools.description: Read tenant-scoped business-verification document references, pending/approved/rejected staff-review states and secure upload requirements. No file bytes, storage paths, signed URLs or tax identifiers. Uploads happen on the secure owner page, by an admin; rejected documents can be corrected and uploaded again. Internal staff verification is separate from carrier registration. Reviewer notes are returned as staff-written data.

tools.name: submit_text_registration
tools.description: Reserved submission contract; execution is currently unavailable and returns submission_unavailable without filing. Shared durable reservation and unknown-outcome reconciliation across dashboard, checkout and cron are prerequisites. Preparation and status are handled by get_text_registration and save_text_registration_details. Saving corrected details does not resubmit existing rejected provider objects: operator reconciliation is required. Another entry point or a new paid registration would duplicate the filing. It accepts no tax identifiers, credentials, file contents or legal attestations. Owner membership and billing:write required.

tools.name: get_consent_proof
tools.description: Read the consent proof for one phone number at a business: for service texts, marketing texts, calls and WhatsApp, the current status, when consent was given or taken back, how (web form, keyword, call, manual, API), the exact wording shown, and the stored proof (form page, form time, submission id), plus up to 50 history entries, newest first. Use it to answer a carrier or customer asking how someone opted in. IP addresses are never returned. found false means no consent record exists for that number. Read-only.

tools.name: get_text_registration
tools.description: Read where a business stands on its own carrier registration for business texting: saved details (never the EIN; only whether one is on file), payment, filing stage, whether sales texts are allowed, and the one next step. In MCP, `known` excludes fields the canonical flow still requires the owner to confirm; `suggestions` preserves those nonprivate values and available provenance. `missing` is the ordered outstanding field-question list, with missing_value or confirmation_required reasons; `next_question` is its first item. `question_progress` counts field questions including next, not website screens. Website screens group several fields and may include a private identity step; unequal counts can be valid. The MCP presentation separates configured registration/enrollment from recipient-specific sending permission and delivery, which remain not_checked. A null own registration does not prove an enrolled platform route cannot text; configured lines do not prove a send is authorized. Dashboard/API presentation is unchanged. Pass check=true to also run the pre-filing check: every problem a carrier reviewer would reject the registration on (business details, campaign wording, website, privacy policy, texting terms, opt-in page), each as `prefiling_check.items` with a plain fix, so it can be fixed before anything is paid. Read-only.

tools.name: save_text_registration_details
tools.description: Save a business's legal name, the name customers know it by (if different), entity type, industry, website, address, authorized contact and what it will text (service only, or service and sales) for its own carrier registration. Business owner, or an admin of the business (such as the partner that created the workspace) preparing it for the owner. Each field holds an answer from the owner; anything omitted is filled from what is already on file (see get_text_registration `known`). Answers can be saved one at a time: answers given so far are kept, and while questions remain the result lists `saved_steps`, `missing` and `next_question`. The owner can finish here or on the registration page. Never takes the EIN: the owner types it on the registration page returned as setup_url. Each saved answer replaces the value on file for that field. Refused once a filing is already with the carriers. Charges nothing and files nothing.

tools.name: start_text_registration_checkout
tools.description: Create the payment link for a business's own carrier registration (a one-time filing fee plus a monthly campaign fee). Business owner only, and only once the details and the EIN are saved. An admin who prepared the details gets owner_required with owner_handoff_url: the page the owner opens to type the EIN, review and confirm. Returns checkout_url for the owner to open and pay; nothing is charged by this tool, and filing starts only after payment. A checkout_url means neither payment nor filing. On a plan that includes registration there is nothing to pay: the tool sends it to the carriers straight away and returns included_in_plan and filed true instead of a link, so that path requires confirm_submission true, which records that the owner reviewed and confirmed the saved details and external submission. Submission is not carrier approval. The tool takes no EIN, document contents, credentials or legal attestations.

tools.name: set_branded_caller_id
tools.description: File the business name that landlines show when the business's number calls out (caller ID name). Included with the business's own text registration once it is paid; charges nothing. Business owner only. The name must be at most 15 characters, start with a letter, and use only letters, numbers, periods, commas and spaces (get_text_registration returns a suggestion in branded_caller_id.suggestedName). Files with the carriers once the business profile is approved; review then takes a day or two and carriers show it within 72 hours. US local numbers only. The result confirms the filing, not that the name is showing on calls.

tools.name: start_own_caller_id
tools.description: Let Kai's outbound calls show a number the person already owns (their cell or an old main line) instead of a KaiCalls line, so people recognize who is calling. A verification call goes to that number and returns a code; the person answers and types the code on the keypad. Then get_own_caller_id confirms it. Ownership is proven only by that call. US and Canada numbers. Business owner only. Charges nothing. Callbacks to the shown number reach that phone, not Kai. use_by_default (default true) shows it on every call unless make_call asks for caller_id 'business_line'. Starting a new number replaces the old one.

tools.name: get_own_caller_id
tools.description: Which number Kai's outbound calls show: the person's own verified number or the KaiCalls line. Also confirms a verification started with start_own_caller_id once the person has typed the code. state is none, pending, verified or failed.

tools.name: remove_own_caller_id
tools.description: Stop showing the person's own number on Kai's calls; calls show the KaiCalls line again. Business owner only.

tools.name: create_customer_workspace
tools.description: Create a new KaiCalls account for a business, owned by the business owner's own email address. It lets a partner or helper set up KaiCalls for a business owner. The account starts without a plan or phone number: the result includes a link the owner opens themselves to choose a plan and add their card, and the line is set up only after they pay. This tool charges nothing. By default the caller is added as an admin of the new account so they can continue setup (get_setup_checklist lists the steps); join_as_admin false skips that. partner_code credits a referring partner and does not apply to a partner's own account. Fails, creating nothing, if the email already has a KaiCalls account.

tools.name: set_up_business
tools.description: Optional line customization: sets the business name and greeting Kai answers with, as the owner requested. Not required to make calls, and never changes payment, usage or fraud limits. Extra business details are optional; no business-qualification questionnaire is needed. An existing business greeting is left unchanged.

tools.name: get_setup_checklist
tools.description: Read where one business stands on setup: plan, phone number, texting registration, WhatsApp, call and lead alerts, connected mailbox for follow-up email, and email campaign sender. Each step has a state (done, in_progress, needs_owner, needs_action or unavailable) and one next action: either the tool that moves it forward, or the page the owner must open for steps only they can do, such as paying, typing their EIN or signing in to Facebook or Google. Read-only; changes nothing and contacts no one.

tools.name: connect_whatsapp
tools.description: Get the one link a business owner opens to put WhatsApp on their KaiCalls number. They sign in to Facebook as an admin of the business's Meta Business account and verify the number; the business owns its WhatsApp account. Uses the business's oldest KaiCalls line unless phone_number names another of its lines. Returns the same link while it is still valid (up to 3 days). Owner or admin only. Creates nothing billable and connects nothing by itself: get_whatsapp_status reports the connection after the owner finishes, and WhatsApp is not connected until it says so.

tools.name: get_whatsapp_status
tools.description: Check whether WhatsApp is connected on a business's KaiCalls number, read live from the carrier. Connected only once the number is verified for WhatsApp; otherwise says whether the owner's link is still waiting, expired or failed.

tools.name: get_channel_status
tools.description: Read customer channel setup. Phone calls report configured number resources only: state configured or needs_setup, with canSend/canReceive null because operational availability is unknown. SMS has state not_checked and null send/receive flags; shared_setup_state retains the existing configuration summary, not recipient-specific permission. Registration detail requires billing:read; this SMS-scope summary reads no new billing details. Other channels retain their existing states and flags. private_test_readiness checks owner-private call setup only when the token also has agents:read; otherwise it is not_checked with reconnect scope guidance. Private testing does not establish customer coverage or outbound call permission, which remain not_checked. Email includes separate managedEmail campaign sender readiness; a connected mailbox does not prove campaign approval or delivery. Read-only; changes nothing.

tools.name: get_trust_level
tools.description: Read one business's KaiCalls trust level (Sprout, Verified, Trusted, Pro, Partner): the current level, the steps to the next one with progress, what each level unlocks, today's outbound calls and texts against current effective account limits, and any hold. Badge progress does not itself establish higher call or text caps. focus 'ladder' explains every level; focus 'level' with level explains one. Read-only: returns saved standing or computes missing/stale standing without saving it or sending notifications. recheck_trust_level recomputes and saves current standing. Levels are earned, never set: no tool can raise one.

tools.name: recheck_trust_level
tools.description: Recompute one business's KaiCalls trust level now from its live account activity (card on file, paid bills, days active, real customer calls) and save the result, the same recheck the dashboard runs, for example right after the owner adds a card. Returns the same view as get_trust_level plus whether the level moved up or down. Requires current business membership. Replaces the saved derived state, may record level-change history and may email the current owner when standing changes. It can only reflect what the account has earned; it never sets or raises a level by request.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Get plan terms and usage for accessible businesses. No-card trials report 25 lifetime minutes, zero price and no overage; paid plans report the mapped subscription price and billing-cycle usage. Answered-call allowance usage is the raw billable call count, matching dashboard and right-sizing. A separate weighted count is informational only, not allowance consumption or right-sizing. Phone allowance includes purchased extra lines. A balance does not prove activation or inbound routing. Unavailable billing data returns an error.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Create, or reuse, a secure payment page hosted by Stripe where the business owner pays for a KaiCalls plan from list_plans with their own card. Needs business_id, plan_id and an idempotency_key: retrying with the same key returns the same page, and choosing a different plan needs a new key. This tool charges nothing; only the owner can pay, by opening the page themselves. It never proves payment or that the phone line is live: get_checkout_status reports payment for the returned session_id.

tools.name: list_numbers
tools.description: List phone numbers assigned to the accessible business(es), with capability and compliance flags. Assignment does not prove a successful inbound test or customer coverage. get_activation_status reports current readiness and private-test proof. Forwarding is an optional customer route.

tools.name: get_phone_flow
tools.description: Read how calls ring on the business's hosted phone system: which cells and desk phones ring, for how many seconds, and whether after-hours callers go straight to Kai. Reconciled from the phone system on every call. Returns 409 when the hosted phone system is not set up for this business.

tools.name: update_phone_flow
tools.description: Replace how calls ring on the business's hosted phone system with a full phone flow: { version: 1, hours: { mode: 'always' | 'business_hours', afterHours: 'kai' }, ring: { members: [{ kind: 'cell', phone: E.164, label, requirePressOne } | { kind: 'desk_phone' | 'user', userId, label }], timeoutSeconds: 5-120 }, overflow: 'kai' }. Applied idempotently (only real differences are written); every member passes the forwarding-loop guard; business_hours mode derives the schedule from the business hours already on file. Because it replaces the whole flow, the input is the full flow as get_phone_flow returns it, with changes applied.

tools.name: set_up_phone_system
tools.description: Turn the business's number into a hosted phone system: Kai is installed as extension 700, the owner's mobile joins the list of phones to ring first, and calls reach Kai when nobody picks up. Idempotent and resumable — a re-run reuses everything already created and reports it under `reused`. Needs a complete US street address on file (the emergency-services and tax location) and the owner's mobile: when either is missing the tool fails with `code` missing_address or missing_owner_mobile plus `required_field` and `next_action` naming exactly what is missing, which business_address or owner_mobile accepts. Returns the status shape (existing setup IDs, extension and the phone-system line) and `next_step`, the owner's next action in one line (forward your line here / dial 700 from any office phone).

tools.name: get_phone_system_status
tools.description: Read saved phone-system configuration: extension, resource IDs (never secrets), assigned line, and agreement. phone_system_configuration.configuration_allows_calls means provisioned resources plus a permitting agreement only; it does not verify calls can connect. ready_for_calls is null because operational availability is unknown. private_test_readiness uses the existing owner-private call setup authority only with agents:read; otherwise not_checked. Customer coverage and outbound call permission remain not_checked. This read differs from the shared phone-system API configuration flag and changes nothing.

tools.name: add_team_phone
tools.description: Add a teammate's (or the owner's) cell to the phones that ring before Kai answers. Idempotent — a cell already listed is reported as already included. Owners and admins are also registered on the admin roster, so calling the business line from that cell reaches the admin secretary; a member only rings. The business's own forwarded-from office line is refused (forwarding_loop) because ringing it would bounce the call straight back. Requires the phone system to be set up first (set_up_phone_system).

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List SMS conversation threads (counterparty timeline metadata) for the authenticated business, most recent first.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Get a single SMS conversation thread by ID.

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.description: List the configured outbound webhook(s) for a business, including supported event types.

tools.name: set_webhook
tools.description: Create or update a business outbound webhook (URL + subscribed events). Returns a webhook secret on first creation only.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Remove a business outbound webhook by ID.

tools.name: list_evals
tools.description: List saved test scenarios for an agent (or all accessible agents). A new agent has none; create_eval adds one.

tools.name: create_eval
tools.description: Save a test scenario for one of the business's agents: what a caller says and what the agent's reply must do to pass. run_eval then grades the agent against it. Saving places no call and changes nothing on the agent.

tools.name: run_eval
tools.description: Run a saved test scenario against one of the business's agents and grade the agent's replies: pass eval_id for one scenario, or agent_id for every scenario saved for that agent (see list_evals). The test is a simulated text conversation with the agent's current live configuration; no phone call is placed, no customer is contacted and the agent's configuration is not changed. Each run uses paid voice-agent provider capacity and is recorded with its result, so scenarios already run on the agent's current configuration are not run again unless force is true, and each agent has a daily limit on runs. Returns pass or fail per scenario with the grader's reasons.

tools.name: find_voices
tools.description: Find the three voices that best match a plain description of what the owner wants (for example 'a Southern man who can also speak Spanish' or 'warm older woman, calm'), and get a page link where the owner can play each one in English and Spanish, pick one to switch the agent's voice, and undo within 24 hours. Show the owner the page link; nothing changes until they pick. The link expires in 7 days.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List the curated, credential-free voice catalog (id, display name, accent, language, gender, sample URL) used to configure agent voices.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create a new KaiCalls agent — the secretary that answers this business’s calls (the live voice agent plus KaiCalls records) — with a system prompt, greeting, voice, and model. Its starting settings are saved as version 1 and each later change as a new version (list_config_versions); rollback_config restores a version's greeting, voice, prompt, model and summary/scoring. Compliance: KaiCalls automatically applies state-aware AI-disclosure and consent handling to every agent it provisions, and flags high-risk business categories for extra review.

tools.name: attach_number
tools.description: Assign a phone number already in the KaiCalls registry pool to a business (and optionally route it directly to an agent). Does NOT purchase a new number; search_available_numbers and buy_number handle purchases.

tools.name: attach_own_twilio_number
tools.description: Have a voice agent answer calls on ONE number from the business's own connected Twilio account, calls only. Reads only that number. dry_run defaults to true and changes nothing: it returns would_change (the number's VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod) and the fields left unchanged. With dry_run false, only that number's VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod change; its text settings (SmsUrl, SmsMethod, SmsApplicationSid, StatusCallback) are read back afterwards and must be unchanged, so a texting setup another service runs on the account keeps working. Refuses a number a Twilio app answers, and a number another service answers unless replace_existing_voice is true. Uses one plan line. Requires admin role.

tools.name: detach_own_twilio_number
tools.description: Stop a voice agent answering a number from the business's own connected Twilio account and put back the call setting (VoiceUrl and VoiceMethod) the number had before it was attached. The number is never released from the account and its text settings are not touched. Requires admin role.

tools.name: set_owner_phone
tools.description: Saves the owner's own mobile number on the business record (the number Kai texts whenever it takes a call for the owner) so Kai can ring it first and so activation/forwarding follow-ups can reach a human — connecting a number alone does not prove the owner can be reached. In the acquisition flow this step comes before search_available_numbers and buy_number (#2086). US numbers only; normalized to E.164 and rejected if it cannot be validated as a US mobile/landline number. When ring_first is true (default), also configures ring-first routing so calls hit this cell before overflowing to the secretary — the same path used at signup. declined=true, in place of owner_phone, records a caller who declines to give a number as an inquiry: a KaiCalls lead, with no provisioned business or number.

tools.name: detach_number
tools.description: Release a phone number from a business back to the unassigned registry pool.

tools.name: search_available_numbers
tools.description: Search the carrier for phone numbers available to purchase (live number inventory). In the acquisition flow this follows set_owner_phone, which saves a reachable owner number or records a decline.

tools.name: buy_number
tools.description: Request a real phone-number purchase. This is APPROVAL-GATED: the carrier bills immediately on execution, so the tool only prepares a request for authenticated owner review. Caller-supplied human_confirmed, dashboard_session, or system_policy fields never authorize execution. Returns the stored request and a review URL for the owner; while approval is pending, no number has been purchased. Existing entitlement and carrier reservation checks still apply. In the acquisition flow this follows set_owner_phone, which saves a reachable owner number or records a decline.

tools.name: list_knowledge
tools.description: List agent knowledge base entries for a business.

tools.name: upsert_knowledge
tools.description: Create a new agent knowledge base entry, or update one when `id` is provided. Creating requires title, content, and content_type.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List a business's agent product catalog.

tools.name: upsert_product
tools.description: Create a new product row, or update one when `id` is provided. Creating requires name and business_id. Pass `quantity` to set/update inventory.

tools.name: get_agent_config
tools.description: Read an agent's settings as the owner edits them: the editable inbound, outbound and text prompts, greeting, voice (with its list_voices id when it has one), model, call length, transfer settings, and the call summary and lead score instructions. Read this before update_agent_config: inbound_prompt there replaces the whole prompt, so edit the text returned here.

tools.name: list_config_versions
tools.description: List the saved versions of an agent's settings, newest first: what saved each one (source), what changed (diff_summary), who (created_by) and which version a rollback came from. Secrets are never included. Pass `version` to fetch one version's full saved settings (config_snapshot). That snapshot holds the compiled prompt; to edit the prompt, read get_agent_config instead.

tools.name: get_change_history
tools.description: List an agent's recent config-change audit trail (change_type, change_source, old/new value, timestamp) — the same change log the owner hears when they call their line and ask what changed. Every change KaiCalls makes to an agent (via update_agent_config, configure_agent_business_rules, the owner's call-in line, or the dashboard) is logged here. Rows carry no version number; to undo a change, pick a version from list_config_versions and use rollback_config.

tools.name: rollback_config
tools.description: Request a rollback to a saved version of the agent settings. It restores the version's greeting, voice, prompt (and the editable prompt copy, when the version saved one), model and call summary/scoring. Transfer settings, call length, tools and speech recognition stay as they are; the result lists what was and was not restored. When the business owner or an admin is signed in through this connector, the rollback applies immediately; otherwise the owner approves it from a review link. Targets are listed by list_config_versions. The rollback is itself saved as a new version, and secrets are never copied.

tools.name: list_observability_events
tools.description: List a business-scoped timeline of compact call-runtime events and redacted integration-delivery attempts. Uses bounded keyset pagination.

tools.name: list_tool_execution_logs
tools.description: List per-call voice-agent tool execution traces — outcome, latency, timeout, and a redacted result preview for each routed tool call. Answers "did this tool call actually work".

tools.name: list_subscription_history
tools.description: List the business plan and price changes, newest first: upgrades, downgrades, add-ons and automatic right-size moves.

tools.name: list_overage_charges
tools.description: List the per-period overage-minutes ledger (older per-minute-overage plans only; current plans carry no overage). GET /v1/balance/get_balance only returns an aggregate; this returns the underlying per-period ledger rows.

tools.name: list_rightsize_recommendations
tools.description: List per-period automatic plan right-size decisions, including the dry_run -> notified -> (kept | applied | superseded) lifecycle. Answers "is this business about to get right-sized".

tools.name: get_billing_contacts
tools.description: Read who gets the monthly invoice email for a business. Every paid invoice is always emailed to the business owner (returned masked); up to 3 extra addresses, such as a bookkeeper or office inbox, get the same email.

tools.name: set_billing_contacts
tools.description: Replace the extra addresses that get the monthly invoice email (at most 3; an empty list clears them). The business owner always keeps getting every invoice and cannot be removed. Requires the current owner role on the business.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.description: Read the business's own plan: no_paid_plan, active, or canceling, with the plan name and the renewal or end date. Use before cancel_subscription to tell the owner what will happen.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.description: Cancel the business's plan when the owner asks to. The plan stays on until the end of the paid period (or trial) and is never charged again; a past-due plan ends now. Pass undo=true to keep a plan whose cancel has not taken effect yet. Requires the current owner role. Confirm with the owner before calling.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Report a problem with your KaiCalls agent, phone number, billing, or account. Saves the report to your change history and notifies KaiCalls support so a person can follow up on anything broken or not working as expected.

tools.name: start_campaign
tools.description: Start a marketing campaign pack on Campaign Pack's own GPUs. Produces a campaign plan, ideas, ad and social scripts, a creator brief, and a client-ready PDF — plus product stills on the image sizes. Returns immediately with a job id; the run itself takes minutes, so poll check_campaign rather than waiting. Write the brief yourself from what the user told you: the richer and more specific it is, the better the pack. Nothing is sent to any third-party model provider.

tools.name: check_campaign
tools.description: Progress of a running campaign: status, the tools it has just called, queue position, and whether it is waiting for a human approval. Poll about every 20 seconds.

tools.name: get_pack
tools.description: Collect a finished campaign: the folder, its files, the written overview, and the path to the PDF. Takes the job_id from start_campaign, or the session_id from list_campaigns — use session_id for a campaign run in an earlier conversation, where no job id survives.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: Campaigns on this account, newest first, including ones shared with it. Start here when you do not already have an id — the ids from start_campaign only exist in the conversation that made them, so this is how you find a campaign from last week. Pass a session_id from here to get_pack to open one.

tools.name: list_workspace_files
tools.description: List files and folders in the account's workspace — campaign folders, scripts, product stills, PDFs, uploads. Directories end in '/'.

tools.name: read_workspace_file
tools.description: Contents of a text file in the workspace — a script, the plan, the creator brief, a transcript. Large files are truncated. For a PDF, image or video call get_download_url instead.

tools.name: get_download_url
tools.description: A link the person can open to get one file — the campaign PDF, a product still, a video. Works for any file in the workspace, including ones too big or too binary to read as text. The link expires within the hour.

tools.name: upload_product_photo
tools.description: Put a product photo into the user's workspace so a campaign can edit stills from the real thing. Base64 of the image bytes.

tools.name: share_campaign
tools.description: Give a teammate access to a campaign by email address — including while it is still running. They see the same live run from their own AI client or the website, can abort it, answer its approval prompts, and take the next turn. They must already have a Campaign Pack account; sharing does not create one.

tools.name: list_campaign_access
tools.description: Who owns a campaign and who it is shared with.

tools.name: unshare_campaign
tools.description: Revoke a collaborator's access. Takes effect on their next request.

tools.name: answer_approval
tools.description: Answer a paused run that wants to send the user's data somewhere outside Campaign Pack. Ask the person; never decide for them.

tools.name: abort_campaign
tools.description: Stop a running campaign.

tools.name: ai_provider_status
tools.description: Get the live status of AI coding providers (Claude, OpenAI, Copilot, Cursor, OpenRouter and more). Returns status, how long each provider has been in its current state, and last check time. Pass service_id for one provider, omit it for all.

tools.name: check_provider_health
tools.description: Check whether one or more AI coding providers are healthy enough to use right now. Returns healthy=true only when every requested provider is operational (or within the allowed statuses). Use this before starting work that depends on a provider, or to decide which provider to route to.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Use this when someone without a Capital Company account wants one for their firm. Opens a Capital Company workspace, an account and the firm’s team. Needs no sign-in. Capital Company emails them a sign-in link.

tools.name: capital_company_create_fund
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to set up an SPV or a fund — to pool investors’ money into one deal, such as buying a startup’s or a pre-IPO company’s shares, or to raise a blind pool — or asks how to start one. Starts setting up the fund in Capital Company: an SPV or a blind pool, with its legal name, expected allocation, strategy, classes and fees, manager and documents. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or a proposed fund for the user to confirm. This call creates nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_invite_investors
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to bring investors into one of their funds. Starts an invitation of investors to the fund by email address. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed invitations for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_send_subscription_agreements
tools.description: Use this when the user wants investors in one of their funds to sign their subscription agreements. Starts the signature requests. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed signature requests for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_send_capital_calls
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a fund’s investors to pay in money they committed. Starts capital call notices to the investors of a fund class. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed notices for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing, and Capital Company never moves money.

tools.name: capital_company_update_fund
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to change a setting on one of their funds. Starts a change to the settings they name. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed change for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_edit_commitment
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to change an investor’s existing commitment in one of their funds. Starts an edit to the fields they name. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed edit, with its effect on capital calls already sent, for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_create_commitment
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to record that an investor committed to one of their funds. Starts recording the new commitment. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed commitment for the user to confirm. This call records nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_create_invite_link
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a link they can share so that investors can ask to join a class of one of their funds. Starts a new shareable invite link, with a label and an expiry if they give one. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed link for the user to confirm; once confirmed, the reply gives the link’s address. This call creates nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_update_invite_link
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to rename a shareable invite link to one of their funds or change when it expires. Starts the change. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed change for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_revoke_invite_link
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a shareable invite link to one of their funds to stop working. Starts revoking it. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed revocation for the user to confirm. This call revokes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_set_invite_link_fees
tools.description: Use this when the user wants investors who join through a shareable invite link to start on different fees. Starts setting the link’s fees: the class’s default, another template, or new terms. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed fees for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_add_fund_class
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a new class in one of their existing funds, with its own fees or commitment limits. Starts adding the class. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed class for the user to confirm. This call creates nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_edit_fund_class
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to change a class of one of their funds: its name, commitment limits, unit price, fees or admin fee reserve. Starts the change to the terms they name. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed change for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_update_capital_call
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to change a capital call already made in one of their funds: its deadline or notes, or one investor’s amount. Starts the change. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed change, with each investor’s amount before and after and whether they are emailed, for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing, and Capital Company never moves money.

tools.name: capital_company_resend_capital_call
tools.description: Use this when the user wants investors reminded of a capital call they have not paid in full. Starts a reminder of the call’s notice to the investors they name, or every investor with something outstanding. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed reminders with their recipients for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing, and Capital Company never moves money.

tools.name: capital_company_cancel_capital_call
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to cancel a capital call in one of their funds that nobody has paid. Starts the cancellation. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed cancellation, with what the investors are told, for the user to confirm. This call cancels nothing, and Capital Company never moves money.

tools.name: capital_company_remind_to_sign
tools.description: Use this when the user wants investors in one of their funds reminded to sign the subscription agreement they were already sent — the ones they name, or everyone who has not signed. Starts the reminders. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed reminders, with who is left out and why, for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_resend_fund_invitations
tools.description: Use this when the user wants invitations to one of their funds sent again to the investors already invited. Starts resending them to the addresses each invitation is out to. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed invitations to resend for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_withdraw_fund_invitations
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to withdraw invitations to one of their funds that nothing has come of yet — one sent to the wrong person or sent twice. Starts withdrawing the ones they name; an investor who has a commitment, was sent a subscription agreement, or has a capital call or payment is not withdrawn here. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed withdrawals for the user to confirm. This call changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_approve_investor_kyc
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to approve the KYC questionnaire an investor submitted to one of their funds. Starts the approval of the questionnaires they name. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed approvals, with any issues flagged on each questionnaire, for the user to confirm. This call approves nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_add_fee_pool
tools.description: Use this when the user wants an admin pool or a management pool added to a class of one of their funds, funded by the fund or by its manager. Starts adding the pool. Returns Capital Company’s next question — the pool’s type, who funds it, how the manager pays, its amount or date — or the proposed pool for the user to confirm. This call creates nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_fund_pool_from_management_fees
tools.description: Use this when the user wants an admin pool their manager funds paid out of the management fees the fund has collected for that manager. Starts the funding, with each manager’s available management fees. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed funding for the user to confirm. This call moves nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_email_pool_invoice
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the invoice for a fee pool of one of their funds emailed, usually to the manager who funds it, at an address they give. Starts the email. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed email for the user to confirm. This call sends nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_record_pool_invoice_paid
tools.description: Use this when the user says their manager paid the invoice for a fee pool it funds and is invoiced for, from its own bank account. Starts recording that payment; any other payment is marked paid on the fund’s Expenses tab, not here. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or the proposed record for the user to confirm. This call records nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_ask
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about their own funds on Capital Company, or how Capital Company works. Answers a question about the user’s team and funds from Capital Company’s records, or about how Capital Company works — where something is, what a page, a status or an email means, what the product offers, such as its API — from Capital Company’s product guide, with a link to the page when there is one. Answers in Capital Company’s words, only from what the user may see. Changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_reply
tools.description: Sends the user’s answer to Capital Company’s last question, in their own words. Returns Capital Company’s next question, or a proposal for the user to confirm.

tools.name: capital_company_confirm
tools.description: Sends the user’s answer, confirm or decline, to a Confirmation from Capital Company. Confirming carries out what it describes; declining carries out nothing, and Capital Company asks what to change.

tools.name: capital_company_show_confirmation
tools.description: Shows a Confirmation from Capital Company on its card, where the user can confirm or decline it. Changes nothing.

tools.name: capital_company_claim
tools.description: For someone without a Capital Company account who said yes to a proposal: emails a sign-in link to the address they give. Opening the link verifies the address and creates what they said yes to.

tools.name: capital_company_conversation
tools.description: Reads the user’s current conversation with Capital Company, including the outcome of anything they confirmed and whether it is waiting on them. Changes nothing.

tools.name: find_journey
tools.description: Use when the user wants a guided, step-by-step journey on a topic, a skill or an exam. Searches the published journeys and returns up to three cards (id, title, summary, shape, languages, number of stops, estimated minutes, who it is for and not for, a premium flag, page_url). `in_progress: true` marks a journey this user already has open. When nothing matches, `alternatives` holds the three nearest journeys.

tools.name: list_journey_categories
tools.description: Use when the user asks what kinds of journeys are available. Returns each category slug, a readable label, the number of journeys in it and a few example titles.

tools.name: browse_journeys
tools.description: Use when the user wants to look through the journeys, optionally within one category (a slug from list_journey_categories). Returns a page of the same cards as find_journey, with the total and next_offset.

tools.name: open_journey
tools.description: Use when the user chooses a journey to start or continue. Opens it, or resumes the user's session for it, and returns the session contract: `session`, the stop titles, the capabilities, the limits in turns and the first step. Calling it again for the same journey resumes the same session; it never resets progress.

tools.name: take_journey_step
tools.description: Use for every step after open_journey. Sends the user's choice and returns the next step: `answer`, `statement`, numbered `options` with ids, `media`, `progress` and `limits`. Send `pick` with an option id when the user chose an option or its number; otherwise send `say` with what the user said. `go` jumps to a stop from the contract; `drill` and `simulate` start practice on exam journeys; `exit` leaves practice. Supply a fresh `turn_id` per step; a repeat returns the stored step. If the step carries `wall`, tell the user `wall.for_human`.

tools.name: get_journey_progress
tools.description: Use when the user asks where they are in a journey, how far they have come or how much is left. Returns the current stop, visited and remaining stops, percent done, practice stats, limits and a resume line.

tools.name: create_takeaway
tools.description: Use when the user asks for a summary to keep. Composes a markdown takeaway from this journey session: what the user asked, the key points and the stops visited. Available on connected accounts; otherwise returns not_available.

tools.name: get_resume_link
tools.description: Use when the user wants to continue the journey later, on the website or in another assistant. Returns a resume link and a short resume code for this session.

tools.name: restart_journey
tools.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to start a journey over, after confirming with them. Returns to the first step and clears the visited stops; turns already used stay used. Returns the same session contract as open_journey.

tools.name: list_backgrounds
tools.description: List the background scenes available for car photos: built-in studios, showrooms and outdoor settings, plus the workspace's own custom backgrounds (`custom: true`, made with create_background or in the app). Call this first to pick a scene: each entry has a preview image, an example with a car, and the `id` that generate_background takes as `background_id` (custom ones also go to refine_background and delete_background). Read-only and free; takes no parameters and returns every scene in one response. For logos use list_logos instead.

tools.name: create_background
tools.description: Create a new reusable background scene for the workspace, such as the dealer's own showroom, a branded studio or a specific outdoor setting. Use it when none of the scenes in list_backgrounds fits; it does not edit a car photo (that is generate_background), and to adjust a custom background that already exists use refine_background instead of creating another. Give a `description`, `reference_image_urls`, or both; add `base_background_id` to start from a built-in scene and describe only what to change. Renders a preview with a demo car and returns it as an image plus the new background's `id`, ready to pass to generate_background. Costs one credit; a rejected or failed request is not charged.

tools.name: refine_background
tools.description: Adjust a custom background that already exists and render a new preview, e.g. after create_background when the preview is close but not right. `description` is only the change to make ('make the floor darker and the lighting warmer'); everything else in the scene is kept, and `reference_image_urls` can show the look to move towards. The background is updated in place under the same `id` and name, so later generate_background calls use the refined scene; photos already generated are not changed. Works on custom backgrounds only, not built-in ones; to start a different scene use create_background. Returns the new preview image. Costs one credit; a rejected or failed request is not charged.

tools.name: delete_background
tools.description: Permanently delete one of the workspace's custom backgrounds, e.g. a scene the user no longer wants in their list. It cannot be undone through this server; a deleted scene has to be made again with create_background. Photos already generated with it are not affected, and no credits are charged or refunded. Only custom backgrounds (`custom: true` in list_backgrounds) can be deleted, never built-in ones. To change a scene instead of removing it, use refine_background. Returns the `id` with `deleted: true`, or `not_found` for an unknown id.

tools.name: generate_background
tools.description: Replace the background of one car photo with a chosen scene: the main tool for turning a phone photo into a listing photo. The car is kept as photographed and gets shadows, lighting and reflections that match the scene. Works on exterior, interior and detail shots. Pick `background_id` with list_backgrounds first and use the same one for every photo of a car. In the same call it can hide the plate (`hide_license_plate`, with `license_plate_style` and, for `logo`, a `license_plate_logo` from list_logos), draw a dealer `logo`, reframe to an `aspect_ratio`, centre the car or show it washed. To hide the plate without changing the background use hide_license_plates; to make a new scene use create_background. One photo per call; the source photo is not modified. Costs one credit, and a failed generation is not charged. Can take up to a minute. Returns a signed `image_url` of the high-resolution result, valid for 7 days.

tools.name: hide_license_plates
tools.description: Hide the license plates in a car photo without changing anything else, for privacy before publishing a listing. Use this when the background should stay as it is; when the background is being replaced as well, set `hide_license_plate` on generate_background instead of calling both. `style` chooses a blur (default) or a solid `block`, and `block_color` sets the block's colour. Uses no credits: it is included with an active subscription, up to a fair-use monthly limit, and returns `subscription_required` for a workspace without one. The source photo is not modified; the result is returned as an image, with the areas that were hidden listed as `plates`.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Read the workspace's current credit balance, returned as `balance`. One credit is one photo from generate_background or one preview from create_background or refine_background; hide_license_plates uses none. Call it before a batch to check there are enough credits, or after an insufficient-credits error. Read-only and free; takes no parameters. It does not show plans or prices: when the balance is too low, use list_plans, then create_checkout (no subscription yet) or change_plan (existing subscription).

tools.name: list_logos
tools.description: List the logos stored for the workspace, to get the `id` that other tools need. `type` selects which set is returned: `logo` (default) for dealer logos drawn on finished photos, passed as `logo.id` to generate_background, or `plate` for designs shown on the license plate, passed as `license_plate_logo.id`. Each entry has `id`, `type`, `image_url` and `created_at`. Also call it before delete_logo, or before upload_logo to see whether the logo is already stored. Read-only and free. For background scenes use list_backgrounds instead.

tools.name: upload_logo
tools.description: Store a logo for the workspace so it can be put on photos later. It does not change any photo by itself: pass the returned `id` to generate_background as `logo.id`, or as `license_plate_logo.id` for a `plate` logo. The file is fetched from `image_url` once and a copy is kept (PNG, WebP or JPEG up to 5 MB; a transparent background works best). `type` is `logo` (default) for dealer logos or `plate` for license plate designs, where `background` sets the plate colour behind a transparent logo. Up to seven per type: when full, remove one with delete_logo first. Check list_logos before uploading to avoid duplicates. Free. Returns the stored logo with its `id`.

tools.name: delete_logo
tools.description: Permanently delete one of the workspace's stored logos, e.g. an outdated logo or to free one of the seven slots before upload_logo. It cannot be undone through this server; the logo has to be uploaded again to restore it. Photos already generated keep the logo they were made with, and later generate_background calls can no longer use this `id`. Get the `id` from list_logos, and pass the same `type` the logo was listed under (`logo` by default, or `plate`). Free. Returns the `id` with `deleted: true`, or `not_found` when the id is unknown for that type.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: List the subscription plans on offer, to quote prices or to get the `price_id` that create_checkout (workspace without a subscription) and change_plan (existing subscription) take. Each plan has its monthly photo allowance (`credits`), billing interval and price: `unit_amount` is in the smallest unit of `currency` (USD), and `currency_options` lists the fixed local prices whose keys create_checkout accepts as `currency`. Read-only and free; takes no parameters and is the same for every caller. It does not show the workspace's own balance: use get_credits for that.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Start a first subscription for a workspace that has none, e.g. when get_credits shows too few credits. Take `price_id` from list_plans; `currency` picks one of that plan's fixed local prices and `buyer` decides VAT handling for EU and UK buyers. This call charges nothing: it returns a Stripe checkout `url` for the user to open and pay, and the plan's photos are added once the payment completes. For a workspace that already subscribes it returns `already_subscribed`; use change_plan there instead. Needs an OAuth sign-in: with an API key it returns an error pointing to the app.

tools.name: change_plan
tools.description: Change the plan of a workspace that already has a subscription, to a `price_id` from list_plans. Always call it first with `confirm: false`, which for an upgrade returns a preview of the prorated charge and charges nothing, and get the user's agreement to that amount. With `confirm: true` an upgrade charges the payment method on file immediately and adds the photos at once, while a smaller plan charges nothing now and is booked to start at the next renewal. For a workspace without a subscription it returns `no_active_subscription`; use create_checkout there instead. It cannot cancel a subscription; the user does that in the app. Needs an OAuth sign-in: with an API key it returns an error pointing to the app.

tools.name: search_cars
tools.description: Search new and used cars for sale at local dealers, in plain language. Every car comes back with its advertised price, its market price, how far under or over market it is, a deal label, a 0 to 100 score and its rank among comparable cars. Use a market name in the query or the market argument. Returns up to 10 cars per call, best deals first.

tools.name: get_car
tools.description: Full details of one car: price against its market price, why it ranks where it does in plain sentences, mileage, color, drivetrain, photos count, the dealer and its phone, and the page to open. Use the id from search_cars.

tools.name: compare_cars
tools.description: Compare 2 to 4 cars side by side on price, market price, percent under market, score, rank, mileage and dealer, and say which is the best deal.

tools.name: market_summary
tools.description: How many of a model (or kind of car) are for sale in a market, the median advertised price and mileage, the price range, and the share priced under market. Use it for questions like 'what does a used Camry cost in Dallas' or 'is now a good time'.

tools.name: dealer_info
tools.description: A dealer's name, address, phone and website, how many new and used cars it has listed, and its best-ranked cars.

tools.name: list_markets
tools.description: The markets Carfinity covers, with the number of cars in each.

tools.name: start_inquiry
tools.description: Prepare a message to the dealer about one car on the shopper's behalf: availability, out-the-door price with fees, add-ons, history. Returns the exact message for the shopper to review. In this version the message is a preview and is not sent. Ask the shopper before calling this, and never invent their name or contact.

tools.name: find_evidence
tools.description: Answers "what does X do?" and "does X affect Y?" for a supplement, nutrient, drug, food compound or plant (for example "does magnesium help sleep?", "what is creatine shown to do?", "omega-3 and triglycerides"). Pass the substance as query and the effect or outcome asked about, if there is one, as about. When the person names two substances ("is creatine safe with caffeine"), pass one as query and the other as about, in one call; findings about the pair together come back under in_combination. It resolves the name to the node that has findings and returns up to limit findings (default 10), strongest evidence first, each with its evidence strength in words, the study design, the quote, the paper, a permalink and a citation to quote as it stands. total_findings counts every reported finding that matches; hypotheses counts the inferred rows listed beside them. The result is complete for the query: another wording of the same substance resolves to the same node, so do not call again to rephrase. Call again only to narrow (evidence_strength, about), to raise limit (at most 50), or to ask about something else. Without about, summary lists everything the node has findings about. If matched is null, or total_findings is 0, Catalyst has recorded no findings on it. That is a complete answer: say so, and do not answer from memory as though from Catalyst. Try search_nodes only when other_matches or summary shows a node the person plausibly meant. An evidence strength says how well the evidence supports a finding and is not a recommendation. For what a compound can become, use reach; for reference-database relations, use get_relations.

tools.name: search_nodes
tools.description: Looks up the node id for a compound, protein, organism or outcome by name or synonym (for example "CoQ10", "caffeine", "CYP1A2", "sleep"). Use it to get the id that get_findings, get_finding, get_relations, get_reactions and reach take; for a question about what a substance does, call find_evidence instead, which needs no id. Returns up to 10 hits, each with id, label, type and the number of findings; hits with findings come first, so the first hit with findings above 0 is usually the one to use. An enzyme or transporter has type protein. It says nothing about a node beyond its id and how many findings it has. If with_findings is 0 the graph holds no findings for the name; the hits may still be the right node for get_relations, get_reactions or reach.

tools.name: get_findings
tools.description: Lists the curated study findings for one node by id, from search_nodes: for a compound, organism or material, what it has been shown to affect; for an outcome, which compounds have been studied against it. Use it to browse a node by id. For a question in words, such as "does X help Y", find_evidence answers in one call and needs no id. summary has one row per thing the node has findings about, counted over all its findings and not only the rows returned. The default number of findings, strongest first, is enough to answer. There is no offset: to see a different slice, pass about (an id from summary, or words such as "sleep") or evidence_strength. Each finding carries its evidence strength, one of five named levels from strong to insufficient (strong, moderate, limited, very_limited, insufficient), the verbatim sentence it was drawn from, the paper, the population and dose, and a permalink. An evidence strength says how well the evidence supports the finding and is not a recommendation; give it with the claim, and link the permalink. An empty list means no findings are recorded for that node, a complete answer that does not show the compound does nothing; empty_means says why.

tools.name: get_finding
tools.description: Explains one finding by its finding id: the claim, its evidence strength and what that level means, the verbatim quote, the study design and the paper, and evidence_strength_reasons, each rule that set the level in order, and what the assessment does not weigh. The finding id is 26 characters, from the id field of a find_evidence or get_findings finding, or the last part of its permalink (/e/{id}). Use it to answer why the evidence behind a finding is as strong as it is, from evidence_strength_reasons and never by guessing. To find findings, use find_evidence or get_findings; this tool takes no name. A head-to-head comparison id returns a sentence naming the page that shows the comparison, not a finding.

tools.name: get_relations
tools.description: Lists what public reference databases (Reactome, UniProt, Rhea, ChEBI and others) record about one node by id, from search_nodes: transporters, enzymes, pathways, expression. Every row is assertion_class 'inferred': a hypothesis about how a compound could act, not a result anyone measured in people. Present these as possible mechanisms and never as effects. For effects, use find_evidence. For the reactions a compound or enzyme takes part in, use get_reactions; for what a compound can become, use reach. predicate limits the list to one relation type, named as in the predicate field of a row (for example transported_by for transporters, metabolized_by for enzymes). Returns total and up to limit rows (default 10); offset pages the rest, and the default is enough to answer. A page too large for one result is cut to fit, and truncated with next_offset says how to get the rest. An empty list with a predicate means the databases record no relation of that type for this node. That is a complete answer, so do not repeat the call with the same predicate. Leave predicate out once only when the person asked broadly and you need to see which types the node has.

tools.name: get_reactions
